[`actor_rig_actuation.gd`](../../godot/scripts/actor_rig_actuation.gd) owns the JSON-safe profile manifest and [`actor_rig_motor.gd`](../../godot/scripts/actor_rig_motor.gd) supplies `simulate_actuator_action(delta, channels, world)`. This path bypasses high-level rig behavior while retaining bounded sampled collision, rotation and motion caps. | Profile | Four channels, in order | Game mass / inertia | Authored actuator gains | |---|---|---|---| | `ripper-metal-v1` | Track drive −1–1; chassis torque −1–1; track brake 0–1; reserved 0 | 2 / 100÷3 | Drive 600; torque 800; traction depends on support and orientation | | `copter-metal-v1` | Collective 0–1; lateral cyclic −1–1; rotor torque −1–1; rotor brake 0–1 | 1 / 52÷3 | Collective 312; lateral 84; torque 416 | | `gemini-metal-v1` | Left thrust 0–1; right thrust 0–1; reserved 0; reserved 0 | 1 / 52÷3 | Each thruster 156, arm 4; unequal thrust creates torque | Forces are reported in world coordinates using game mass × cells/s²; torque uses game inertia × radians/s². The unconstrained increments are force/mass × step duration and torque/inertia × step duration, including passive forces separately. Gravity is 156 cells/s² in this lane. Braking is commanded dissipative drag, without a hidden target heading or target velocity. Powered demand is reduced proportionally when energy is insufficient; holding powered demand at zero energy does not recharge it. Neutral powered demand permits 0.30/s ground or 0.14/s air recharge. The profile owns remaining drag and energy coefficients. The additive session publication has `actuation_version: 1`, `actuation_stride: 32`, `actuation_states`, `actuation_profiles`, `actuation_capabilities` and `control_modes`. It preserves the existing wire observation/action versions. Each 32-value actuation row means: | Offsets | Values | |---|---| | 0–3 / 4–7 | Requested actuator channels after range handling / applied channels | | 8–10 / 11–13 | Requested world force x/y and torque / resource-and-contact-limited actuator force x/y and torque | | 14–16 | Passive force x/y and passive torque | | 17–19 | Actual post-collision delta velocity x/y and delta angular velocity | | 20–25 | Mass, inertia, resource scale, energy used, contact scale, consumed step duration | | 26–31 | Center displacement x/y, rotation displacement, flags, profile index, remaining energy | “Applied force” precedes collision and speed/rotation caps. Actual motion is reported separately and cannot be reconstructed from actuator force alone when the hull is constrained. Flags distinguish input clamping, resource/contact limits, motion/collision constraints, invalid input and unsupported profiles. Metal has no terrain-tool channel; arena virtual tags remain a separate request.

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > How should the control modes be classified?
Human fly-by-wire, a central oracle, an NCA and an emergent swarm describe different properties. Classify them on independent axes before comparing presets. | Axis | Meaning | Examples | |---|---|---| | Actuation lane | What commands reach the motor, with which assists and limits? | High-level wire intent; direct metal actuator channels | | Decision placement | Where are decisions made and which actors share a decision process? | Human pilot; one independent controller per actor; central team controller | | Perception privilege | What information may that decision process receive? | Own state; filtered nearby observations; camera image; full present-state oracle | | Coordination | What agent-to-agent or environment-mediated information changes decisions? | None; shared altered terrain; designed neighbor steering; bounded messages | | Controller family | What computes a decision from its permitted inputs? | Hand-authored reflex; search; recurrent neural policy; NCA-inspired graph; vision/language planner | | Training privilege | What information was used to produce the deployed controller? | No training; local rollouts; global critic; full-state teacher | A central process can aggregate only permitted local views and still lack oracle knowledge. Independent actor processes can each receive full state and therefore be privileged. Shared neural weights do not mean shared runtime memory. Human input can feed either actuation lane if that rig exposes the lane. The same local controller can be compared with and without communication while preserving its motor and sensory capabilities. Keep the actuation lane fixed for an actor's configured lifetime. Wire inputs request rig behavior: movement, aim, effort, trim, reel and the three action buttons. Metal inputs address the supported rig's direct actuators and bypass the high-level behavior dispatch. A force or torque expressed in game units is only meaningful with the published mass, inertia, channel map and integration law. It must not be described as a physical SI quantity or a Rapier force when the motor is an authored sampled approximation.

results.query: What distinguishes an all-knowing oracle from an independent lemming or locally coordinating actor swarm, and can neural controllers see hidden enemies?
facts: Control abstraction, decision placement, perception privilege, coordination and training privilege are separate design axes; v1 only implements its explicitly supported registry combinations.

Policies receive copied self/local/oracle views before any motor steps. Local views contain a bounded material stencil, nearby line-of-sight actors and permitted typed messages; global evaluator snapshots are separate.

Oracle receives full copied actor states/HP and coarse global terrain; local messaging is same-team radius/line-of-sight gated and delayed. Trusted in-process scripts are not a malicious-code sandbox; the full-view human scene is explicitly asymmetric.

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > How is oracle knowledge kept separate from local decisions?
The owner has authoritative state for collision, tags and validation; controllers receive their assigned views. Oracle privilege covers declared present state, not future outcomes or internal random-generator state. Filter observations before invoking policy code or helper functions. Choosing the nearest opponent from the full roster and passing that target to a “local” policy already leaks privileged information; filtering its output cannot undo it. A remembered track retains its original timestamp; invisible position or health must not keep updating. Future image adapters must apply the same privilege to camera centering, overlays and semantic labels. Image-only input cannot quietly include an exact hidden-state side channel. Review roster counts, persistent identifiers, kill notifications, rewards, debugging telemetry and shared recurrent buffers for undeclared information. Keep evaluator records separate. An action packet cannot upgrade its actor's configured perception privilege. The desktop demonstration explicitly displays the **full evaluator view**. Human examples therefore use `mechanics` or `asymmetric`, not a claim of equal visual privilege with local bots. The current oracle example centrally assigns targets using copied oracle actor states; it is a greedy reference, not an optimal planner or theoretical upper bound. This is a data contract for the supplied registered controllers, not a security sandbox for arbitrary in-process scripts. Isolating an untrusted controller would require a separate process or service boundary with the same observation rules. Centralized training is a distinct permission. For example, a global teacher can generate demonstrations or a critic can use additional state while the deployed actor remains local. The MADDPG paper explicitly separates privileged training information from the local actors used at execution. Record both privileges and evaluate the deployed controller through the actual local observation boundary. [Lowe et al. 2017](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2017/file/68a9750337a418a86fe06c1991a1d64c-Paper.pdf).

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > What does explicit nearby coordination require?
Separation, alignment, cohesion, target votes and teammate status vectors can all implement intentional coordination. “Decentralized” does not mean communication is absent. Current `local_swarm` and `nca` actors may send one typed four-float message per accepted command. Same-team recipients must still be alive, within 64 cells and in clear LOS. Delivery occurs on the next tick, with at most one newest message per sender and seven per receiver. Messages retain `sent_tick` and expire at the source command's observation-derived deadline; leaving the permitted neighborhood also removes them. `goal_hint` belongs to `local_swarm`, `latent_state` to `nca`; each example ignores the other kind. The local-swarm example combines explicit teammate spacing with a permitted target hint. Receiving a hint can guide travel but cannot authorize firing at an unseen enemy. It is intentional local coordination, including when no message is available and only the spacing rule affects movement. Read from a completed previous neighborhood snapshot and deliver new messages according to the declared schedule. In-place actor updates can otherwise let a message traverse an entire ordered list in one nominal local step. Likewise, several graph message-passing rounds enlarge effective information reach. Record the rounds and their latency instead of advertising only the one-hop radius. Tolstaya and colleagues demonstrate controllers that use local exchanges to obtain multi-hop information, including changing communication graphs; this is a relevant architecture reference, not a performance result for Thunderbowl. [Tolstaya et al. 2020](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v100/tolstaya20a.html). Packet loss, delayed updates, partitioned neighborhoods and inactive actors are useful planned ablations. They should alter only the declared communication mechanism. A globally computed replacement target would invalidate a claim that the local controller tolerated loss using local information alone.

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > What are the three different swarm experiments?
Individual intent, population effects and intentional use of peers are separate experimental variables. The baseline presets isolate their mechanisms. | Baseline | Individual decision rule | Coupling | What a result may establish | |---|---|---|---| | Independent selfish actors | Each actor pursues its own local task or tag opportunity | Ordinary shared terrain and arena rules; no designed collective objective or peer message | Performance of independent local decision makers | | Density or environment-mediated emergence | The same simple rule is repeated at different population densities | Shared terrain changes, constrained passages or another explicitly implemented common resource | Whether population and environmental changes produce useful aggregate behavior without peer coordination | | Explicit nearby coordination | An actor deliberately adjusts behavior using permitted nearby peers | Neighbor steering or a bounded communication protocol | Whether that particular information exchange improves a stated outcome | Reynolds's original flock model uses programmed local behaviors and local perception to produce collective motion. Vicsek's particle model explicitly aligns heading with nearby particles. Those are useful local-coordination comparators; their neighbor rules must not be hidden inside a baseline described as having no coordination. [Reynolds 1987](https://www.red3d.com/cwr/papers/1987/boids.html), [Vicsek et al. 1995](https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.75.1226). Clustering can arise from a different mechanism. Fily and Marchetti studied self-propelled repulsive disks without alignment and found density separation and clusters in that model. This supports distinguishing aggregation from alignment; it does not establish that CyberSand actors reproduce the same mechanism or gain a combat advantage from it. [Fily and Marchetti 2012](https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.108.235702). Thunderbowl's density example uses Diggers modifying shared destructible terrain. One actor may open a passage that another subsequently encounters through its own local terrain sensing. There is no message, neighbor alignment or assigned collective route. This is environment-mediated coupling. A resulting passage or cluster is not proof that the actors intended or learned cooperation. The sampled actor path does not provide actor-to-actor exclusion or contact. Increasing the number of overlapping actors therefore cannot demonstrate collision-driven crowd pressure. It may merely increase independent attempts or aggregate tag opportunities. Report the implemented coupling and compare against a terrain-edit-disabled control before attributing a benefit to emergence.

results.query: Does the Thunderbowl emergent swarm actually improve with density, and is the NCA example a trained terrain cellular automaton?
facts: Independent Diggers incidentally share edited native terrain without messages, neighbor steering or actor-to-actor contact. Density benefit is a testable hypothesis; more aggregate attempts or firepower alone do not establish emergence.
The provided 1/2/4/8 Digger presets are bounded pilot conditions. Compare normalized utility, fixed resources, terrain-coupling ablations, seeds and held-out layouts before efficacy claims.

The executable NCA-inspired example is a shared 12-to-8-to-4 residual neural update on the local actor communication graph, with four hidden channels and explicit untrained weights. Trained policies and a regular terrain-lattice NCA remain Planned.

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > Where could neural cellular automata fit?
Growing Neural Cellular Automata uses shared learned local updates and recurrent cell state on a grid. Its demonstrations concern pattern growth, persistence and regeneration. These results motivate a local recurrent design experiment; they do not show that an NCA is an effective actor pilot, battle policy or population controller. [Mordvintsev et al. 2020](https://distill.pub/2020/growing-ca/). The executable candidate and a future lattice experiment retain different names and contracts: | Form | State and neighborhood | Claim boundary | |---|---|---| | NCA-inspired actor graph | A small recurrent vector per actor; shared update using permitted neighboring actor state | A bounded graph-controller candidate; untrained weights provide no learned-control evidence | | Proposed terrain-lattice NCA | A separate coarse spatial lattice with recurrent channels and local cell updates | A training/interface proposal until its encoder, update, action readout and evaluation actually exist | Current [`nca.gd`](../../godot/examples/thunderbowl/nca.gd) uses a shared 12→8→4 residual MLP with four private recurrent values per actor. Inputs are own recurrent values, the mean of delivered `latent_state` messages, visible-enemy displacement, own horizontal velocity and energy. One update uses old delivered state; output is bounded to −1–1 and controls movement, effort and primary action. Episode or actor identity changes reset recurrence. The supplied weight artifact is explicitly `untrained`; loading `trained_external` metadata alone proves no training quality. For a proposed version-1 lattice experiment, start with an explicit spacing, 16 latent channels, a radius-one Moore neighborhood, one synchronous update round and a declared stochastic update probability. Freeze boundary handling, reset, sensor injection and local action readout before training. Keep the neural grid separate from authoritative material cells. A full-arena truth encoder creates a distributed sensor field with more coverage than an actor's local view and needs its own perception tag. Neither variant may hide global pooling, full-roster attention or in-place unbounded propagation behind a local label. Account for recurrent state, communication and update cost separately from the actor's collision queries. The existing world is not a differentiable training graph. Learning an update rule for this arena therefore needs an explicit route such as imitation, black-box policy optimization or a separately validated differentiable surrogate.

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > What comparisons would establish useful behavior?
Record a comparison manifest before interpreting a score. At minimum it should identify the source/runtime and rig capabilities, arena layout and material configuration, actor counts, actuation/assist lane, observation profile, decision and message schedules, controller/checkpoint, training privileges, seed policy, time limit and scoring rules. Distinguish these evaluation classes: | Evaluation tag | Intended interpretation | |---|---| | `matched` | Equal rig, lane and observation profile with scripted cadence; humans are rejected. Further resource/compute matching still needs an experiment manifest | | `asymmetric` | Declared information, actuation, population or compute differences | | `oracle_reference` | Declared oracle privilege; no optimal-play claim | | `mechanics` | Mechanism, capacity or timing demonstration; not a policy ranking | Use paired map/initial-state seeds, exchange sides or spawn locations, retain failed runs and report variation across episodes. A single arena win is an example, not a statistically supported policy ranking. A stronger aggregate force is not necessarily a more efficient actor policy. For density experiments report both actor count per free arena area and a stated body-footprint measure. More actors at fixed area also adds action opportunities, energy and tag capacity. Smaller areas at fixed count change travel distance and confinement. Preserve those distinctions when interpreting the result. Useful ablations include fixed-area count sweeps, fixed-count area sweeps, constant-density population/area scaling, terrain edits enabled versus disabled, independent random streams versus correlated inputs, and nearby coordination enabled versus disabled under a matched budget. Geometry and passability changes must be recorded; the ablation is not automatically a pure density intervention. Actor-contact-on/off trials remain unavailable until actor contact is implemented. Measure the outcome that matches the hypothesis: passage creation and traversal time for the Digger example, coverage and dispersion for exploration, or virtual tags and survival for battle. Also report per-actor and aggregate results, energy or actuator work, saturation, decision age and capacity/command refusals. Clustering, heading agreement and success are different measurements. Crowding may help, hinder or make no difference; no monotonic density benefit, trained-NCA advantage or advanced-model advantage is claimed without those experiments.

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > How should the control modes be classified?
Human fly-by-wire, a central oracle, an NCA and an emergent swarm describe different properties. Classify them on independent axes before comparing presets. | Axis | Meaning | Examples | |---|---|---| | Actuation lane | What commands reach the motor, with which assists and limits? | High-level wire intent; direct metal actuator channels | | Decision placement | Where are decisions made and which actors share a decision process? | Human pilot; one independent controller per actor; central team controller | | Perception privilege | What information may that decision process receive? | Own state; filtered nearby observations; camera image; full present-state oracle | | Coordination | What agent-to-agent or environment-mediated information changes decisions? | None; shared altered terrain; designed neighbor steering; bounded messages | | Controller family | What computes a decision from its permitted inputs? | Hand-authored reflex; search; recurrent neural policy; NCA-inspired graph; vision/language planner | | Training privilege | What information was used to produce the deployed controller? | No training; local rollouts; global critic; full-state teacher | A central process can aggregate only permitted local views and still lack oracle knowledge. Independent actor processes can each receive full state and therefore be privileged. Shared neural weights do not mean shared runtime memory. Human input can feed either actuation lane if that rig exposes the lane. The same local controller can be compared with and without communication while preserving its motor and sensory capabilities. Keep the actuation lane fixed for an actor's configured lifetime. Wire inputs request rig behavior: movement, aim, effort, trim, reel and the three action buttons. Metal inputs address the supported rig's direct actuators and bypass the high-level behavior dispatch. A force or torque expressed in game units is only meaningful with the published mass, inertia, channel map and integration law. It must not be described as a physical SI quantity or a Rapier force when the motor is an authored sampled approximation.

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > What is Thunderbowl for?
Thunderbowl (ACT-003, [issue #172](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/172)) compares the same actor rigs under different control laws, information access and group behavior. Controller sophistication, population size and privileged knowledge are separate advantages that each result must identify. The sampled v1 arena is a standalone native desktop scene with at most eight actors, separate from the ordinary F5 rig comparison and the registered scientific fixtures. Its battle model is an arena-owned virtual tag exercise with bounded aim, range, line of sight and cooldown. Virtual hit points and tag outcomes are gameplay bookkeeping. They do not establish native actor damage, actor-to-actor collision, rigid-body impacts or a general weapons simulation. The [actor-rig contract](actor-rigs.md) remains the authority for the underlying sampled locomotion and terrain tools. Current source defines the prototype below; the [validation ledger](../reference/validation-evidence.md) owns dated acceptance evidence, with source/runtime identities and preserved failures in the [ACT-003 audit](../audits/2026-10-18-act003-thunderbowl-control-lab.md). Trained policies, a terrain-lattice NCA and a live model service remain **Planned**. No controller-efficacy or target-machine performance claim follows from having executable examples.

results.query: How can a slow vision or decision model control Thunderbowl without stale replies taking over or blocking the physics loop?
facts: The smart-link adapter permits one outstanding observation-bound request, at most every 30 ticks; model plans expire within 120 ticks of the original observation. Forged identities, replayed/out-of-order and expired replies are rejected.
A fresh 10 Hz local reflex converts a still-valid intention to ordinary 12-tick input leases; zero drive demand, missing/expired plans or hold cancel armed actions and leave passive physics.

The optional capped file adapter operates between arena steps and never waits for model inference, but synchronous filesystem latency can delay the caller. The Python client is an offline mock; no live vision model, trained policy or hard real-time performance is claimed.

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > How should a smart model link run at several rates?
```mermaid flowchart TD owner["Arena owner"] --> view["Permitted observation"] view --> reflex["Fresh local reflex"] view --> slow["Slow decision adapter"] slow --> admission["Identity and age checks"] admission --> reflex reflex --> command["Wire command"] command --> owner owner --> judge["Separate evaluator record"] ``` A large decision or vision/language model can propose a goal while a smaller local controller handles fresh observations. The current driver samples humans at 60 Hz, runs scripted/local-reflex/NCA decisions at 10 Hz, and steps motors and materials at 60 Hz. No external service latency is assumed. Current [`smart_link.gd`](../../godot/examples/thunderbowl/smart_link.gd) permits one outstanding request, no more often than every 30 simulation ticks, expiring 120 ticks after its source observation. The request includes `request_id`, run/actor/epoch/observation identity, `observed_tick`, `expires_tick` and the copied permitted observation. A response echoes those identities and supplies `valid_for_ticks` in 1–120 and `intent: {"mode": "pursue_visible", "goal": [0, 0], "speed": 0.65, "engage": true}`. Modes are `hold`, `move_to` and `pursue_visible`; goal components are world-cell coordinates 0–1024. `speed` is normalized drive demand, not guaranteed velocity. Plan expiry stays anchored to the request observation; admitting a late reply does not renew it. A fresh local reflex converts an admitted goal into a new 12-tick motor command and only aims tags at currently visible enemies. Zero drive, `hold`, missing/expired plans or an absent pursuit target cancel armed actions and coast under passive physics. There is no implicit hover, brake or path solver. No owner waits for model inference or a reply. The sample adapter synchronously polls bounded files between arena ticks, so filesystem latency can still delay the next step; this is not asynchronous I/O or a hard real-time guarantee. Log the sensor sample tick, material/render sample age when images are involved, request time, response time, plan admission, local action production and actual command consumption. Measure service latency separately from simulated-time age. A model trained or tested with paused decision time belongs to a different evaluation class from a real-time pilot. The sample file adapter only exercises the decision contract; it does not establish a live LLM, vision encoder, reward trainer or neural service integration.

It may merely increase independent attempts or aggregate tag opportunities. Report the implemented coupling and compare against a terrain-edit-disabled control before attributing a benefit to emergence.

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > What does the arena publish and resolve?
[`CyberThunderbowlArena`](../../godot/scripts/thunderbowl_arena.gd) exposes `configure(config)`, `observation(actor_id)`, `snapshot()`, `step(commands)` and `close()`. A successful configuration installs an exclusive native world and actor session; a refused configuration preserves the existing instance. Each `step` advances one 1/60-second motor/material tick, with at most eight commands. An oversized batch is refused as a whole. Failed material ticks quarantine the owner and retain the last completed actor/reward publication. | Published view | Contents and permission | |---|---| | Every policy observation | Run/actor/epoch/tick/observation identity; assigned model, lane, team and view mode; own alive/HP/tag readiness; own 40-value rig state and 32-value actuation state/profile | | Own terrain stencil | 9×9 material samples spaced four cells, with explicit origin; this is a sampled 32-cell span, not every intervening cell | | `self` | Empty neighbor and message arrays | | `local` | Up to seven alive neighbors within 64 cells and clear terrain LOS; visible ID/team, relative center, velocity, body size and rotation; no neighbor HP, energy, actions or hidden state | | `oracle` addition | All actors' current 40-value states, HP and alive status, plus a 32×18 terrain grid sampled every eight cells; not every native cell or future state | | Evaluator `snapshot()` | Full copied actor/session state, HP, rewards, tags, bounded events, admission/work counters, layout and material hashes; never the ordinary local-policy input | Neighbor order is actor-ID order. LOS uses bounded supercover rays and treats any non-Empty material as blocking. At most 8,192 sensor and 10,752 tag cell reads are available per completed tick; exhaustion refuses visibility/hits. Optional full-arena presentation samples are separately bounded and excluded from those policy-sensing budgets. Virtual tags require a rising edge, nonzero aim, range ≤56 cells, aim dot product ≥0.94, clear LOS and a 30-tick cooldown. The nearest eligible opponent center is selected; a shot attempt consumes cooldown even on a miss. Each actor starts with three HP. Simultaneous hits resolve before eliminations: each hit gives +1/−1 reward, and an elimination's +2 bonus is shared among that tick's attackers; the victim loses two more. Ring-out costs two and eliminates the actor. Elimination cancels input and marks virtual status; it does not remove a native body or slot.

results.query: How do I spawn and run Thunderbowl battle tests, and are tags, eliminations and rewards real native weapon damage?
facts: A separate native owner and CLI/playable scene load version1 match JSON with1 to 8 current rigs. Fourteen presets cover wire/metal/oracle/lemming/emergent/local/NCA/smart-link experiments without replacing scientific fixtures.
Arena-only virtual tag combat uses 3 HP, 56-cell range, aiming/line-of-sight checks, rising shots and 30-tick cooldown, with simultaneous hits, explicit rewards and a 128-event history.

Elimination cancels input without physical corpse/removal or generic actor damage. Seeded setup and material hashes are scoped experimental identities, not complete replay; evaluation labels do not prove empirical fairness.

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > How is oracle knowledge kept separate from local decisions?
The owner has authoritative state for collision, tags and validation; controllers receive their assigned views. Oracle privilege covers declared present state, not future outcomes or internal random-generator state. Filter observations before invoking policy code or helper functions. Choosing the nearest opponent from the full roster and passing that target to a “local” policy already leaks privileged information; filtering its output cannot undo it. A remembered track retains its original timestamp; invisible position or health must not keep updating. Future image adapters must apply the same privilege to camera centering, overlays and semantic labels. Image-only input cannot quietly include an exact hidden-state side channel. Review roster counts, persistent identifiers, kill notifications, rewards, debugging telemetry and shared recurrent buffers for undeclared information. Keep evaluator records separate. An action packet cannot upgrade its actor's configured perception privilege. The desktop demonstration explicitly displays the **full evaluator view**. Human examples therefore use `mechanics` or `asymmetric`, not a claim of equal visual privilege with local bots. The current oracle example centrally assigns targets using copied oracle actor states; it is a greedy reference, not an optimal planner or theoretical upper bound. This is a data contract for the supplied registered controllers, not a security sandbox for arbitrary in-process scripts. Isolating an untrusted controller would require a separate process or service boundary with the same observation rules. Centralized training is a distinct permission. For example, a global teacher can generate demonstrations or a critic can use additional state while the deployed actor remains local. The MADDPG paper explicitly separates privileged training information from the local actors used at execution. Record both privileges and evaluate the deployed controller through the actual local observation boundary. [Lowe et al. 2017](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2017/file/68a9750337a418a86fe06c1991a1d64c-Paper.pdf).

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > What comparisons would establish useful behavior?
Record a comparison manifest before interpreting a score. At minimum it should identify the source/runtime and rig capabilities, arena layout and material configuration, actor counts, actuation/assist lane, observation profile, decision and message schedules, controller/checkpoint, training privileges, seed policy, time limit and scoring rules. Distinguish these evaluation classes: | Evaluation tag | Intended interpretation | |---|---| | `matched` | Equal rig, lane and observation profile with scripted cadence; humans are rejected. Further resource/compute matching still needs an experiment manifest | | `asymmetric` | Declared information, actuation, population or compute differences | | `oracle_reference` | Declared oracle privilege; no optimal-play claim | | `mechanics` | Mechanism, capacity or timing demonstration; not a policy ranking | Use paired map/initial-state seeds, exchange sides or spawn locations, retain failed runs and report variation across episodes. A single arena win is an example, not a statistically supported policy ranking. A stronger aggregate force is not necessarily a more efficient actor policy. For density experiments report both actor count per free arena area and a stated body-footprint measure. More actors at fixed area also adds action opportunities, energy and tag capacity. Smaller areas at fixed count change travel distance and confinement. Preserve those distinctions when interpreting the result. Useful ablations include fixed-area count sweeps, fixed-count area sweeps, constant-density population/area scaling, terrain edits enabled versus disabled, independent random streams versus correlated inputs, and nearby coordination enabled versus disabled under a matched budget. Geometry and passability changes must be recorded; the ablation is not automatically a pure density intervention. Actor-contact-on/off trials remain unavailable until actor contact is implemented. Measure the outcome that matches the hypothesis: passage creation and traversal time for the Digger example, coverage and dispersion for exploration, or virtual tags and survival for battle. Also report per-actor and aggregate results, energy or actuator work, saturation, decision age and capacity/command refusals. Clustering, heading agreement and success are different measurements. Crowding may help, hinder or make no difference; no monotonic density benefit, trained-NCA advantage or advanced-model advantage is claimed without those experiments.

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > What is Thunderbowl for?
Thunderbowl (ACT-003, [issue #172](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/172)) compares the same actor rigs under different control laws, information access and group behavior. Controller sophistication, population size and privileged knowledge are separate advantages that each result must identify. The sampled v1 arena is a standalone native desktop scene with at most eight actors, separate from the ordinary F5 rig comparison and the registered scientific fixtures. Its battle model is an arena-owned virtual tag exercise with bounded aim, range, line of sight and cooldown. Virtual hit points and tag outcomes are gameplay bookkeeping. They do not establish native actor damage, actor-to-actor collision, rigid-body impacts or a general weapons simulation. The [actor-rig contract](actor-rigs.md) remains the authority for the underlying sampled locomotion and terrain tools. Current source defines the prototype below; the [validation ledger](../reference/validation-evidence.md) owns dated acceptance evidence, with source/runtime identities and preserved failures in the [ACT-003 audit](../audits/2026-10-18-act003-thunderbowl-control-lab.md). Trained policies, a terrain-lattice NCA and a live model service remain **Planned**. No controller-efficacy or target-machine performance claim follows from having executable examples.

The [match presets](../../godot/examples/thunderbowl/matches) use the same [`driver`](../../godot/examples/thunderbowl/thunderbowl_driver.gd): | Preset filename stem | Demonstration | |---|---| | `human_wire`, `human_metal` | Human input through the selected lane | | `wire_duel`, `metal_lab` | Reactive intent pursuit; direct actuator pulses | | `oracle` | Central greedy assignment with privileged actor state | | `lemmings` | Independent, self-only turning and blind periodic tag attempts | | `emergent_1`, `_2`, `_4`, `_8` | Digger population examples without peer sensing/messages | | `local_swarm` | Nearby teammate spacing and typed target hints | | `nca` | Untrained recurrent actor-graph candidate | | `smart_link` | Local reflex plus optional external intention file | | `mixed` | Eight-actor asymmetric demonstration | From the repository root, replace `<godot>` with the pinned executable from the [build guide](../operations/local-build-and-validation.md): ```sh <godot> --headless --path godot --script res://examples/thunderbowl/run_thunderbowl.gd -- --match=res://examples/thunderbowl/matches/wire_duel.json --ticks=600 --output=/tmp/thunderbowl.json <godot> --path godot res://examples/thunderbowl/thunderbowl.tscn -- --match=res://examples/thunderbowl/matches/human_metal.json ``` The headless runner also accepts `--seed=INT`. Its JSON result contains final evaluator state, configuration, timing scope and adapter statistics; it is not a complete serialized replay. The output parent directory must exist. Keyboard input uses WASD, mouse aim/left-click tag, Space/Shift/C actions, Q/E trim and Z/X reel. The scene has a power slider and requires release/rearm after focus or device changes. Metal Ripper uses A/D drive and Q/E torque; Copter uses W collective, A/D cyclic and Q/E torque; Gemini uses Space/Shift for independent engines. Direct gamepad input supports independent analog Gemini triggers. Touch JSON demonstrates the normalized boundary; no touch UI or physical-device acceptance is implied. To exercise the **mock** smart-link client, start the arena with the following arguments, then run the Python client in a second terminal: ```sh mkdir -p /tmp/thunderbowl-link <godot> --headless --path godot --script res://examples/thunderbowl/run_thunderbowl.gd -- --match=res://examples/thunderbowl/matches/smart_link.json --smart-dir=/tmp/thunderbowl-link --realtime --output=/tmp/thunderbowl-smart.json ``` ```sh python3 tools/thunderbowl/mock_smart_link.py --request /tmp/thunderbowl-link/actor-0-request.json --response /tmp/thunderbowl-link/actor-0-response.json --watch --seconds 60 python3 tools/thunderbowl/validate_examples.py ``` The schema validator requires development-only `jsonschema`; the application does not. Fast headless stepping and `--realtime` wall-clock pacing are distinct experiment settings, especially for an external client.

The value boundary is [`CyberThunderbowlContract`](../../godot/scripts/thunderbowl_contract.gd). Its version-1 dictionaries require every named field and reject unknown fields, wrong types, nonfinite values and oversized files. File loading is capped at 65,536 bytes. Structural validation is followed by owner checks for the issued observation, run, actor, epoch, sequence, configured lane, liveness and expiry. The corresponding JSON Schemas live in [`examples/thunderbowl/schemas`](../../godot/examples/thunderbowl/schemas): `match`, `command`, `observation`, `input`, `actuator-input`, `smart-request`, `smart-decision` and `nca-weights`, each with the `.schema.json` suffix. | Object | Required fields and bounds | |---|---| | Arena configuration | `version: 1`, `seed` integer 0–2,147,483,647, `max_ticks` 1–36,000, `layout: "training_pit"`, `evaluation`, `actors` with 1–8 entries | | Actor definition | `model`, `control_mode`, `observation_mode`, `team` integer 0–7, `controller` | | Command envelope | `version`, `run_id`, `actor_id`, `epoch`, `sequence`, `observed_tick`, `observation_id`, `lease_ticks`, `kind`, `action`, `tag`, `message`, `message_type`, `cancel` | | Wire action | `movement[2]`, `aim[2]`, `effort`, `trim`, `reel`, `primary`, `secondary`, `auxiliary` | | Metal action | `actuators[4]`, `tag_aim[2]` | | Normalized input frame | Wire fields plus `version: 1`, `device`, `tag`, `deadman` | | Direct input frame | `version: 1`, `device`, `actuators[4]`, `aim[2]`, `tag`, `deadman` | `control_mode` is `wire` or `metal`; `observation_mode` is `self`, `local` or `oracle`. The prototype registry permits metal for `human_metal` and `metal_pulse`, using Ripper, Copter or Gemini. Other controller IDs use wire. Only `oracle` receives the oracle profile. `lemming` and `emergent` require `self`; `wire_seek`, `local_swarm`, `nca` and `smart_link` require `local`. `emergent` specifically uses Digger. These are the implemented preset combinations; the independent classification axes describe how future combinations should be specified without silently expanding this registry. Action vector components and trim/reel lie in −1–1, effort in 0–1; buttons are Booleans. The metal profile supplies narrower actuator ranges and requires every reserved channel to be zero. `tag` requests the arena's virtual tag independently of rig tool buttons. `message` is either empty or exactly four values in −1–1; `message_type` is respectively `none`, or `goal_hint`/`latent_state`. A cancel packet has zero/neutral action, no tag and an empty message; it also clears armed charge rather than turning release into an unintended launch. Commands identify an opaque `run_id` and a previously issued `observation_id` bound to the run, epoch, actor and tick. Actor IDs are 0–7; epochs start at one; sequence numbers are nonnegative bounded integers. Leases are 1–18 simulation ticks, anchored to the observation tick. `Contract.command(view, sequence, action, tag, message, cancel, message_type)` copies the issued identity and requests 12 ticks. Receiving a command is distinct from consuming it, and expiry does not grant an action a new observation timestamp. The example driver binds each ordinary controller result to the exact actor

Section: Depth layers and parallax prototypes > Four material planes
The prototype owns four separate CyberNativeCellWorld objects through CyberDepthLayerRuntime. Each world uses the existing native material IDs, rules and RG8 RenderBridge projection. Godot owns only authoring, presentation and explicit lab commands. | Plane | Strata default rate | Intended use | |---|---:|---| | play | 60 Hz | Active foreground/play material. | | scripted | 20 Hz | Rear set, destructible scenery and set-piece sequences that should not perturb foreground material. | | effects | 30 Hz | Rain, snow-like Dust, Steam fog, Spark energy and other environmental material effects. | | background | 0 Hz | Authored distant city. It is never ticked and its first copied RG8 publication is cached. | The rates are independent. Dynamic planes may be reduced or paused without changing the others. The background rejects non-zero rates. Deepworks selects 30/20/15/0 Hz for play/scripted/effects/background. Every Deepworks plane spans the full 1024 × 1024 authored map; the rear `scripted` world runs native reactions while the true `background` world remains frozen. Each plane has its own render canvas and a material surface covering the accepted authored ROI, defaulting to 640 × 360 in Strata Theatre. Frozen surfaces request a one-shot bake when a copied publication arrives or updates are paused, so pausing before the first draw still renders the admitted state. See [`CyberDepthLayerSurface.apply_packet()` and `set_render_enabled()`](../../godot/scripts/depth/depth_layer_surface.gd). The current host uses one native adapter owner and serializes calls into its four worlds. Production adoption should integrate the play plane with the existing asynchronous owner rather than introduce another mutable owner.

Reset increments a generation and retires queued commands from the previous theatre. The **Rear reactor sequence / E** applies three bounded breaches to the rear world, followed by a Spark burst in the effects world. The play world is not modified. This is authored event projection; native explosions/reactions are not automatically watched and forwarded between worlds. These routes and the E control belong to Strata Theatre. Section: Articulated Rapier actors and shared physical control > How do humans and external policies share authority?
[`CyberPhysicalActorSession`](../../godot/scripts/physical_actor_session.gd) owns the rigs and scripts on the main thread. Its version-2 `physical_wire_action` envelope binds each request to a run, actor, epoch, monotonic sequence and actually issued observation. Lease expiry is measured from that observation's simulation tick. Reusing a slot, resuming after a reset, or receiving a late response does not renew old authority. Human, demonstration and policy producers use the same normalized action and actuator path. The session validates producer ownership, numeric types, finiteness, known fields and source freshness. The API publishes copied parts, joints, capabilities, actuator response and lifecycle state. This is a distinct physical interface; the sampled v1/v2 rows and four-channel metal experiment are not silently reinterpreted as arbitrary articulated actions. Faulted rigs report suspension and refuse new commands explicitly. Cancellation clears stored launch intent, pending effects, ropes and temporary grips through the owner. It is not a deliberate charged release and does not erase physical velocity. Reset/close retires the bodies and joint graph. Long-latency decision models should issue tasks through fresh local feedback; ACT-004 provides a bounded action consumer, rather than an asynchronous model service. Exact envelope and step boundaries are linked from [interfaces](../reference/interfaces-and-message-contracts.md#physical-actor-control-and-effects).

Section: Articulated Rapier actors and shared physical control > What does plausible physical behaviour mean here?
The owner explicitly chose gameplay emulation: bounded assistance, approximate connections and controlled flex/play are legitimate mechanics. There is no requirement to track finite gyro momentum or represent a perfect mechanical joint. Rapier still resolves actual body motion and contacts. The [rig runtime](../../godot/scripts/physical_actor_rig.gd) provides: - Rotary pin joints with optional angle limits, bounded motor targets and continuous wheel rotation where declared. - Endstop-constrained pin-in-slot slides with compliant angular alignment; spring variants also use a damped spring. Their residual angular play is intentional, rather than a promise of exact prismatic kinematics. - Damped, bounded gyro assistance with a settled-angle band; command slewing avoids abrupt microcorrections without eliminating deliberate bursts. - Support-conditioned ground propulsion, reactive joint gait, aimed impulses, rotor or vector thrust, hover clearance, speed-dependent sail lift and recovery. - Bounded grip and one straight terrain rope; released bodies preserve motion. Ropes have no wrapping or general object-to-object rope simulation. Ripper is fast and low with slip and strong reversals. Scrabbler uses a three-foot rhythm and compliant knees. Pouncer deliberately holds a coil before releasing its leap and unfolds its actual fin joints. Vector and Pulse steer their actual pod gimbals through bounded joint targets. Digger aims bounded excavation through horizontal or vertical burrows. Copter retains recoverable instability. Lineshank and Rocketblade concentrate mass near the grip of a thin blade. Tandem, Tricopter, Tiltrotor and Heavylift vary lever arms, articulation and mass distribution; Heavylift carries a suspended payload. The resource reserve is authored gameplay state. Ordinary powered movement can replenish a reserve while bursts, gripping and tools consume it. This does not claim a calibrated energy model. Units, caps and publication capacity belong in the [configuration reference](../reference/configuration-reference.md#physical-actor-values).

Section: Articulated Rapier actors and shared physical control > How do the scripted examples behave?
Every physical entry has a deterministic local feedback producer in [`physical_actor_script.gd`](../../godot/scripts/physical_actor_script.gd). It consumes the same copied pose, velocity, contact, local-ray, resource and attachment observations available to a policy. It cannot read native World, teleport a body, replenish resources or bypass command admission. The scripts patrol relative to their starting location, reverse before a target becomes an asymptotic stopping point, and use actual contact and progress towards the route to decide when to vault or recover. Vertical bouncing against a wall and backward shoves do not disguise a stall; intended climbing, winching and drilling retain their relevant progress directions. A stalled actor gets a debounced escape attempt. Flyers use altitude, velocity, ceiling and attitude feedback; Duet pulse-width modulates its two buttons with collective off periods and an inverted-thrust cutoff. Heavylift reads its connected payload's pose and velocity, reduces acceleration while it swings, and applies a bounded correction beneath an outward-moving load. Rope pilots take up slack from a floor start, pump the observed swing and release during a useful ascent, while Winchbug favours hauling and damping. Charge actions have explicit hold/release phases. A resource hysteresis band suppresses expensive bursts while the reserve recovers. These are energetic demonstration controllers and useful baselines. They are not global route planners. A difficult enclosure can still defeat a local controller; reported obstruction and recovery state allow later policies to make a different decision. No neural training or live LLM inference is supplied by ACT-004.

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > How should a smart model link run at several rates?
```mermaid flowchart TD owner["Arena owner"] --> view["Permitted observation"] view --> reflex["Fresh local reflex"] view --> slow["Slow decision adapter"] slow --> admission["Identity and age checks"] admission --> reflex reflex --> command["Wire command"] command --> owner owner --> judge["Separate evaluator record"] ``` A large decision or vision/language model can propose a goal while a smaller local controller handles fresh observations. The current driver samples humans at 60 Hz, runs scripted/local-reflex/NCA decisions at 10 Hz, and steps motors and materials at 60 Hz. No external service latency is assumed. Current [`smart_link.gd`](../../godot/examples/thunderbowl/smart_link.gd) permits one outstanding request, no more often than every 30 simulation ticks, expiring 120 ticks after its source observation. The request includes `request_id`, run/actor/epoch/observation identity, `observed_tick`, `expires_tick` and the copied permitted observation. A response echoes those identities and supplies `valid_for_ticks` in 1–120 and `intent: {"mode": "pursue_visible", "goal": [0, 0], "speed": 0.65, "engage": true}`. Modes are `hold`, `move_to` and `pursue_visible`; goal components are world-cell coordinates 0–1024. `speed` is normalized drive demand, not guaranteed velocity. Plan expiry stays anchored to the request observation; admitting a late reply does not renew it. A fresh local reflex converts an admitted goal into a new 12-tick motor command and only aims tags at currently visible enemies. Zero drive, `hold`, missing/expired plans or an absent pursuit target cancel armed actions and coast under passive physics. There is no implicit hover, brake or path solver. No owner waits for model inference or a reply. The sample adapter synchronously polls bounded files between arena ticks, so filesystem latency can still delay the next step; this is not asynchronous I/O or a hard real-time guarantee. Log the sensor sample tick, material/render sample age when images are involved, request time, response time, plan admission, local action production and actual command consumption. Measure service latency separately from simulated-time age. A model trained or tested with paused decision time belongs to a different evaluation class from a real-time pilot. The sample file adapter only exercises the decision contract; it does not establish a live LLM, vision encoder, reward trainer or neural service integration.

Reset, suspension, cancellation and lease expiry revoke pending control. The session cancellation signal also retires worker effect generations, including requests already copied out of its queue but not yet admitted. For physical usables, the mutex serializes cancellation with material consumption, and extracted work remains in the admission capacity until resolved. Cancellation leaves already committed projectiles and deployed physical devices in the current world; reset/replacement retires that world-owned state. An old epoch cannot actuate new bodies. Desktop still has independently paced physical and cellular timelines, so this is not a claim of lockstep cells/body integration. **Current physical Thunderbowl v2:** [`CyberPhysicalActorArena.step`](../../godot/scripts/physical_actor_arena.gd) owns one native world and an isolated Rapier space synchronously at 60 Hz: 1. Prepare the occupancy mask from the current actual part poses. 2. Admit policy packets and advance the common actor session without integrating bodies yet; source/muzzle positions still correspond to that mask. 3. Consume bounded effects and physical usable requests against those copied poses, complete one native material tick and apply its cellular responses. 4. Synchronize hard terrain, step Rapier, and publish the next actor observation. Its schedule identifier is `synchronous-mask-actuation-effects-material-feedback-terrain-rapier/v1`. The ACT-005 usable course uses the same synchronous schedule and isolated owners. Its material targets and processor Feed/Jam/Clear actions are explicit bounded fixture authoring; they do not grant actor controllers an additional world-write path. The lab completes all pending bounded terrain chunks before its Rapier step; this makes no desktop frame-time claim. Local material patches disclose both their sample tick and preceding body-mask pose tick. Native failure stops the environment and publishes the failure disposition without another physics step. This separate manoeuvre/usable lab does not change sampled Thunderbowl v1's schedule, rewards or observation privileges, and does not migrate Web control.

The physical command envelope is version 2 with exactly these top-level fields: ```json { "version": 2, "kind": "physical_wire_action", "run_id": "issued-run-id", "actor_id": 0, "epoch": 1, "sequence": 1, "observed_tick": 0, "observation_id": "issued-observation-id", "lease_ticks": 12, "action": {"move": [1, 0], "aim": [1, -0.6], "effort": 0.8, "primary": false} } ``` The identity strings above are illustrative. `make_command(view, sequence, action, lease_ticks)` copies an actually issued `observation(actor_id)` view. `submit(command, producer)` requires matching run, actor, epoch and producer ownership, a strictly newer nonnegative sequence, and an observation still retained in the bounded issuance history. Integer identity fields accept only exact finite integers. Lease expiry is `observed_tick + lease_ticks`, never receipt time; future, invented, stale and misaddressed views are refused. A queued model response cannot extend its authority by arriving late. See the [configuration bounds](configuration-reference.md#physical-actor-values). Legacy physical profiles admit `move`, `aim`, `effort`, `trim`, `reel`, `primary`, `secondary`, `auxiliary`, `tool`, `release_usable`, `attach_usable` and the optional `equipment` dictionary described below. Unknown keys, wrong types and nonfinite values are refused. Vectors accept `Vector2` or two numeric array values and are length-clamped to one; effort is clamped to zero through one, trim/reel to minus one through one. Missing action fields receive neutral defaults; buttons must be Booleans. All producers reach the same normalized action and bounded physical actuator path. The additive [4LY velocity profile](#physical-free-flight-actions) retains this envelope and ownership fence but admits only its declared `move` field. Existing actor IDs and their action meanings are unchanged. `observation(actor_id)` returns copied identity, tick, selected profile, pose/velocity, contacts and local rays, resource/charge/cooldown, part and joint states, attachment/tool state and lease status. These dictionaries do not change the sampled actor state/observation strides. Physical actors currently expose the wire lane only; sampled v1 tag, message, metal and NCA contracts remain separate. Desktop exposes `physical_actor_observation(actor_id)` and `submit_physical_actor_command(command)` and `cancel_physical_actor_command(actor_id)` from `main.gd` for a policy-owned actor. No network transport or model service is supplied by those methods. Desktop command admission remains suspended until the selected native reset is acknowledged and that epoch's initial hard-terrain colliders are installed. A faulted rig reports `suspended=true` and `lease_remaining=0`; its session refuses new commands with `actor_fault` and does not issue new control authority. `cancel_input(actor_id, epoch, producer)` clears the command and calls runtime cancellation; pause and close also revoke pending authority. Cancellation clears charged launch

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > How should the control modes be classified?
Human fly-by-wire, a central oracle, an NCA and an emergent swarm describe different properties. Classify them on independent axes before comparing presets. | Axis | Meaning | Examples | |---|---|---| | Actuation lane | What commands reach the motor, with which assists and limits? | High-level wire intent; direct metal actuator channels | | Decision placement | Where are decisions made and which actors share a decision process? | Human pilot; one independent controller per actor; central team controller | | Perception privilege | What information may that decision process receive? | Own state; filtered nearby observations; camera image; full present-state oracle | | Coordination | What agent-to-agent or environment-mediated information changes decisions? | None; shared altered terrain; designed neighbor steering; bounded messages | | Controller family | What computes a decision from its permitted inputs? | Hand-authored reflex; search; recurrent neural policy; NCA-inspired graph; vision/language planner | | Training privilege | What information was used to produce the deployed controller? | No training; local rollouts; global critic; full-state teacher | A central process can aggregate only permitted local views and still lack oracle knowledge. Independent actor processes can each receive full state and therefore be privileged. Shared neural weights do not mean shared runtime memory. Human input can feed either actuation lane if that rig exposes the lane. The same local controller can be compared with and without communication while preserving its motor and sensory capabilities. Keep the actuation lane fixed for an actor's configured lifetime. Wire inputs request rig behavior: movement, aim, effort, trim, reel and the three action buttons. Metal inputs address the supported rig's direct actuators and bypass the high-level behavior dispatch. A force or torque expressed in game units is only meaningful with the published mass, inertia, channel map and integration law. It must not be described as a physical SI quantity or a Rapier force when the motor is an authored sampled approximation.

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > How is oracle knowledge kept separate from local decisions?
The owner has authoritative state for collision, tags and validation; controllers receive their assigned views. Oracle privilege covers declared present state, not future outcomes or internal random-generator state. Filter observations before invoking policy code or helper functions. Choosing the nearest opponent from the full roster and passing that target to a “local” policy already leaks privileged information; filtering its output cannot undo it. A remembered track retains its original timestamp; invisible position or health must not keep updating. Future image adapters must apply the same privilege to camera centering, overlays and semantic labels. Image-only input cannot quietly include an exact hidden-state side channel. Review roster counts, persistent identifiers, kill notifications, rewards, debugging telemetry and shared recurrent buffers for undeclared information. Keep evaluator records separate. An action packet cannot upgrade its actor's configured perception privilege. The desktop demonstration explicitly displays the **full evaluator view**. Human examples therefore use `mechanics` or `asymmetric`, not a claim of equal visual privilege with local bots. The current oracle example centrally assigns targets using copied oracle actor states; it is a greedy reference, not an optimal planner or theoretical upper bound. This is a data contract for the supplied registered controllers, not a security sandbox for arbitrary in-process scripts. Isolating an untrusted controller would require a separate process or service boundary with the same observation rules. Centralized training is a distinct permission. For example, a global teacher can generate demonstrations or a critic can use additional state while the deployed actor remains local. The MADDPG paper explicitly separates privileged training information from the local actors used at execution. Record both privileges and evaluate the deployed controller through the actual local observation boundary. [Lowe et al. 2017](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2017/file/68a9750337a418a86fe06c1991a1d64c-Paper.pdf).

Local rebuilt artifacts are measured inputs, not automatically updated published LFS runtime manifests; the current release gate remains separate from M11 integrity. The shared threaded probe must yield before replacing a newly constructed default world, after replacement and after teardown so browser pthread startup/recycling can finish before synchronous native joins. This fixture lifecycle requirement does not change production native ownership or introduce asynchronous Web simulation.

results.query: Does a passing headless run prove material pixels were rendered, and how does CI detect skipped graphical tests?
facts: The runner automatically gives test_*_render.gd an actual display and compatibility renderer; Linux CI provides Xvfb and Mesa software rendering.
Explicit skips, timeout, missing executables, nonzero exits and engine/script errors fail required cases, including errors with exit code zero.
Keep-going retains later test outcomes after ordinary case failure, while failed import stops immediately; final timing reports record completion and status.
Linux software framebuffer checks do not establish target-GPU performance or fresh WebAssembly browser execution.

GEN-005 adds [`test_generation_planes.cpp`](../../native/tests/test_generation_planes.cpp) to both existing generation targets. Its oracle compares all four material arrays and canonical registration unions across reversed negative-coordinate tiles, worker counts and bounded slices, including shared typed masks and actor proposals. Run it with the ordinary generation suite: ```sh make worldgen-test ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:strict_string_checks=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=1 make worldgen-sanitize godot --headless --path godot --script res://tests/test_worldgen_planes.gd godot --headless --path godot --script res://tests/test_semantic_planes_runtime.gd godot --headless --path godot --script res://tests/test_semantic_planes_examples.gd ``` The runtime test requires every transaction, lifecycle, event, native reaction, cleanup and actor section to complete. The actual-example runner loads both checked-in recipes, requires all 40 fixture IDs and verifies every scheduled application/cleanup. Rear-only ticks must produce native Brine and transport while play/effects/background bytes stay unchanged. Separate play/effects ticks verify Water transport and complete the finite programmes. Inactive and missing-partner controls must fail the positive product/transport predicates. Any script error or required skip fails even if the process exits zero. The graphical oracle requires a real rendering backend: ```sh xvfb-run -a godot --path godot --rendering-method gl_compatibility --display-driver x11 --audio-driver Dummy --script res://tests/test_semantic_depth_render.gd ``` It compares rendered pixels while camera pan/zoom/parallax leave generation, semantic records and live ownership unchanged. The [authoring guide](semantic-depth-authoring.md) documents reproducible composites, isolated planes, region details and capture manifests. The new scene uses the current materialized native runtime without changing its ABI or dependency pins. Open it with `godot --path godot -- --deepworks` or `godot --path godot res://deepworks.tscn`. Run focused headless checks with the pinned engine, for example: ```sh godot --headless --audio-driver Dummy --path godot --script res://tests/test_deepworks.gd godot --headless --audio-driver Dummy --path godot --script res://tests/test_deepworks_controller.gd godot --headless --audio-driver Dummy --path godot --script res://tests/test_deepworks_reactions.gd godot --headless --audio-driver Dummy --path godot --script res://tests/test_depth_dimensions.gd godot --headless --audio-driver Dummy --path godot --script res://tests/test_depth_compositor.gd ``` | Case | Meaningful scope | |---|---| | `test_deepworks.gd` | Full recipe, all districts/planes, passage openings, catalogue coverage, bounded programme and rejected-install atomicity. | | `test_deepworks_controller.gd` | Production host controls, view changes, input transforms, pause/reset/tour and foreground/rear painting. | | `test_deepworks_reactions.gd` | Actual full-map native simulation through the production source scheduler, copied material observations, reaction products and transport away from feeds. | | `test_depth_dimensions.gd` | Default, non-square, minimum and 1024 × 1024 worlds; failed reset preserves prior state; guards, weather, far-edge camera and input. | | `test_depth_compositor.gd` | Packet admission and surfaces, including an older generation with a higher serial leaving pixels and identity untouched. | | `test_depth_dimensions_render.gd` | Actual far-edge pixels across all four planes, full-size composition, pointer mapping and MAT-002 relief bands. | | `test_deepworks_render.gd` | Actual production scene pixels, usable HUD area, per-district rear/distant contribution and atmospheric visibility. | The two new `*_render.gd` cases require a graphical compatibility renderer: ```sh godot --audio-driver Dummy --rendering-method gl_compatibility --path godot \ --script res://tests/test_depth_dimensions_render.gd godot --audio-driver Dummy --rendering-method gl_compatibility --path godot \ --script res://tests/test_deepworks_render.gd ``` Use a 180-second per-test deadline, as in the shared regression runner. The retained depth runtime, default lab and material-surface regressions remain applicable. Linux suite discovery includes every new `test_*.gd`; rendered suffixes require a display and cannot pass by skipping headless pixels. The Windows lane separately discovers the applicable headless cases. Discovery does not establish that either platform executed this source successfully. Reaction acceptance additionally requires all 32 expected district/plane identities to complete and pass their mechanism checks. Check both the process exit status and the complete log for `SCRIPT ERROR:` / `ERROR:`. Section: Local build and validation > Procedural generation candidates and workbench
GEN-001/GEN-002 provide native-only comparison, field/modifier regressions and focused fresh-chunk admission checks. GEN-003 adds independent typed analytical, multiresolution/cache/worker, bounded seed/mapping and finite solver regressions to the same native targets: ```sh make worldgen-test ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:strict_string_checks=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=1 make worldgen-sanitize make worldgen-demo ./build/worldgen_demo --output build/worldgen-plain.ppm --seed 314159 --plain ``` The explicit sanitizer command disables leak detection for environments where LeakSanitizer cannot inspect processes under ptrace. Without that override the sanitizer runtime enables it; use `detect_leaks=1` in a supported execution environment. The [GEN-001](../audits/2026-10-18-gen001-procedural-generation.md) and [GEN-002](../audits/2026-10-18-gen002-fields-and-aggregates.md) evidence distinguish actual LeakSanitizer infrastructure failures from passing ASan/UBSan results. The PPM contains actual generated material pixels from Strata, Flow Network and District Grammar; its printed local elapsed time is not a performance gate. With a source-matched extension, launch the separate authoring scene or its regression script using the pinned Godot executable: ```sh godot --path godot res://worldgen_workbench.tscn godot --headless --path godot --script res://tests/test_worldgen_workbench.gd godot --headless --path godot --script res://tests/test_worldgen_fields.gd godot --headless --path godot --script res://tests/test_worldgen_typed.gd ``` The generation workbench is separate from the ordinary sandbox and its optional [actor prototypes](../systems/actor-control-prototypes.md). It previews bounded native chunk generation, with theme/parameter strokes, guide paths, hard rectangles, module instances, fields/sidechains, context masks, aggregate materials and complete JSON profiles, without ticking the simulation. The [field/modifier contract](../systems/procedural-generation-fields-and-modifiers.md) owns the extended controls and diagnostic channel meaning. Load the examples under `examples/worldgen/`; use the [generation contract](../systems/procedural-world-generation.md) for exact ranges, module registration, receipt ownership and the separate fresh-chunk installer. Native generator/binding changes require rebuilt runtimes before these Godot commands establish source-matched evidence. Merely importing an old extension does not register `CyberWorldGenerator`. The [typed contract](../systems/procedural-typed-spatial-fields.md) and [operator inventory](../reference/procedural-spatial-operators.md) own GEN-003 numerical/type guarantees. The Workbench's Typed spatial graphs page selects five executable schema-2 profiles: `typed-industrial-structure.json`, `typed-vector-utilities.json`, `typed-categorical-districts.json`, `typed-reusable-decay.json` and `typed-multiscale-seeds.json`. They exercise transforms, vector guidance, exact districts, nested parameterized authoring and world-aligned coarse sampling. Typed Godot validation checks configuration roundtrips, typed diagnostics, malformed/refused inputs and Workbench integration; native analytical tests remain the numeric oracle. New native tests do not replace source-matched Linux/Windows runtime publication and ready-PR gates. To reproduce the five GEN-003 material/typed-diagnostic pairs, use the typed renderer with an absolute script path from the repository root: ```sh GENERATION_ROOT="$PWD" godot --headless --path "$GENERATION_ROOT/godot" --script "$GENERATION_ROOT/tools/render_worldgen_typed.gd" -- --output "$GENERATION_ROOT/build/worldgen-typed" ``` It samples a 256×192-cell region at `[-128,0]` from each checked-in profile and writes ten PNGs plus `render-manifest.json`. The manifest records the actual platform/Godot version, runtime and source SHA-256 values, recipe SHA-256, accepted graph fingerprint, typed diagnostic metadata and per-chunk material and receipt hashes. Colour mapping is the Workbench's presentation mapping; the native diagnostic payload retains signed numbers, vector components and exact categorical identity.

results.query: Which actor tools, projectile payloads and functional processors exist, and who owns their material edits, triggers and bounded work?
facts: The catalogue contains 12 material tools, 10 swept ballistic payloads and 10 fixed processors/responders with stable U01-U32 identities. ACT-005 binds the complete catalogue to physical equipment while retaining the sampled USABLE-001 route.

Physical equipment actions use the shared physical issued-observation envelope with explicit equipment identity, independent aim and power. The retained sampled session has its own actor epoch/sequence/lease stream. Only the serialized cellular owner performs material queries and writes.

Committed projectiles/devices survive input release, freeze on pause and clear with their World/reset lifetime. Real processors drop, settle and fix before worker admission; complete batch preflight and blocked outputs prevent partial consumption.

Recipe accounting measures authored cell slots, not exact Water mass, heat, momentum or chemistry conservation. All 41 physical rigs have explicit default loadout policies; general inventory/economy, health/damage and complete physical replay remain outside this increment.

The eight sections expose different interactions: | Section | Observable interaction | |---|---| | Bore / Cut | Editable packed-earth seams for advancing excavation rigs | | Sort / Drain | Powder, glass and liquid targets for selective material work | | Penetrate | Separate editable leaves for swept projectile penetration | | Ricochet | Protected hard faces for damped bounce and physical firing recoil | | Stage / Burst | Flight space for fuse, airburst and staged ignition behavior | | Drop / Deposit | Receiving bins for downward payloads and native deposits | | Release / Grip | Same-body release, retained momentum and nearby physical reattachment | | Place / Jam | A service pad for dropping, settling, fixing and operating processors | For a deployed processor belonging to the selected follow actor, **Feed**, **Jam** and **Clear output** perform explicit bounded fixture edits at the current physical ports. Feed uses that device's real material recipe; Jam/Clear expose the existing rule that blocked outputs prevent input consumption. Section: Actor usables — 32-item catalogue and physical equipment > U13–U22: ballistic payloads
Projectiles are sparse bounded records with swept cell-space contact, gravity, lifetime and explicit state transitions. They are separate from the native pixel-material `Rocket`. | Ref / ID | Usable | Activation | |---|---|---| | U13 `impact_slug` | Impact Slug | First editable contact chips a small footprint. | | U14 `borer_round` | Borer Round | Up to three editable penetrations, losing speed after each. | | U15 `ricochet_pellet` | Ricochet Pellet | Up to two damped terrain bounces. | | U16 `sticky_delay_charge` | Sticky Delay Charge | First contact sticks; 0.55 s simulation-time fuse excavates locally. Right click activates the oldest eligible owned charge early. | | U17 `timer_airburst` | Timer Airburst | 0.45 s flight fuse splits into five bounded child chip shots. Right click bursts the oldest live owned canister early. | | U18 `water_capsule` | Water Capsule | Contact releases Water into nearby available cells. | | U19 `oil_igniter` | Oil Igniter | Contact deposits Oil; 0.35 s later it attempts one Fire pulse. Right click activates the oldest primed owned payload early. | | U20 `seed_pod` | Seed Pod | Contact disperses Seed locally. | | U21 `cement_blob` | Cement Blob | Heavy short-range Cement payload. | | U22 `water_contact_charge` | Water Contact Charge | Contact arms the carrier; nearby Water or Brine triggers one Fire pulse. | A swept non-owner actor contact publishes a bounded hit receipt containing tick, owner, target, projectile and usable identity. Physical hits also identify the target body part. Accepted physical use applies bounded recoil through the main-thread equipment owner. The catalogue does **not** add health, damage numbers or a general damage/impact impulse system. Fuse time is simulation time and still advances if the movement read budget is exhausted; position remains at the last verified point. Collision sweep examines the valid in-bounds segment before discarding an out-of-world endpoint. Early activation of an eligible committed U16/U17/U19 payload is independent of new-launch charge, cooldown, power and muzzle clearance. It still requires the current held equipment identity and an active command lease, and adds no launch recoil. A zero-power primary use is refused; processor placement rejects it before releasing the physical chassis.

results.query: Can a delayed physical equipment request or receipt fire a replaced, dropped or cancelled tool, and how is the worker queue bounded?
facts: Physical actions share issued-observation identity and additionally carry usable_index, instance_id and equipment_epoch; copied requests and receipts are scoped to run, actor, generation, equipment/body identity and request ID.
Worker admission is atomic for at most eight requests globally and one pending request per actor, counting extracted in-flight work. Explicit refusals do not replace already admitted queued work.

Cancellation is serialized with material consumption; old generations, expired leases, reset epochs and duplicate receipts cannot apply a new transaction or repeat recoil. Already committed projectiles and devices remain until their normal or World lifetime ends.

Open **F5**, select the actor rig as usual, then choose equipment. **Equip only** changes the current human actor through its admitted equipment action. A physical item can be changed only while its chassis is held; a dropped or deployed object must be recovered first. The same chassis and existing shared equipment charge remain in use when its selected usable changes. - pointer position supplies equipment aim; - left mouse is primary activation; - right mouse is a tool precision pulse or supported early payload activation; - **N** drops the physical held item and **U** requests nearby pickup; processor primary starts physical placement, while sampled processors retain right-click logical retrieval; - equipment power is independent from movement effort; - tools repeat while held; projectiles and deployments consume a press edge; - choosing **None** returns the pointer to painting only after the owner publishes the unequipped selection and all pointer buttons have been released. While equipment is selected, ordinary world painting is suppressed. Focus loss, blocking UI, pause, reset or stale input cancels held equipment input. Already launched projectiles and deployed devices are owner state, not held input: they continue after release/cancellation, freeze while simulation is paused and clear on a fresh actor/World reset. Cancelled physical input retires pending requests and late receipts without teleporting a released body or erasing actor momentum. Changing equipment while a trigger is held requires release before rearming.
