Section: Simulation tick and threading > Physical actor scheduling
**Current ACT-004/ACT-005 desktop:** live bodies, joints and [`CyberPhysicalActorSession`](../../godot/scripts/physical_actor_session.gd) stay on the main thread. The owner installs a complete physical assembly with a new epoch for the selected reset. The sandbox can create it while reset is pending; scenario installation waits for acknowledgement. Before its first step, the host requires the matching reset acknowledgement and actor epoch, the current hard-terrain revision and an empty collider-installation queue. An early Play request cannot release this initial terrain fence. Subsequent terrain changes keep the desktop's existing bounded asynchronous installation. The worker binds retained geometry to its physical epoch, refreshes full/reset publications and invalidates the cache when replacing a scenario. Equal revision numbers in different worlds do not authorize reuse of the previous geometry. The physics callback admits permitted input, applies matching cellular feedback, advances bounded actor actuation, manually steps Rapier, reads the resulting parts and publishes their copied states with drained usable requests. Equipment poses, muzzle directions, generations and body states enter the worker together through `set_physical_usable_state`; the worker never obtains a Rapier object. Demo decisions run every six physical ticks from copied actor views collected before any demo output is submitted. The internal [4LY flight profile](../systems/physical-free-flight.md) reuses this main-thread owner and requires a 1/60-second actuation step. Its pure controller produces bounded force/torque from own velocity/attitude before the shared Rapier step. The rig owns a constant-force/torque channel for that one integration; `Session.complete_step` calls `Rig.complete_step` to clear the channel after Rapier advances. Cancellation clears unconsumed force immediately. Copied post-step motion and completed-step history remain distinct from a prepared actuator request/receipt. A session containing 4LY binds preparation/completion to the bridge's actual manual-step counter: duplicate preparation or no-step completion is refused, and unexpected physical steps produce a sticky session fault requiring replacement. Cancellation after physics preserves the original completed receipt even if producer ownership changes before accounting. The initial 4LY demo emits neutral conformance requests at the existing six-tick decision cadence. Invalid cadence, cancellation or expiry removes actuation authority, rather than clamping a different step into the flight contract. No new cellular worker, body solver or independent world clock is introduced. The desktop worker prepares the native body mask before consuming copied usable effects under exclusive cellular ownership. ACT-005 validates the captured physical source against the current equipment identity, lease and native body mask, charges source/part-mask queries against the usable work budget, and applies tools, projectile sweeps or fixed processor work before the material tick. It then advances materials when unpaused and publishes usable readback, request receipts and body responses with the actor epoch. Matching accepted, consumed

The normalized `action.equipment` dictionary has these fields: | Field | Meaning and validation | |---|---| | `usable_index` | Required exact integer -1 through 31; -1 selects None | | `instance_id` | Required nonempty String from the observed physical equipment | | `equipment_epoch` | Required current positive exact integer; selection and lifecycle transitions advance it | | `aim` | Optional finite Vector2/two-number array, length-limited to one; zero falls back to the enclosing locomotion aim | | `power` | Optional finite number, clamped to 0–1; defaults to 1 | | `trigger`, `alternate`, `drop`, `attach` | Optional Booleans, default false; transitions share bounded physical button-edge admission | Unknown fields and wrong types are refused. `make_command` can fill the three identity fields from its copied observation and maps local `tool`, `release_usable` and `attach_usable` requests to this dictionary. Raw policy packets cannot activate those legacy buttons without equipment identity. Selecting another usable requires the existing chassis to be held; it does not replace a released body. Holding a trigger during selection requires a neutral release before a new activation. The session owns one [`CyberPhysicalUsableEquipment`](../../godot/scripts/physical_usable_equipment.gd) per actor. It publishes copied `equipment` observations and prepares `equipment_frame()` plus `drain_equipment_requests()` for the cellular owner. The worker seam is: ```gdscript set_physical_usable_state( frame: Dictionary, requests: Array = [], states: PackedFloat32Array = PackedFloat32Array() ) -> Dictionary ``` A version-1 frame binds `run_id`, actor `epoch`, physical `tick`, suspension, actor rows and deployed-device rows. Actor rows contain control `generation`, `equipment_epoch`, `instance_id`, selected usable, stable equipment `body_id`, state, pose, extents, muzzle/direction, owning-part origin, lease deadline and copied individual part records. Device rows retain the physical instance/body and current fixed pose. Body-state values can be published at the same mutex boundary, preserving their relationship with the source/muzzle frame. No node, RID, live World or controller object crosses that boundary. Each ordinary version-1 request has `version`, `run_id`, `epoch`, `actor_id`, `generation`, `equipment_epoch`, `instance_id`, `usable_index`, `body_id`, `sequence`, `request_id`, `operation` and `power`. An entire incoming batch is admitted or refused, within eight requests and one in-flight request per actor. Refusal leaves other pending requests intact. Copied admission fields include status (`no_requests`, `queued`, `refused`), reason, requested/queued/refused counts, capacity and pending count. `CyberSimulationSnapshot.physical_usables` returns copied actor charge/cooldown, projectiles, physical processors, effects, hit records, work counters, admission and at most one retained result per actor. results.query: Does picking up a real deployed processor refill its stock, and how do rotated ports, settling and output jams affect material consumption?
facts: A processor is the same coupled body across held, released, fixed, deployed and nearby pickup states. It must remain supported within bounded linear/angular speed for eight consecutive ticks before fixing; distant or obstructed pickup is refused.
Worker admission checks the fixed physical source and four distinct exterior ports rotated from the actual body pose. It preflights every input/output cell; a blocked output consumes no inputs.

Bounded per-actor/per-processor history retains stock, age, cycles and cooldown across pickup, redeployment and selection. Same/older equipment epochs and exhausted deployment are refused; exhausted physical objects remain observable and inert until their physical owner retires them.

Every rig has a defined default loadout in [`physical_usable_loadouts.gd`](../../godot/scripts/physical_usable_loadouts.gd). Each loadout names its usable, power, strategy and purpose; no physical actor is left with an unspecified equipment policy. SetP explicitly starts with an empty mount and human movement strategy; F5 can still select ordinary equipment. Mount definitions bind a specific host/held part, grip, joint, aiming limits and clearance. The equipment owner aims the actual configured joint when it supports aiming. The shot direction comes from the current held body's pose; a limited joint cannot acquire an unlimited virtual muzzle. The suspended payload, hammer and blade preserve their authored mechanical roles. A selection change retools the existing held chassis without allocating another body. Release clears the held connection and retains the same object, pose, velocity and body ID. A short collision grace ages with physical time even after input cancellation. Pickup checks the owning grip's proximity and terrain clearance; it does not teleport the object or reset its velocity. An already held, remote, occluded or ambiguously owned item is refused. A released chassis must return before it can select another usable. Processors are deployed by dropping that real body, waiting for supported settling, and fixing it at its current pose. A worker receipt admits processing; blocked output leaves recipe inputs and stock unchanged. The body and its rotated intake/output ports remain visible while it works, jams or exhausts. The launcher entry **Physical usable course — 32 tools, payloads and processors** opens the same physical scene in its **Usable course** mode. The scene's **Manoeuvre / Usable course** selector resets the environment into the selected authored layout. All 46 rigs retain their catalogue loadout and the same human/demo/policy admission path; the course does not provide a separate actor controller with direct material access. ```text godot --headless --path godot --script res://examples/thunderbowl/run_physical_thunderbowl.gd -- --course=usables-v1 --rig=digger --actors=8 --ticks=600 --seed=0 --output=physical-usable-result.json ``` [`CyberPhysicalUsableCourse`](../../godot/scripts/physical_usable_course.gd) defines bounded native material fixtures and a varied default roster. The eight sections expose different interactions: | Section | Observable interaction | |---|---| | Bore / Cut | Editable packed-earth seams for advancing excavation rigs | | Sort / Drain | Powder, glass and liquid targets for selective material work | | Penetrate | Separate editable leaves for swept projectile penetration | | Ricochet | Protected hard faces for damped bounce and physical firing recoil | | Stage / Burst | Flight space for fuse, airburst and staged ignition behavior | | Drop / Deposit | Receiving bins for downward payloads and native deposits | | Release / Grip | Same-body release, retained momentum and nearby physical reattachment | | Place / Jam | A service pad for dropping, settling, fixing and operating processors | For a deployed processor belonging to the selected follow actor, **Feed**, **Jam** and **Clear output** perform explicit bounded fixture edits at the current physical ports. Feed uses that device's real material recipe; Jam/Clear expose the existing rule that blocked outputs prevent input consumption. These are visible authoring controls, separate from the actor's copied local observation and equipment actions. They do not imply autonomous material creation or a general inventory economy. Course configuration adds `"course": "usables-v1"` to the physical version-2 environment schema. Equipment observations, requests, receipts and native processor state follow the [physical equipment interface](../reference/interfaces-and-message-contracts.md#physical-equipment-actions-and-results). Body pose, joint aim, charged resources and native changes remain separate observable facts; the course has no virtual combat score or automatic assertion that every scripted actor completed every section. Acceptance is recorded in the [ACT-005 audit](../audits/2026-10-19-act005-physical-usables.md), with [focused validation commands](../operations/local-build-and-validation.md#physical-usable-validation).

results.query: Does current CI actually execute the retained Windows DLL, and how does it reject stale native source or incomplete headless coverage?
facts: The GitHub-hosted Windows execution job is separate from Windows cross-build inspection and runs the retained DLL after exact checkout, committed LFS, provenance and complete current native source/header input-set checks.

The helper verifies pinned official Godot 4.7 and Rapier, imports the project and dynamically executes every applicable headless case exactly once with the shared runner timeouts and strict diagnostic/skip rejection.

All dynamically discovered rendered cases are explicitly outside the Windows lane and are executed by the Linux rendered shards; headless execution does not establish Windows rendered-output or browser acceptance.
The Windows execution artifact retains commands, source/runtime/tool identities, per-case logs and hashes, source drift and completion; actual pass claims require the dated exact workflow run.

Only the four declared Rapier texture import-descriptor text files normalize CRLF to LF for comparison; descriptor content changes still fail, and DLLs, images and all other tracked inputs retain byte-exact SHA-256 checks.

For intermittent physical actor/usable/flight stalls, use the [timeout diagnostic procedure](testing-validation-and-replay.md#physical-regression-timeout-diagnostics). The ordinary 180-second case bound is unchanged. Dispatch the full registered 600-attempt stress workflow only after it exists on `main`, with `source_sha` set to the exact immutable diagnostic source. Inspect the independent reducer and raw logs even if the Actions run badge is green or red. The [dated audit](../audits/2026-10-24-issue-233-physical-regression-timeouts.md) records executions and remaining uncertainties separately from workflow availability. **Current:** the GDExtension workflow executes the retained Windows DLL on four independent GitHub-hosted `windows-2022` runners. This lane is separate from the Windows cross-build job. The [Windows execution helper](../../tools/ci/run_windows_godot_regressions.py) requires an exact workflow checkout, committed LFS bytes, matching runtime provenance and complete coverage of the current native source/header input set. Any changed or newly added native input requires a matching runtime publication before the retained DLL can satisfy this gate. Historical build-input hashes continue to describe their original build. The helper verifies the pinned official Windows Godot 4.7 archive, executable version and Rapier runtime before import. It dynamically selects every discovered headless case, including the two profile probes and scene startup, and preserves the shared runner's per-case timeouts and error/skip rejection. Each applicable case must execute exactly once. All discovered `test_*_render.gd` cases are explicitly outside this Windows lane; Linux's rendered shards execute them. After the ACT-005 integration, the source inventory is 97 Windows headless cases and 103 Linux cases, with import counted separately. These counts describe discovery, not an executed pass. Each shard uses `--shard-count 4 --shard-index 0..3` and retains `windows-execution.json`, source/runtime/tool identities, commands, individual logs and their SHA-256 hashes under its `windows-godot-headless-<shard>-<run-id>` artifact even when execution fails. The independent coverage reducer requires all four assignments and original logs, and cannot pass an admitted failed/missing matrix. The [production CI audit](../audits/2026-10-31-ci-parallel-production-integration.md) records source-qualified predecessor counts and timings; discover the actual current inventory rather than reusing the older ACT-005 count above. The report records incomplete import, failed cases, source drift and final completion explicitly. Only the four declared Rapier texture `.import` descriptors normalize CRLF to LF for content comparison: the hosted checkout and Godot's re-save can differ in newline representation. Changes to descriptor content still fail. All other tracked inputs use raw SHA-256, including DLLs, images and source, so binary byte changes cannot be hidden by text normalization. The execution step is bounded to 40 minutes within a 45-minute job. Use the dated audit and exact workflow run to establish actual platform results; this lane does not establish Windows rendered-output or browser acceptance.

Section: Testing, validation, and replay > CI execution sharding
Linux hosted GDExtension validation may execute the current Godot suite as four isolated shards after a single verified runtime build. Sharding is an execution schedule only: automatic `test_*.gd` discovery, both explicit profile probes and scene startup remain in the suite, every non-import case must occur exactly once across the four shards, and every shard performs its own import preflight. A failed shard fails the aggregate Linux gate while the remaining shards continue to retain evidence. The deterministic planner records the complete assignment and per-case timings. Approximate weights are scheduling hints from dated CI evidence, not acceptance limits. The initial migration checkpoint executed the unsharded suite against the same source/runtime artifact and proved exact case coverage equivalence. The serial lane is retained as an explicit opt-in diagnostic, while ordinary PR validation uses the four isolated shards. Every discovered `test_*_render.gd` case requires a display and executes with the OpenGL compatibility renderer. Linux CI provides Xvfb and Mesa software rendering; logic cases and import retain `--headless`. An explicit skip, missing display or executable, timeout, nonzero exit, or engine/script error fails the applicable case. An exit code of zero alone cannot satisfy the gate. Pixel assertions are rendered-output evidence for the recorded software backend, not target-GPU performance evidence. `--keep-going` retains outcomes for all assigned cases after an ordinary test failure; an import failure still stops that shard because the project could not be prepared. `timings.json` records the executed command, display requirement, skip/error details, completion state and aggregate status. The planner and runner regressions execute child processes to check failure, timeout, skip and continuation handling as well as exact discovery and assignment. The separate GitHub-hosted Windows lane runs import and every applicable headless case against the retained Windows DLL, after verifying the committed LFS bytes, provenance and complete current native-input set. It uses the same discovery, per-case timeouts and strict failure semantics, continues after individual case failures, and records graphical cases as explicitly outside its scope. Its `windows-execution.json` includes exact case coverage, tool/source/runtime identities, commands, log hashes and drift/completion checks. The [Windows execution procedure](local-build-and-validation.md#windows-retained-runtime-execution) owns the job bounds and artifact route. This actual execution gate and the separate Windows cross-build check must retain their distinct evidence scopes.

Section: Current validation and retained M11 integrity > Which build and CI gates use each policy?
**Current:** native builders retain compiler, SCons and exact godot-cpp source checks. M11 archive/output byte equality requires the explicit `CYBERSAND_VERIFY_M11_OUTPUT=1` flag; an explicit historical check is never bypassed by the existing toolchain-drift override. Normal current outputs are identified and tested independently. M11 output constants and dependency locks are retained. The existing local override can still bypass compiler/dirty-source checks; inspect and record those inputs. It is not a reproducible-release attestation. Documentation CI checks current identity, retained M11 integrity, checker failure contracts and both retrieval sets. It checks out the pinned companion workspace because canonical links cross the two repositories. Release hashing separates current runtime/provenance manifests from historical records. GDExtension CI builds Linux and Windows from current source. Its Linux job installs the freshly built extension, checks the ABI floor, then runs every `test_*.gd`, two profiles, project import and scene smoke using exact Godot 4.7. It retains source/binary identity and logs. The earlier separate Godot workflow, which loaded the retained M11 Linux binary and a fixed fixture list, is superseded; Git history preserves it. Windows cross-compilation is not Windows execution. **Current workflow extension, 2026-10-20:** a separate Windows job now executes every applicable headless case using the retained, source-matched Windows DLL and pinned Windows Godot 4.7. Its harness checks the complete native input set, committed LFS/provenance identity, exact case coverage and source drift. See [Windows retained-runtime execution](local-build-and-validation.md#windows-retained-runtime-execution). The build-only Windows job remains a separate check; neither its success nor Linux execution substitutes for actual Windows execution. Linux graphical shards retain ownership of display-dependent pixel checks. **Planned, still tracked by issue #3:** Web producer/consumer toolchain alignment, real CI runtime coverage and current export/template provenance. Local browser acceptance for issues #1/#2 has its own recorded artifact identity. No historical hash reconciliation settles these separate Web obligations.

results.query: Where can I open the full Deepworks map, watch its foreground and background chemistry exhibits, and replay a room after the guided tour has passed it?
facts: The desktop launcher, --deepworks user argument or res://deepworks.tscn opens one total 1024 by 1024 map with sixteen 256 by 256 districts and 32 paired native exhibits. It is a free-camera material viewer with foreground/rear painting, not the ordinary actor sandbox.

Four independent full-size native worlds run at target rates play 30 Hz, scripted rear 20 Hz, effects 15 Hz and frozen background zero. The live rear supplies the interacting background sets; the fourth distant architecture plane is never ticked. Source events supply reactants while native rules own the products.

The serpentine camera tour changes district every 14 running seconds, or 224 seconds per nominal circuit, while every district continues simulating. Finite reaction feeds can finish before a late visit. Whole-map R reset restores all four worlds and sources, pauses and preserves the camera; P then replays the selected view. Camera selection and layer hiding alone do not reset or pause worlds.

Section: Deepworks — the exhibition below > How do the scripted drops and reactions work?
The current recipe contains **77 bounded source events**. Each record names a unique ID, district, target plane, rectangle, material, first native tick, period and repetition limit. Immediately before that plane's due native tick, the owner applies its due source rectangles, then calls the ordinary native step. The scheduler supplies reagents and environmental edits; native rules produce and subsequently move or consume the reaction products. Apparatus descriptions and expected-product metadata do not paint results into the world. Reaction feeds have finite repetition limits so completed specimens and their products can be inspected. Repeating environmental sources and drains are confined to the effects plane. Switching **Automatic material sources** off prevents future scheduled writes while existing material continues to simulate. Switching it back on admits future due ticks; missed opportunities are not replayed in a catch-up burst. Pause stops the three dynamic clocks and freezes material animation. **N** advances each active dynamic plane once; this manual step is not one frame of the normal 30/20/15 Hz pacing. The **guided tour** starts simulation and follows a serpentine district route, changing view every 14 running seconds. A nominal circuit takes 224 seconds. It is camera automation: it neither resets districts on arrival nor delays their native clocks until visited. A late visit can therefore show an already completed reaction. Stop the tour and use **R**, then **P**, to replay a room from its original state while retaining its camera view. The complete candidate programme and all four authoring layers are validated before replacement. Invalid dimensions, rectangles, material IDs, schedules or capacity requests preserve the current exhibition. Successful reset advances the generation and clears earlier queued commands and event counters. The [configuration reference](../reference/configuration-reference.md#depth-host-and-deepworks-configuration) owns event and authoring limits. This dedicated programme does not change the shared MicroScenario schema or implement general serialized replay. Source: [`CyberDeepworksRuntime.install()`, `_validate_programme()` and `_step_layer()`](../../godot/scripts/exhibition/deepworks_runtime.gd), [`CyberDeepworks._process()` and `toggle_tour()`](../../godot/scripts/exhibition/deepworks.gd) and [`CyberDeepworksMap.recipe_hash()`](../../godot/scripts/exhibition/deepworks_map.gd). The recipe hash includes all four layer definitions and explicit event fields; it identifies authored content, not a saved running state.

| Input or control | Result | |---|---| | **P / Space** | Run or pause all three dynamic planes and their material animation. | | **N / Step** | Pause and advance each active dynamic plane by one native tick. | | **R / Reset** | Restore all worlds, specimens and sources; pause while preserving the current camera. | | **District grid**, **[ / ]** | Select a 256 × 256 district view without changing material state. | | **Inspect foreground / rear setup** | Centre a 200 × 200 view on that district's selected apparatus. | | **O / Home / Whole map** | Show the full 1024 × 1024 composition. | | **WASD / arrows**, **middle-drag** | Pan the camera. | | **Mouse wheel** | Zoom around the pointer; supported view widths run from 128 to 1024 cells. | | **T / Guided tour** | Start or stop the camera tour; starting it also resumes a paused exhibition. | | **1–5** | Foreground only, quantized relief, four material layers, Hybrid depth, Diorama cutaway. | | **Layer visibility checkboxes** | Show or hide foreground, rear apparatus, atmosphere or distant architecture. | | **Automatic material sources** | Enable or disable scheduled material writes; existing native reactions continue. | | **Paint foreground / Paint rear apparatus** | Choose the independently editable native world. | | **Left mouse / right mouse** | Add the chosen material / erase, using the selected brush radius of 1–8 cells. | | **F8 / Tab** | Hide or show the controls for a clean view. | | **F2 / Escape** | Close the exhibition and return to the feature launcher. | The painting palette includes Water, Sand, Acid, Spark, Fire, Lava, Salt, Steam, Brine, Oil, Packed Snow, Thermite Brick, Magnesium Plate, Quicklime Block and Wall. Pointer coordinates use the selected plane's inverse parallax transform, so rear painting and the foreground brush target their own visible native cells. UI interaction, modal menus and focus loss release painting/panning input; a fresh press is required after those boundaries. Arrow keys continue adjusting a focused brush slider without moving the camera. Click the map to return keyboard focus to it, then release and freshly press any movement key held while using a control. Section: Deepworks — the exhibition below > Open, inspect and replay a setup
Choose **Deepworks** in the desktop feature launcher, pass the user argument `--deepworks`, or open [`res://deepworks.tscn`](../../godot/deepworks.tscn) directly: ```sh godot --path godot -- --deepworks godot --path godot res://deepworks.tscn ``` Use the pinned Godot and materialized native libraries from the [build guide](local-build-and-validation.md). Deepworks starts paused in the whole-map Hybrid view. Click a district, then **Inspect foreground setup** or **Inspect rear setup** for a closer view and the apparatus description. Press **P** to start its native clocks and material sources. This is a free-camera material exhibition with painting controls. It has no ordinary actor session, player-follow mode or F5 actor picker. The shared foreground circulation is real cleared native geometry: horizontal galleries and vertical shafts make 24 internal district connections. Camera movement and district selection preserve the entire map and all ongoing reactions. Reaction supplies are finite. To watch a selected setup from its original condition, choose the district or apparatus, press **R**, then **P**. **R resets all four worlds and all sixteen districts**, reinstalls the source programme, and pauses; it preserves the camera and selected district. It is not a local specimen refill. The resulting products remain in the world until further native interactions, painting or a whole-map reset changes them. ![Deepworks controls and district notes](../images/deepworks/deepworks-guide.png) Source: [`CyberDeepworks._ready()`, `reset_exhibition()`, `select_district()` and `focus_exhibit()`](../../godot/scripts/exhibition/deepworks.gd).

Section: Deepworks — the exhibition below > Four full-size worlds and independent clocks
Every plane owns a separate **1024 × 1024 native material world**. The displayed map remains 1024 × 1024 in total; the four overlapping planes do not form a 2048 × 2048 terrain or sixteen separately loaded scenes. | Internal plane | UI name | Running target | Authority and coverage | |---|---|---:|---| | `play` | Foreground | 30 Hz | Full map, cleared circulation and sixteen interactive foreground apparatuses. | | `scripted` | Rear reactions & machinery | 20 Hz | Full map, independent rear scenery and sixteen native apparatuses. | | `effects` | Atmosphere | 15 Hz | Authored atmospheric material and bounded local environmental sources across every district. | | `background` | Distant architecture | 0 Hz | Full authored distant map, never ticked; the first copied material publication is cached. | The **rear layer** is the interacting background set: it runs real native material drops, reactions and transport. The fourth plane, whose internal key is `background`, is deliberately frozen distant architecture. Its pixels are rendered through the same canonical material appearance system. Hiding a plane only changes visibility; it does not pause its native clock or source schedule. All districts run together, including those outside the camera. The host serializes adapter calls into its four isolated worlds. Rendering consumes copied RG8 packets, never mutable native storage. Failure of a native step or publication stops the exhibition and freezes presentation; it is not silently replaced with a successful frame. Layer visibility, parallax, relief, haze and liquid reflections do not transfer cells, charge, mass or collisions between worlds. The [depth contract](../systems/depth-layers-and-parallax.md) owns their rendering and publication rules. Source: [`CyberDeepworks.reset_exhibition()` and `_fault()`](../../godot/scripts/exhibition/deepworks.gd), [`CyberDeepworksRuntime`](../../godot/scripts/exhibition/deepworks_runtime.gd) and [`CyberDepthLayerRuntime`](../../godot/scripts/depth/depth_layer_runtime.gd).

Section: Deepworks — the exhibition below > What is the map?
**Current source:** Deepworks is one **1024 × 1024 total map**, divided into a 4 × 4 grid of sixteen 256 × 256 districts. Every district has foreground architecture, an independent rear apparatus and service layer, local atmosphere, and a distant architectural scene. Its **32 exhibits** pair one foreground setup with one rear setup per district. The composition uses all **51 MAT-002 building materials, IDs 81–131**, including architectural specimens and material swatches; the [building catalogue](../systems/building-material-catalogue.md) owns their actual native rules and material identities. The map extends the layered presentation of [Strata Theatre](../systems/depth-layers-and-parallax.md), with the connected industrial composition and small architectural details of the earlier showcase maps. Numbered bays, valves, pipe clamps, specimen shelves, signal lamps, cargo, stained windows, domestic niches and distant machinery give each district a distinct setting. Foreground apertures deliberately expose the rear apparatus. Full coverage means all four planes are authored across all sixteen districts; open space remains part of the composition. Source: [`CyberDeepworksMap.build()`](../../godot/scripts/exhibition/deepworks_map.gd), [`CyberDeepworksArchitecture`](../../godot/scripts/exhibition/deepworks_architecture.gd) and [`CyberDeepworksExhibits.build()`](../../godot/scripts/exhibition/deepworks_exhibits.gd). ![Deepworks atlas rendered from the four material planes](../images/deepworks/deepworks-atlas.png) The atlas is a 2048 × 2048 presentation capture of the 1024 × 1024 map. Image resolution does not enlarge the simulation. The sixteen retained 512 × 512 tile images are exact crops of this atlas.

results.query: Can a depth host use non-square or 1024 by 1024 material surfaces without changing Strata Theatre defaults, and what happens to its old world or pixels after an invalid resize or stale packet?
facts: Depth runtime reset accepts an authored size with each axis from 8 through 1024, including non-square worlds, and keeps 640 by 360 as the default. Compositor and surface configure methods use the same accepted ROI while retaining 1024 by 1024 native RG8 backing. Deepworks selects 1024 by 1024 for all four planes; no native ABI changes follow.

Reset validates the complete candidate before replacing worlds, dimensions, clocks, cached background, queued commands or generation. Invalid dimensions, geometry or reserved material ID 10 preserve the prior live state. Guard, weather and effects sinks follow the accepted extent.

Compositor set_view validates origin and extent, synchronizes uniforms/layout and clamps the camera; configured world dimensions cannot be changed in place. Surface packet validation stages all patches before the first blit and rejects older reset generations even when their serial is higher, preserving pixels, accepted serial, tick and generation.

Section: Depth layers and parallax prototypes > Four material planes
The prototype owns four separate CyberNativeCellWorld objects through CyberDepthLayerRuntime. Each world uses the existing native material IDs, rules and RG8 RenderBridge projection. Godot owns only authoring, presentation and explicit lab commands. | Plane | Strata default rate | Intended use | |---|---:|---| | play | 60 Hz | Active foreground/play material. | | scripted | 20 Hz | Rear set, destructible scenery and set-piece sequences that should not perturb foreground material. | | effects | 30 Hz | Rain, snow-like Dust, Steam fog, Spark energy and other environmental material effects. | | background | 0 Hz | Authored distant city. It is never ticked and its first copied RG8 publication is cached. | The rates are independent. Dynamic planes may be reduced or paused without changing the others. The background rejects non-zero rates. Deepworks selects 30/20/15/0 Hz for play/scripted/effects/background. Every Deepworks plane spans the full 1024 × 1024 authored map; the rear `scripted` world runs native reactions while the true `background` world remains frozen. Each plane has its own render canvas and a material surface covering the accepted authored ROI, defaulting to 640 × 360 in Strata Theatre. Frozen surfaces request a one-shot bake when a copied publication arrives or updates are paused, so pausing before the first draw still renders the admitted state. See [`CyberDepthLayerSurface.apply_packet()` and `set_render_enabled()`](../../godot/scripts/depth/depth_layer_surface.gd). The current host uses one native adapter owner and serializes calls into its four worlds. Production adoption should integrate the play plane with the existing asynchronous owner rather than introduce another mutable owner.

Section: Depth layers and parallax prototypes > Parallax and authoring coordinates
**Strata Theatre defaults** to a 640 × 360 authored ROI over the existing 1024 × 1024 native backing. Its initial scale/parallax factors are: - play 1.00 / 1.00; - scripted 0.94 / 0.70; - effects 0.88 / 0.44; - background 0.78 / 0.18. **Current parameterized API:** [`CyberDepthLayerRuntime.reset(definitions, authored_size)`](../../godot/scripts/depth/depth_layer_runtime.gd) accepts each authored axis from 8 through 1024, including non-square worlds. Omitting the size retains 640 × 360. It validates the whole candidate before replacement; rejected dimensions, geometry or material ID 10 leave the existing worlds, clocks, cached background, queued edits and reset generation intact. Guard cells, effects sinks, weather, authoring bounds and simulation interest all use the accepted `world_size`. [`CyberDepthCompositor.configure(authored_size)`](../../godot/scripts/depth/depth_compositor.gd) configures that size before the compositor enters the scene tree. `set_view(origin, extent)` synchronizes the view uniforms and layout, clamps the camera to the authored extent and refuses invalid/non-finite views before mutation. An already configured compositor cannot be resized to a different world. `CyberDepthLayerSurface.configure(id, frozen, authored_size)` likewise sets the complete material viewport ROI while retaining the 1024 × 1024 RG8 backing. Each plane has its own canvas and material surface. Deepworks sets all layer scales to 1, with closely spaced parallax factors so rear apparatus remains associated with its district at every corner of the map. The [configuration reference](../reference/configuration-reference.md#depth-host-and-deepworks-configuration) owns exact dimensions, rate, event and presentation limits. `screen_to_layer()` is the exact inverse of the rendered layer transform. Painting therefore addresses the selected world's cell under the pointer.

Section: Depth layers and parallax prototypes > Material-surface rendering and bounds
Each world is rendered by CyberDepthLayerSurface through the existing material_palette.gdshader and CyberMaterialAppearanceLut. The private compositing palette only changes Empty alpha to zero; material IDs and the canonical appearance program remain unchanged. Copied native packets are validated before changing an Image: RG8 only, matching layer identity, nondecreasing reset generation and monotonic integer serial within a generation, at most 4096 patches and 2 MiB packet bytes, in-bounds rectangle/stride data, cumulative staged area no greater than one 1024x1024 backing, and exact full-refresh shape. Every patch Image is constructed before the first blit. A packet from an older reset generation is refused even if it has a higher serial. Rejection leaves pixels, accepted serial, tick and generation intact. This is enforced in [`CyberDepthLayerSurface._validate_packet()`](../../godot/scripts/depth/depth_layer_surface.gd). ImageTexture.update currently uploads the whole 1024x1024 RG8 image after an admitted changed packet: **2 MiB per changed layer upload**. Region texture uploads or a smaller presentation backing are the clearest follow-up optimizations.

In `--player-playground` (optionally `--player=ID`), use 1–7 or Tab/Shift+Tab to select, R to restart, P/Escape to pause, F for overview/follow, and F2 for the launcher. These scene controls accompany the movement actions below. | Key / ID | Preset | Movement and actions | |---|---|---| | **1** / `stuntbuggy` | **Loose Cannon** — loose-jointed stunt buggy | W/S drive/reverse; A/D or Q/E lean and rotate in air; Space hops from support; Shift brakes; hold C for recovery assistance. Sprung wheels and a hinged rider carry the motion. | | **2** / `trialsbike` | **Trials Rat** — trials bike | W/S throttle/reverse; A/D or Q/E lean; hold Space while supported to preload, then release to hop; Shift brakes; hold C for recovery assistance. The rear wheel drives and the front wheel rolls freely until braking. | | **3** / `acrobat` | **Afterimage** — momentum acrobat | A/D run and steer in air; Space jumps, then double jumps; hold Shift or S to slide; tap Shift to roll; Shift+Space or S+Space bullet jumps; C cancels/brakes and, held in air, glides. Mouse position aims bullet jumps. | | **4** / `arcadelander` | **Vector Rush** — arcade lander | W or Space fires the body-axis main engine; A/D or Q/E rotates; S gives reverse thrust; Shift applies a strong airbrake; tap C toggles damped flight/coast. | | **5** / `dryswarm` | **Dust Devil** — Sand cloud | WASD guides actual Sand; Space surges in the movement direction, or upward from neutral; Shift spreads; C gathers. Neutral admitted input keeps the cohesion/loft field active. | | **6** / `liquidswarm` | **Undertow** — Water blob | WASD guides actual Water; Space surges; Shift squeezes transverse to travel into a stream; C gathers. Neutral admitted input keeps the cohesion/loft field active. | | **7** / `jetbarrel` | **Barrel Rocket** — barrel with jetpack | W or Space fires the body-axis jet; A/D or Q/E provides strong rotation; S gives reverse thrust; Shift brakes; hold C for upright assistance. | Arrow keys duplicate WASD in the dedicated scene. The lander and barrel thrust along their current orientation, so rotation changes the direction of the next burst. Damping and recovery are authored game assistance with bounded forces; contacts and rigid-body motion remain Rapier's responsibility. A cancelled bike preload is discarded without firing a hop.

Section: Articulated Rapier actors and shared physical control > How do I select and control them?
F5 in the ordinary sandbox, Blacksite Nine and the four showcase districts selects a representation, set, actor and keyboard, scripted-demo or external policy producer. Physical Rapier choices are the default actor route. Applying rebuilds the selected map at its initial spawn and starts paused. R retains the selection; changing district uses that district's spawn. Registered scientific fixtures and Benchmark mode retain their own actors. The new assembly remains suspended until its matching native reset and initial hard-terrain colliders are installed, including when Play is requested early. Physical wire controls are WASD movement, mouse aim, brackets for effort, Q/E trim, Z/X reel, Space primary, Shift secondary and C auxiliary. M uses the tool, N releases a held item and U requests nearby pickup. Left/right pointer buttons use equipment primary/alternate; its aim and power are independent of locomotion. F5 equipment selection changes a held chassis through the same admitted action. Exact ability meaning is displayed from the selected profile. These map to `tool`, `release_usable` and `attach_usable` in the shared API. These are bounded gameplay requests; no command writes a transform or assigns velocity as locomotion. Focus loss, pause, replacement and input cancellation revoke pending actions. SetP supplies five distinct human movement controllers through the same action path. Its buggy/bike use vertical movement for throttle and horizontal movement for lean; the acrobat supplies slides, rolls, bullet/double jumps, cancels and glide. results.query: How do I chain Afterimage slides, rolls, bullet jumps, double jumps and airglide, and can cancelling reload those airborne moves?
facts: A/D runs and steers, Space jumps/double jumps, holding Shift or S slides, tapping Shift rolls, and Shift/S plus Space requests an aimed bullet jump; actual joints tuck the physical body.

Space can jump-cancel a roll using available inventory; held crouch requests a bullet jump first. C cancels/brakes and held airborne C glides near the apex/fall with positive gravity and finite reserve. Releasing Space shortens an ordinary jump.

One extra jump, one bullet jump, one air roll and glide reserve recharge after confirmed landing. Cancelling, focus changes and authority transitions clear intent without replenishing spent airborne inventory or erasing velocity.

Section: Player control playground > Acrobat movement chains and cancels
Afterimage preserves momentum through a low-drag slide and uses actual folding hip/ankle joints for its tucked posture. Steering during slides and rolls is weaker than running; reversing input changes momentum gradually. A held crouch can keep the tuck during a brief loss of support. The controller does not teleport the body or replace its velocity with a character trajectory. - **Run → slide → bullet jump:** gain speed with A/D, hold Shift or S to tuck, aim with the mouse, then press Space. Grounded bullet jumps include an upward component; faster velocity already aligned with the launch is retained. - **Jump → double jump → roll → glide:** Space gives the ground jump and one airborne jump. Press Shift in air for the separate air roll. Hold C near the apex or while falling to reduce descent while steering with A/D. - **Roll → jump cancel:** press Space during a roll to leave it using an available jump. If Shift/S remains held, the same press requests a bullet jump first while that separate launch is available. Release crouch for an ordinary jump cancel. - **Slide/roll → brake cancel:** press C to end the slide or roll. On support, C brakes; slide stays suppressed until crouch is released. Releasing Space early shortens an ordinary jump. Q/E adds airborne attitude trim. The controller supplies a short coyote window and input buffer. One airborne jump, one bullet jump, one air roll and a finite glide reserve recharge after confirmed support, not after focus changes or cancellation. Glide retains positive gravity and has a finite duration; it is not hover. Exact timing and actuation limits belong to the [configuration reference](../reference/configuration-reference.md#player-playground-values). Sources: [acrobat controller](../../godot/scripts/player_acrobat_controller.gd) and [physical rig actuator](../../godot/scripts/physical_actor_rig.gd).

F5 in the ordinary sandbox, Blacksite Nine and the four showcase districts selects a representation, set, actor and keyboard, scripted-demo or external policy producer. Physical Rapier choices are the default actor route. Applying rebuilds the selected map at its initial spawn and starts paused. R retains the selection; changing district uses that district's spawn. Click **Build selected session**, wait for the actual applied actor/policy, release controls, then **Play / resume**. Use the in-host **Play session** button to change rigs. results.query: Do the dry cloud and liquid blob move real native material, and what prevents steering from repainting Water, moving it through walls or scanning the whole world?
facts: The dedicated exclusive owner applies a between-tick native field to local Sand or Water, then runs the normal native simulation. Complete stored cells and temperature move through existing relocation; partial Water quantity is exact within the call. No per-cell Rapier objects, erase/repaint or Water kernel rewrite is introduced.

The radius-32 selection scans at most 4225 candidate positions, snapshots at most 512 sources once and attempts at most four axis-adjacent moves each. Occupied cells, terrain, transient bodies, bounds and unavailable destination storage refuse moves; invalid commands refuse mutation.

The field selects matching material by location, so environmental material may join and material outside the circle is uncontrolled. Centre following uses the observed quantity-weighted centroid, not a remote cursor or hidden persistent parcel cohort.

Section: pressure_flow_v1 reference — corrected Water pressure family > Kernel (`update_water_pressure`)
Stages 1, 2, 4, 5 of the [material hooks](liquid-solver-family-policy.md#material-hooks-versus-motion-gate-c-correction-2026-10-23) are unchanged: pair chemistry runs before dispatch, the coherence countdown is kept and suppresses lateral motion, `mix_after_motion` receives the real moved quantity, body-mask contact uses `record_transient_contact`, and identity stays `Material::Water`. Stage 3 is replaced: 1. **Gravity:** down, then the two diagonals; into Water only to visible capacity (never overfill), otherwise `try_move` (whole tuple and sidecar). 2. **Overfill relief/relay:** overfill rises into unsaturated Water or creates Water in Empty above; a saturated column relays it whole (receiver not epoch-marked, so a bottom-up scan reaches the surface in one tick); under a lid it spreads sideways toward less overfill when the difference is ≥ 2. 3. **Adhesion film:** kept only for a **resting** thin cell (flow 0). 4. **Velocity:** `flow += gradient × kAccelNumerator / maximum` (deterministic dither), where `gradient = (h(x−2)+h(x−1)−h(x+1)−h(x+2))/2`. A sample at x±2 is used **only** if both faces toward it are open (Water or Empty); a wall, foreign liquid or body mask is a closed face that reflects the cell's own head. Overfill adds `kOverfillStiffnessRows × maximum` per unit (v1: 0). Start dead band 128/255 of a row (static friction above integer-gas gauge noise), moving band 10/255; `kRetain` 256/256 and `kFriction` 0 (momentum is lost only through mass-weighted merges and contacts). 5. **Surface skin:** a resting top-of-run cell relaxes sub-row steps with the FreeMass ¾ rule and `tolerance()`; saturated cells and overfill never move here. 6. **Flux:** `|flow| × quantity / kFlowScale` (dither) toward `sign(flow)`; Empty receives a new cell carrying this tick's **updated** velocity (front ≤ 1 cell/tick, receiver epoch-marked); Water receives visible then overfill capacity with a mass-weighted velocity merge whose truncation remainder is booked (`PressureFlowLedger.flow_remainder`). A source with Water directly above never empties laterally (no interior voids). A closed face zeroes flow and books `contact_loss`. Every direct authoritative write is witnessed like `transfer_water` (job effects or serial dirty/wake/discovery). Per-job ledgers merge after the phase barrier; there are no shared counters. Partial transfers propagate the maximum source/receiver coherence, capturing source coherence before an emptied tuple is retired. Every successful quantity transfer calls the unchanged material post-motion hook with its actual moved quantity, including surface skin and overfill relief/relay; the hook itself determines whether that motion qualifies for grain carrying. Reaction products start at family defaults even when a product retains Water identity. Same-material coherence countdowns retain family state. Repainting an identical visible tuple still publishes dirty/wake/discovery witnesses if its pressure state changed.

Section: Player control playground > Native Sand cloud and Water blob ownership
The [playground runtime](../../godot/scripts/player_playground_runtime.gd) exclusively owns one synchronous native World for a material preset. Setup seeds 256 Sand or Water cells. Each admitted step applies the native field before the ordinary material tick; normal kernels still own gravity, Water flow and reactions. Mechanical presets instead use the existing synchronous physical arena and its main-thread Rapier session. Neither lane borrows the asynchronous sandbox worker's World. `World::apply_player_material_field` moves complete stored cells through `relocate_stored_cell`, preserving compact state, temperature and exact partial Water quantity within that call. It does not erase/repaint the cloud, create per-cell physics bodies, or introduce a Water pressure/flow rule. The next normal tick can redistribute Water and apply ordinary interactions. A field therefore does not promise conservation across unrelated chemistry or authoring actions. Selection is **matching material within a local radius**, not a persistent collection of owned particles. Nearby environmental Sand/Water can join; material that leaves the field is no longer controlled. The field follows the returned quantity-weighted material centroid with a bounded centre adjustment. WASD moves material rather than a remote selection cursor. The visible ring shows this local selection boundary. The native call scans at most 4,225 candidate positions within a radius-32 selection, captures at most 512 source parcels once, and attempts at most four axis-adjacent moves per parcel. Stable ordering and phase-based scan rotation prevent repeated source processing. Occupied cells, hard terrain, transient bodies, world bounds and unavailable destination storage stop a step. No occupied cell is overwritten. Invalid commands and failed/in-tick Worlds are refused before mutation. Exact API, receipt and limits are in [interfaces](../reference/interfaces-and-message-contracts.md#player-material-field-control) and [configuration](../reference/configuration-reference.md#player-playground-values).

Correction requested by the [independent review](../audits/2026-10-23-lcb000-independent-admission-review.md). Historical prepass anchors are `world.cpp` at `9012425`/`4caa2c3`; those line numbers identify the baseline, not the merged pressure or residual-native files. **Current dispatch, per cell.** The sequence is: - `World::update_cell` (L3500) skips any position under a transient body mask; - it calls `update_rule_kernel` (L2725 onward); - that computes the temporal lanes (`contact_chemistry_due`, `lifecycle_due` and so on, L2753); - then runs **generic pair chemistry before any kernel** (`has_pair_reactions` block, L2797–L2826); - then the `RuleKernel` switch (L2829). The Water kernel is `update_water` (L2650–L2723), which mixes material behaviour with FreeMass motion. A family-aware implementation splits each cell step into five stages: | Stage | Owner | Water content today | Under W-CY / W-PF / W-IN | |---|---|---|---| | 1. Contact chemistry | material (generic, pre-switch) | Pair rules with Water as a participant: Lava quench, Fire extinguish, Salt dissolve, Sodium react, Toxic Sludge, Molten Glass, BareIron, building materials | **Preserved unchanged.** Products take their own descriptor default state and family default state. Quantity follows the [state-transition matrix](#state-and-quantity-boundaries-gate-c-correction-2026-10-23). | | 2. Material pre-motion | material | Coherence countdown: `state_b` decremented each tick it is visited (L2654–L2658) | **Preserved.** The family must decrement it, and must suppress *lateral* motion while it is above zero (L2687). Gravity still runs. | | 3. Motion and quantity | **family** | Gravity: merge into Water, relocate or swap (L2663–L2682). Then the adhesion film stop (≤`film()` on a non-Water/non-Empty support, L2691–L2695), `lateral_due` cadence, and the ¾-difference same-row relaxation with `tolerance()` (L2698–L2720). | **Replaced** by the family law. Adhesion is defined on fractional mass, so it is **not applicable** to whole-cell W-CY or whole-cell W-IN v1, which always hold `maximum()`. That is declared, not hidden. W-PF must state whether it keeps the film rule. | | 4. Section: Player control playground > Gamepad and quick scene controls
The dedicated scene samples the first connected standard gamepad. Its left stick supplies WASD, A supplies Space/primary, B supplies Shift/secondary, X supplies C/auxiliary, and the shoulder buttons supply Q/E trim. Start pauses. The stick has a radial deadzone and is combined with keyboard input before unit-length clamping. The mouse supplies aim while inside the play view; otherwise movement supplies aim, with a diagonal fallback at neutral. Gamepad mapping is implemented; physical controller qualification is separate. **Accepted PLAY-UI-004 shared-course event slice:** The normal desktop scene attaches a small main-thread [gamepad event bridge](../../godot/scripts/playable_course_gamepad_events.gd). When the existing course/human SetP capability gate is active, unhandled A/B/X press and release events from the first connected pad invoke the existing `publish_actor_keyboard_input` path immediately. This lets its existing bounded physical-session FIFO retain a short tap between physical callbacks, rather than relying only on the next polled state. Controls receive events first; other devices, unmapped buttons and non-course/specialist configurations are not intercepted. Focus, pause, reset, rearm, equipment and epoch authority stay in the original host; the bridge never steps or owns any simulation object. Analog stick/trim polling and standalone scene behavior are unchanged. The [focused fixture](../../godot/tests/test_play_ui004_gamepad_events.gd) uses genuine Viewport events and physical-session/Rapier steps, with a disclosed synthetic selected-device index and test host publisher. It verifies ordered button pairs and a matched no-event/poll-only negative control, not a physical controller, the complete desktop focus path or interactive feel. [PR #286](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/pull/286) merged as `e076819e086abb762796303b830314e330f87234`; its source-matched Windows/Linux fixture passed **32 assertions per OS**. The later combined #284 suite preserves that fixture. The [dated candidate audit](../audits/2026-10-28-play-ui004-gamepad-events.md) records the gap, test boundaries and integration obligations. | Control | Scene operation | |---|---| | 1–7 or preset buttons | Select a preset and construct a fresh course/session | | Tab / Shift+Tab | Select next / previous preset | | R or Restart | Reset the selected preset and course; keep this scene's best times | | P, Escape or gamepad Start | Pause/resume; pause revokes current input | | F or camera button | Toggle course overview and player-follow view | | F2 or Menu | Close the current owner and return to the feature launcher | Selection, restart, pause and focus changes require movement/action controls to be released before input rearms. Window focus loss, GUI focus or a mouse-button press cancels pending control. Focus loss alone does not pause the physics; uncontrolled material settles and mechanical momentum continues. Use pause to stop stepping. The scene begins running after successful setup, unlike the ordinary F5 map replacement, which begins paused. Source: [local sampler](../../godot/scripts/player_playground_input.gd)

Section: Articulated Rapier actors and shared physical control > How do I select and control them?
F5 in the ordinary sandbox, Blacksite Nine and the four showcase districts selects a representation, set, actor and keyboard, scripted-demo or external policy producer. Physical Rapier choices are the default actor route. Applying rebuilds the selected map at its initial spawn and starts paused. R retains the selection; changing district uses that district's spawn. Registered scientific fixtures and Benchmark mode retain their own actors. The new assembly remains suspended until its matching native reset and initial hard-terrain colliders are installed, including when Play is requested early. Physical wire controls are WASD movement, mouse aim, brackets for effort, Q/E trim, Z/X reel, Space primary, Shift secondary and C auxiliary. M uses the tool, N releases a held item and U requests nearby pickup. Left/right pointer buttons use equipment primary/alternate; its aim and power are independent of locomotion. F5 equipment selection changes a held chassis through the same admitted action. Exact ability meaning is displayed from the selected profile. These map to `tool`, `release_usable` and `attach_usable` in the shared API. These are bounded gameplay requests; no command writes a transform or assigns velocity as locomotion. Focus loss, pause, replacement and input cancellation revoke pending actions. SetP supplies five distinct human movement controllers through the same action path. Its buggy/bike use vertical movement for throttle and horizontal movement for lean; the acrobat supplies slides, rolls, bullet/double jumps, cancels and glide. Full controls and the separate seven-preset keyboard/gamepad course are in the [player control playground](player-control-playground.md). Its dry/liquid presets are native material fields and are not members of the Rapier roster. The retained single-body barrel/Ripper comparison is described separately in the [physical programme](../operations/physical-actor-programme.md). The current articulated Ripper is the five-part sprung crawler, not that historical hull arm. Desktop integration does not migrate the synchronous Web control owner.

Focus loss, pause, replacement and input cancellation revoke pending actions. SetP supplies five distinct human movement controllers through the same action path. Its buggy/bike use vertical movement for throttle and horizontal movement for lean; the acrobat supplies slides, rolls, bullet/double jumps, cancels and glide. Full controls and the separate seven-preset keyboard/gamepad course are in the [player control playground](player-control-playground.md). Its dry/liquid presets are native material fields and are not members of the Rapier roster. The retained single-body barrel/Ripper comparison is described separately in the [physical programme](../operations/physical-actor-programme.md). The current articulated Ripper is the five-part sprung crawler, not that historical hull arm. Desktop integration does not migrate the synchronous Web control owner.

Section: Typed spatial fields, transforms and reusable generation graphs > Which values and units are preserved?
Every output has a declared type, cell-unit exponent, component bounds, natural sampling scale, identity and conservative work cost. Unit exponents range from −8 through 8. Coordinates and geometric distances have `cells^1`; gradients reduce the input exponent by one; products add exponents. Angles are radians with exponent zero. All numeric values are finite and bounded by the declared component range within ±`1e100`. | Type | Meaning | Conversion and comparison | |---|---|---| | `normalized` | Dimensionless scalar in `[0,1]` | May drive a material mask directly through a `spatial:<id>` reference | | `scalar` | General scalar, including signed values, with a declared unit exponent | No implicit clamping; `to_mask` explicitly maps its `low..high` interval into `[0,1]` | | `signed_distance` | Negative inside, zero at the boundary, positive outside, measured in cells | Only supported exact constructions retain this qualification; arbitrary arithmetic loses it | | `distance` | Nonnegative distance to a declared feature, with the operator's stated search scope | Bounded Poisson distance is a capped local search result; it is not an infinite-world nearest-seed guarantee | | `vector2` | Two continuous components sharing one unit exponent | Vector arithmetic, components, length, dot and normalization are explicit | | `category` | Exact tuple of signed integer x/y identity plus a 64-bit domain | Equality compares the full tuple; IDs are never numerically blended or converted to a mask | | `boolean` | Exact false/true, represented by zero/one | `equal`, `less` and local extrema produce it; explicit `to_mask` yields exact zero/one | Addition/subtraction and ordered scalar comparison require compatible units. Vector components require equal units. `equal` requires matching types and units, including exact categorical tuples. `select` consumes `[boolean, true_value, false_value]` with matching branch types/units. `mix` requires matching continuous inputs and a normalized weight. No categorical ordering or arithmetic is inferred from its payload. `category_is` compares a categorical input with an exact authored tuple. Its explicit literal domain zero selects the signed x/y ID within the input's own domain; a nonzero literal also requires exact domain equality. This supplies a declarative selector for generated district identities without requiring an author to reproduce the compiler's domain fingerprint. Ordinary `equal` still compares complete tuples. `constant` accepts normalized, general scalar, vector, category or boolean values. A constant with cell units is not automatically a distance to a shape. Distance types come from declared geometric operators. In JSON, categorical integers use exact text representations: signed decimal strings for x/y and exactly 16 lowercase hexadecimal digits for the unsigned domain. Section: Typed spatial fields, transforms and reusable generation graphs > How are typed authoring controls and diagnostics used?
The Workbench's **Typed spatial graphs** page edits the `spatial` JSON section, inserts operator drafts from the native catalogue and selects complete executable examples. It shows accepted output type, units, scale, bounds, distance qualification, identity and work. `spatial:<expanded.id>` selects a copied typed diagnostic. The display may map a signed scalar or category to colour, while the inspector preserves the raw typed value. Presentation colour is never the stored categorical identity or a material mask. GEN-004 schema-3 recipes may populate selected `spatial` geometry inputs from [immutable semantic route/feature exports](procedural-hierarchical-generation.md). The planner resolves those names before the typed compiler runs. Each export is one actual polyline or feature boundary; separate routes are never joined by invented segments. Fields retain no dependency on grammar types, live World state or partially rasterized neighboring cells. GEN-004 also reuses this finite assignment solver for declared district themes. The Workbench writes JSON with full floating-point precision. External GDScript authors should use `JSON.stringify(recipe, " ", true, true)` so the `full_precision` argument preserves accepted double values and the compiled `spatial_fingerprint`; default JSON formatting can round them. Category strings remain exact independently of that numeric formatting. Reapplying an accepted recipe intentionally advances the adapter revision and recipe fingerprint; unchanged spatial content retains its separate graph fingerprint. Only `normalized` spatial outputs may feed existing application/exclusion, aggregate variation and parameter-mapping controls. Authors must add an explicit `to_mask` conversion for signed scalars or booleans. A category can first be compared with `equal`, then explicitly converted. The initial proposal context, modifier order, restored route skeleton and final hard-material authority remain owned by the retained [field/modifier contract](procedural-generation-fields-and-modifiers.md). Executable profiles under [`examples/worldgen`](../../examples/worldgen) cover transformed industrial structure, vector-guided utilities, exact categorical districts, reusable decay masks and multiscale feature seeds. This is minimal authoring/inspection support for the native implementation; GEN-007 owns the full visual editor and content-quality tools. GEN-004 owns hierarchical places, GEN-005 semantic depth and GEN-006 persistent runtime streaming/reconciliation.

Section: Typed spatial fields, transforms and reusable generation graphs > How do immutable routes and finite region assignments work?
Geometry inputs contain an ID, 1..256 finite points and a `closed` flag; a closed boundary requires at least three points. `geometry_distance` names one immutable input and returns Euclidean distance to its point, open polyline segments or closed boundary. Closed geometry measures the boundary; it does not silently become an inside/outside classifier. A single point and repeated points have bounded explicit segment handling. Geometry is copied/prepared before publication, and its actual coordinates enter the consuming node's identity. GEN-004 can supply routes and feature boundaries through this value interface without a dependency from fields into the future grammar implementation. An assignment input declares a finite tile of at most 16×16 cells, up to 16 exact categories, four directional adjacency masks and optional per-cell domain masks. Opposite adjacency relations must be reciprocal. Deterministic propagation and bounded backtracking prepare the entire solution before a field can sample it. Unsatisfiable constraints and exhausted work are distinct explicit failures; neither exposes a partial assignment. `assigned_region` returns one exact category from the prepared tile. The tile repeats using floor addressing. `wrap_x`/`wrap_y` enable constraints across those tile edges; without a wrap constraint, adjacency is guaranteed only inside the finite tile. GEN-004 owns hierarchical layout use of this contract and should reuse this solver rather than introducing a conflicting field solver.

Section: Procedural world generation candidates > What is implemented?
**Current candidate source, GEN-001 / [#163](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/163) and GEN-002 / [#171](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/171):** three CPU procedural generators share one immutable recipe, theme hierarchy, spatial control stack and extensible native feature registry. They produce actual material IDs for signed-coordinate chunks. Generation is separate from simulation: it does not tick materials, query a mutable World, call Godot, request neighboring chunks or share a mutable random generator. The [public native API](../../native/include/cybersand/world_generation.hpp) and [implementation](../../native/src/world_generation.cpp) own these semantics. GEN-002 adds named structured-noise/finite-curve fields, scalar sidechains, masked context-aware guidance and sculpting, aggregate material recipes and paced diagnostic channels. The focused [fields and modifiers contract](procedural-generation-fields-and-modifiers.md) owns those controls, immutable initial context and finite Hilbert/Morton scope. GEN-003 / [#190](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/190) adds explicit schema-2 [typed spatial functions](procedural-typed-spatial-fields.md): signed distance/vector/category values, transformed/derived geometry, reusable parameter subgraphs, structured seeds, finite adjacency assignments and world-aligned multiresolution sampling. The retained scalar graph remains separately defined; typed spatial functions have no per-cell initial-context input. Only explicit normalized `spatial:<id>` outputs may drive existing masks and mappings. GEN-004 / [#191](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/191) adds explicit schema-3 [hierarchical semantic plans](procedural-hierarchical-generation.md). Finite canonical regions own nested places and cross-chunk structures; stable rule/slot IDs, placement constraints, matched sockets, explicit loops/service trunks and final-raster route reports precede ordinary chunk publication. Selected immutable semantic geometries may feed the typed graph. The hierarchy does not add World streaming or replace final hard material authority. | Candidate | Generated structure | Suitable starting point | |---|---|---| | `strata` | Smoothly varying surface, domain-warped caves, strata, deposits and material-specific deep fill | Organic terrain, underground spaces and theme transitions | | `flow_network` | Strata plus a connected macrocell hub/port network, carved after structural modules | Interconnected passages, service routes and excavation networks | | `district_grammar` | Global room/floor lattice with repeated doors and accents, plus the same hub/port network | Dense urban interiors, industrial districts and structured construction | ![Actual native generation with the same authored controls across the three candidates](../figures/worldgen-candidates.png) Seed 314159; each panel covers 512 by 384 cells at origin `[-256,0]`. Reproduce the material pixels with `make worldgen-demo`. This is generation output, before simulation. Every candidate consumes the same brushes, paths, overrides and feature instances. A hard candidate override can choose another generator inside a rectangular zone. This is deliberately a set of provisional algorithms, not a selected production world style or a proof of useful player navigation. In particular, generator connectivity does not establish actor clearance, gravity traversal or fluid equilibrium; the existing material and actor owners retain those semantics. **Current authoring surface:** the separate [worldgen workbench](../../godot/worldgen_workbench.tscn) previews generated material pixels and performs bounded demand generation while panning.

Section: Typed spatial fields, transforms and reusable generation graphs > How are coordinate transforms composed?
`transform` samples its source in local coordinates. For local point `q`, world point `p`, origin `o`, translation `t`, rotation `R`, shear `H` and anisotropic scale `S`, the convention is: ```text p = o + t + R H S (q − o) q = o + (R H S)^−1 (p − o − t) H = [[1, shear_x], [shear_y, 1]] S = diag(sx, sy) ``` Positive angles use the ordinary coordinate rotation matrix. World y is the generator's downward-positive axis, so the on-screen visual interpretation follows that axis convention. Translation and origin are positions in cells; angles are radians. Nested transforms compose through explicit source inputs and are bounded by graph depth and recursive sampling work. `transform_vector` samples its vector source at the original point and applies the **forward linear part** `R H S`. It does not add translation or origin. Coordinate deformation of a vector field and transformation of its vector values are therefore separate operations an author may compose deliberately. The compiler rejects zero/tiny scales, singular shears, nonfinite parameters and excessive declared bounds. Translation, rotation/reflection and uniform scale preserve an exact SDF. A uniform scale multiplies the sampled distance by the absolute scale. Anisotropic scaling or shear preserves the zero set but changes the result to a general implicit scalar. Its reported minimum/maximum distance factors are the affine matrix's singular-value bounds: multiplying the absolute local distance by those factors bounds the world distance to the transformed boundary. General warps, polar maps and coarse interpolation discard an exact-distance claim. Do not use a warped scalar as an exact clearance radius. `repeat` subtracts its phase origin and maps each axis into local `[0,period)` using floor-equivalent remainder. `mirror` folds the phase-shifted, period-doubled axis into local `[0,period]`. Negative inputs and exact seams obey the same rules as positive inputs. These coordinate maps repeat a function; they do not imply that material routes connect across the repeated boundary. `polar` samples its source at `(radius/radial_scale, angle/angular_scale)`; `log_polar` replaces the first component with `log(max(radius,min_radius)/radial_scale)`. Both measure radius/angle relative to an explicit origin. Angle uses `atan2`, with angle zero at the origin; the negative-x, zero-y branch is positive pi. Radial/angular scales map physical radius/radians into the source's sampling coordinates. The logarithm's minimum-radius clamp and angle branch seam are explicit numerical conventions, independent of resident chunks. `warp` takes `[source, displacement_vector]`; the displacement is sampled at the original point and radially capped to `max_displacement` cells before resampling the source. Repeated composition is bounded; no neighbor-generation recursion is introduced. Public samples use integer world coordinates in `[-2^40,2^40)`. Internal transformed,

Section: Procedural world generation candidates > What is the control precedence?
The evaluation order is stable and independent of manifest array insertion order. IDs are required; duplicate IDs within a layer are rejected. For brushes, paths, modifiers and hard overrides, lower `priority` runs first, with lexical ID as the tie-break. Later values win. Moving an item in a JSON array is not a hidden priority control. | Order | Control | Meaning | |---|---|---| | 1 | Global parameters and resolved theme parameters | Establish the selected candidate's initial shape and palette distribution | | 2 | Broad polyline brushstrokes | Blend theme weights and selected shape parameters using radius, strength and falloff | | 3 | Hard parameter/candidate overrides | Assign exact values within a half-open world-space rectangle | | 4 | Initial raster and context | Capture the original proposed material, surface and route context before later changes | | 5 | Scalar fields and modifier influence | Evaluate the field DAG once and capture each modifier's application/exclusion/context/shape mask | | 6 | Masked theme and geometry guidance | Apply all theme blends; reblend theme/old brush parameters; apply direct edits and mappings; reapply hard geometry controls and rasterize | | 7 | Prepared feature modules | Add or carve structured zones in dependency order, clipped to bounds and optional field masks | | 8 | Masked material or aggregate modifiers | Use the original captured influence to select discrete existing material IDs | | 9 | Shared network and explicit guide paths | Reserve connective space after modules/modifiers; a guide may carve Empty or paint another material | | 10 | Hard material overrides | Force the final material, including intentionally blocking a route | Schema 3 inserts accepted semantic shell/interior/aggregate proposals between steps 6 and 7 and restores explicit semantic passages after step 9. Existing native modules and material modifiers can therefore contribute to semantic places, while final hard material overrides still win. The hierarchy's final-cell route report observes that complete stack and reports any blocked passage; it does not reinterpret a hard override as optional. Recipes without grammar retain the table's preceding behavior. The [field/modifier contract](procedural-generation-fields-and-modifiers.md) defines the two guidance stages, mapping endpoints and immutable context. No earlier modifier can change the context observed by a later modifier. Recipes without new controls retain their old material behavior; fixed legacy hashes cover all three candidates in four signed chunks. Brush points are world-space `[x,y]` pairs. A single point is a dab; multiple points form a polyline. Influence uses distance to the nearest segment, a smooth radial falloff raised

results.query: Which signs, spacing, units and edge behavior do procedural gradient, curl, ridge and level-set curvature use across chunk boundaries?
facts: Centered first derivatives use four axial immutable absolute-world samples with spacing 1..64 cells, not resident neighboring chunks.
Gradient reduces cell exponent by one; curl is dVy/dx-dVx/dy; slope is gradient magnitude and aspect uses signed atan2 radians.
Ridge/valley use positive negative/positive Laplacian; local extrema strictly compare four axial neighbors.
Curvature uses nine-point level-set derivatives, reciprocal-cell units and an explicit zero at zero gradient; nonlinear finite differences remain approximations.
