Section: Typed spatial fields, transforms and reusable generation graphs > How are typed authoring controls and diagnostics used?
The Workbench's **Typed spatial graphs** page edits the `spatial` JSON section, inserts operator drafts from the native catalogue and selects complete executable examples. It shows accepted output type, units, scale, bounds, distance qualification, identity and work. `spatial:<expanded.id>` selects a copied typed diagnostic. The display may map a signed scalar or category to colour, while the inspector preserves the raw typed value. Presentation colour is never the stored categorical identity or a material mask. GEN-004 schema-3 recipes may populate selected `spatial` geometry inputs from [immutable semantic route/feature exports](procedural-hierarchical-generation.md). The planner resolves those names before the typed compiler runs. Each export is one actual polyline or feature boundary; separate routes are never joined by invented segments. Fields retain no dependency on grammar types, live World state or partially rasterized neighboring cells. GEN-004 also reuses this finite assignment solver for declared district themes. The Workbench writes JSON with full floating-point precision. External GDScript authors should use `JSON.stringify(recipe, " ", true, true)` so the `full_precision` argument preserves accepted double values and the compiled `spatial_fingerprint`; default JSON formatting can round them. Category strings remain exact independently of that numeric formatting. Reapplying an accepted recipe intentionally advances the adapter revision and recipe fingerprint; unchanged spatial content retains its separate graph fingerprint. Only `normalized` spatial outputs may feed existing application/exclusion, aggregate variation and parameter-mapping controls. Authors must add an explicit `to_mask` conversion for signed scalars or booleans. A category can first be compared with `equal`, then explicitly converted. The initial proposal context, modifier order, restored route skeleton and final hard-material authority remain owned by the retained [field/modifier contract](procedural-generation-fields-and-modifiers.md). Executable profiles under [`examples/worldgen`](../../examples/worldgen) cover transformed industrial structure, vector-guided utilities, exact categorical districts, reusable decay masks and multiscale feature seeds. This is minimal authoring/inspection support for the native implementation; GEN-007 owns the full visual editor and content-quality tools. GEN-004 owns hierarchical places, GEN-005 semantic depth and GEN-006 persistent runtime streaming/reconciliation.

Section: Semantic four-plane generation and bounded interlayer contracts > How are planes projected and rasterized?
A plane policy declares its uncovered material, rate, whether play consumes the existing generator, and an explanation of intentionally empty space. Only play may use `base_generator`. A projection template selects an authored grammar rule or `$region`, chooses a plane, and references `feature` or `routes` geometry. Feature projections use the canonical rectangle, or an explicitly contained feature-relative rectangle. Route projections reuse a region's actual passage, service or liquid polyline and its width; an override must remain bounded. `fill` paints the selected geometry. `shell` uses explicit wall/interior material and thickness. `omit` preserves an explicit composition decision and reason. Material overrides use ordinary valid native IDs; material 10 remains invalid. Density is a deterministic feature/coordinate mask in absolute world space. Optional `application` and `exclusion` reference the same immutable GEN-003 graph as `spatial:<expanded.id>`. Only dimensionless normalized or boolean outputs are admitted; raw scalar, distance, vector and category outputs need an explicit typed conversion. Effective density is `density * application * (1 - exclusion)`, with absent masks equal to one/zero. The shared graph is evaluated once per affected plane and coordinate, charged to raster work, and its transitive input identity is retained in projection revisions. Both examples share a weathering field between rear and far geometry. Ascending priority and stable projection ID determine raster precedence. Final play hard-material overrides remain final. An authored empty passage projection can deliberately carve the semantic route through decorative geometry. Every region needs explicit atmosphere and far-plane projection records, even when the intended composition is empty. Per-feature omissions are not runtime permissions. Static appearance is produced by the existing material renderer, not by generated bitmap textures or a second material catalogue. Parallax, pan, zoom and visibility live only in `CyberDepthCompositor`. They are absent from native schema input, seed selection, ownership and hashes. Admission translates absolute semantic coordinates into the local finite World only once; all retained IDs and geometry still refer to the absolute plan.

Section: Hierarchical procedural places and structural routes > What is implemented, and what stays separate?
**Current source, GEN-004 / [#191](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/191):** opt-in recipe schema **3**, generator algorithm **4**, adds a grammar with its own schema **1** and algorithm **1**. The [native semantic API](../../native/include/cybersand/generation_grammar.hpp) and [planner](../../native/src/generation_grammar.cpp) compile complete immutable places before the existing generator rasterizes material proposals. Schema-1/2 recipes retain their previous algorithms and material behavior when grammar is absent. Runtime acceptance remains separately recorded in the [dated audit](../audits/2026-10-21-gen004-hierarchical-generation.md). A hierarchy may contain region, district, complex, room, apparatus and detail features. The authored namespace represents the world; kinds are descriptive, while parent/child references define nesting. Recipes can skip levels or use multiple district scopes for theme subdivisions. Each feature carries its exact identity, parent/children, canonical owner, absolute half-open rectangle, selected rule and candidate, tags, normalized theme blend, typed parameters, allowed materials, sockets, constraints, seed, content revision and finite-curve order. This version uses axis-aligned integer rectangles and explicit rectilinear routes. It does not claim arbitrary implicit solids or a general-purpose architectural packing solver. Semantic planning has no World pointer, resident-neighbor read, shared mutable random stream or Godot callback. GEN-003 fields consume explicitly exported immutable geometry; they do not depend on grammar types or partially rasterized neighbors. Material proposal publication, native World admission and presentation remain separate owners. The planner does not evict chunks, reconcile player edits, run simulation or complete persistent streaming. [GEN-005 semantic planes](procedural-semantic-planes.md) now compose this immutable hierarchy for finite four-plane projection. GEN-007 owns the full authoring/quality editor, and GEN-006 streaming and reconciliation.

Section: Typed spatial fields, transforms and reusable generation graphs > How do immutable routes and finite region assignments work?
Geometry inputs contain an ID, 1..256 finite points and a `closed` flag; a closed boundary requires at least three points. `geometry_distance` names one immutable input and returns Euclidean distance to its point, open polyline segments or closed boundary. Closed geometry measures the boundary; it does not silently become an inside/outside classifier. A single point and repeated points have bounded explicit segment handling. Geometry is copied/prepared before publication, and its actual coordinates enter the consuming node's identity. GEN-004 can supply routes and feature boundaries through this value interface without a dependency from fields into the future grammar implementation. An assignment input declares a finite tile of at most 16×16 cells, up to 16 exact categories, four directional adjacency masks and optional per-cell domain masks. Opposite adjacency relations must be reciprocal. Deterministic propagation and bounded backtracking prepare the entire solution before a field can sample it. Unsatisfiable constraints and exhausted work are distinct explicit failures; neither exposes a partial assignment. `assigned_region` returns one exact category from the prepared tile. The tile repeats using floor addressing. `wrap_x`/`wrap_y` enable constraints across those tile edges; without a wrap constraint, adjacency is guaranteed only inside the finite tile. GEN-004 owns hierarchical layout use of this contract and should reuse this solver rather than introducing a conflicting field solver.

Section: Hierarchical procedural places and structural routes > What are the work, memory and failure bounds?
The [configuration reference](../reference/configuration-reference.md#hierarchical-generation-limits) owns exact defaults and hard maxima. The planner bounds region count, rules, hierarchy depth, children, candidates, feature/socket/route records, spatial queries, solver work, prepared bytes and raster verification size/work, including support-contact scans and retained reports. Logical work measures conservative declared work rather than wall-clock time or machine instructions. Compiling a requested window and validating its final raster are separate bounded operations. Low work/memory limits, malformed input, failed attachment, solver exhaustion, cancellation and raster-budget rejection must expose actionable errors and no partial published plan, cells or diagnostics. Final blocked-route reports preserve the complete authored material proposal; that is a reported content conflict rather than partial publication.

Section: ADR-013: Canonical semantic generation before rasterization > Why this boundary?
Request-order ownership would make neighboring chunks disagree when produced independently. A mutable shared global plan would add synchronization, lifetime and streaming obligations before the programme's streaming stage. Recursive neighbor planning would lack a finite dependency footprint. Canonical regions and shared boundary records provide independently reproducible discovery while keeping the plan's work and memory finite. Semantic identity and content receipts answer different questions. The former identifies a place across unrelated edits; the latter detects changed geometry, material or constraints. Declaration order and recipe revisions therefore do not rename surviving places. Changing the region grid explicitly changes the identity namespace instead of silently moving an old place to a new owner. Curve order supplies a repeatable structural sequence. It cannot certify a physical path, especially for Morton jumps or repeated finite tiles. Routes use explicit rectilinear geometry and compatible sockets. Final raster validation then checks Empty-cell clearance/connectivity for the declared floating square profile, including independently authored shared apertures. Final support qualification separately checks retained solid contact along declared floor/ceiling/wall edges, with partial-contact diagnostics. Neither profile claims post-simulation structural stability or controller performance.

Section: Hierarchical procedural places and structural routes > How do I author and inspect the multi-district example?
Load [`hierarchy-multi-district.json`](../../examples/worldgen/hierarchy-multi-district.json) through the Workbench hierarchy example control or `CyberWorldGenerator.configure`. It covers `[-128,-128,256,256]` cells in four canonical 128-cell regions, using 64-cell storage chunks. Each region contains semantic theme subdivisions, one 104×72 foundry, a 64×66 gallery, a machinery bay, an inspection dais with floor and wall constraints, a floor-mounted pump, a ceiling console and two embedded dais lights. The machinery bay occupies 22.22% of its foundry. Neighbor, separation, service, exact multiplicity, socket and occupancy constraints are authored data. The profile uses the shared finite assignment solver for district theme blends, order-1 Hilbert-ranked foundry candidates and detail placement, a real theme-boundary preference for a marker, explicit primary routes and secondary loops, a four-site curve-ordered service tour and straight service/liquid trunks, a prepared vault module, a weathered aggregate shell and a typed distance mask around an exported tour loop. Its Strata base is composed with Flow Network and District Grammar overrides. `get_semantic_plan()` exposes the hierarchy and receipts; `inspect_cell()` reports contribution provenance; `validate_routes()` reports the declared final-cell traversal and support-contact qualifications separately. The example deliberately places its compact apparatus away from both semantic passage footprints and the existing candidate macro network for the authored seed. Its retained qualification and the footprint inspection are recorded in the [dated audit](../audits/2026-10-21-gen004-hierarchical-generation.md). For a new place, choose its canonical region/window and stable rule IDs first. Declare parent-relative candidate rectangles and exact counts, then add hard requirements and socket apertures. Give higher-priority scopes to required supports or theme areas. Add preferences only after a valid hard layout exists. Use explicit omission fallback only when absence is an acceptable authored outcome. Inspect semantic receipts before tuning masks/materials, then recheck final raster routes after any hard override. Save accepted JSON with full numeric precision using the existing Workbench configuration path. [`grammar-v1.schema.json`](../../examples/worldgen/schemas/grammar-v1.schema.json) is the versioned JSON authoring schema for the `grammar` member of a schema-3 recipe. The native compiler additionally checks relational, geometric, type, cycle, work and memory invariants that JSON Schema cannot establish. The [build guide](../operations/local-build-and-validation.md#hierarchical-generation-example-and-acceptance) routes executable tests. Human movement feel, Windows/browser behavior and render throughput require their own dated execution evidence.

graph, geometry and prepared region assignment | Immutable `generation::SpatialGraph`; copied typed parameters, routes and bounded complete solver results | No per-cell context or mutable World access; transforms and derivatives resample absolute-coordinate functions | | Semantic hierarchy, sockets, routes and constraint receipts | Immutable `generation::GrammarPlan`, prepared before rasterization for a finite world-anchored region window | Stable owner/rule/slot identities are separate from recipe revisions; pending bytes stay private, failure/cancel discards both payloads | | World-generation workbench previews | One main-thread `CyberWorldGenerator` owner plus copied material/texture cache | Accepted recipe changes retire old preview work; Section: Interfaces and message contracts > Current public surfaces > Native semantic plans and copied hierarchy inspection
**Current schema-3 / GEN-004 extension:** `Recipe::grammar` is a versioned `GrammarDefinition`. `GrammarPlan::compile(definition, seed)` returns immutable features, sockets, routes and constraint receipts, with finite `bounds()`, `fingerprint()`, work/storage metadata, ID lookup, bounded rectangle `query()` and `ancestry()` APIs. Feature IDs include the world namespace, region grid size, signed region address, parent path, rule ID and stable numeric slot. Content revision, recipe revision and receipt identity are separate values. `Generator::semantic_plan()` exposes the const plan. `validate_routes()` returns the complete retained report for final material cells and the declared odd square clearance profile. `RouteValidation::passed` records the aggregate required-route result; `supports_passed` independently records final solid contact for declared floor/ceiling/wall constraints. The named profiles are `floating-square-v1` and `static-solid-contact-v1`. `SupportOutcome` carries `feature_id`, `constraint`, `passed`, `checked_cells`, `missing_cells`, `first_missing_x/y` and `detail`. One surviving contact suffices for a support check; the wall check scans both vertical sides. The report records success/failure per required explicit route; intentional final hard material blockers remain in the material output and fail their route checks. `explain(x,y)` returns a bounded `CellProvenance` value with final material, semantic ancestry, constraint receipts, stage contributions and scalar/typed field values. Native query pointers borrow only their immutable plan, so callers must retain that plan's lifetime. Godot adds `get_semantic_plan()`, `inspect_cell(Vector2i)` and `validate_routes()` to the separate `CyberWorldGenerator`. They return copied dictionaries/arrays; no live World or feature pointer crosses the adapter. The copied report includes `support_profile`, `supports_passed` and a `supports` array using those same outcome fields. `configure` includes this report for accepted grammar recipes, while `get_configuration` preserves the authored `grammar` declaration. The grammar's `district_assignment` wraps GEN-003 `specification` and optional `limits`, and `district_themes` uses exact 16-digit lowercase hexadecimal keys. Typed feature parameters use the existing `SpatialValue` JSON encoding. Unknown fields and malformed inputs reject transactionally, preserving the previous configuration. The [hierarchy contract](../systems/procedural-hierarchical-generation.md) and [grammar JSON schema](../../examples/worldgen/schemas/grammar-v1.schema.json) own exact semantic meaning and relational checks.

Section: Hierarchical procedural places and structural routes > Which edits preserve semantic identity?
A region ID is `<world>/grid<size>/region(<x>,<y>)`. Each authored feature extends its parent with `/<rule-id>/<slot>`, where slots are stable integers from zero through `count-1`. For example: ```text four-foundries/grid128/region(0,0)/district/0/foundry/0/machinery/0/pump/0 ``` The feature seed derives from the world seed and this exact string. Array position, planning-window extent, recipe revision and receipt hash are excluded from identity. Reordering rules, candidates, children, tags or theme entries does not rename features. Adding an unrelated rule does not renumber existing slots. Competition may legitimately change a surviving feature's chosen bounds or candidate while its identity remains stable; its content revision records that change. Renaming a world/rule, changing a parent path or reducing/removing its stable slot intentionally removes or replaces identities. Changing `region_size` changes the grid namespace and deliberately replaces regional identities; existing resident content is never automatically reconciled. Material, parameters, constraint and geometry edits affect revision/plan receipts rather than becoming new semantic names. The whole compiled plan fingerprint also binds the selected window and configuration. It is a different object from a feature ID.

Section: Hierarchical procedural places and structural routes > How does a semantic plan become material cells?
The base Strata, Flow Network and District Grammar candidates, existing brush controls, native modules, scalar/typed fields and aggregates remain available. Semantic feature proposals supply bounded shell/interior material and optional aggregate/application/exclusion references. Named field references use the retained normalized mask contract; general scalar, vector and category values must first convert explicitly. The final semantic route carve is applied before final hard material overrides, which retain their existing authority. `geometry_exports` maps at most sixteen aliases to exact semantic route or feature IDs. A route export contains that route's actual ordered points; a feature export contains its rectangular boundary. The alias is the immutable geometry name consumed by a GEN-003 `geometry_distance` node. Separate routes are never concatenated into fictitious joining segments. Exports are validated before typed graph compilation; changing geometry changes graph identity. Inspection exports complete ancestry, rule/candidate choice, constraint and fallback receipts, socket matching, geometry inputs and material decisions. Copied semantic/cell data belongs to the caller, with no borrowed World storage. Section: Hierarchical procedural places and structural routes > How does a semantic plan become material cells? > What does floating-square route validation prove after a hard override?
`validate_routes()` checks **final rasterized cells**, after fields, modules, aggregates and hard overrides, for an explicitly declared odd square clearance. This is the `floating-square-v1` geometric profile with four-neighbor connectivity. At the finite window edge, footprint checks are clipped to the canonical shared aperture; the report explicitly sets `boundary_apertures`. Independently planned opposite halves complete that aperture, and stitched boundary controls are required to establish the full crossing. It does not model gravity, jumps, a particular articulated actor, controllers or material motion after simulation. An authored hard override can intentionally block a required route: material output preserves the override and the route report records failure. A blocked report must not be described as successful traversal. No abstract graph result substitutes for this final-cell check. For a semantic-plane recipe, additional projections can subsequently change material. The [GEN-007 qualification oracle](../operations/procedural-qualification.md#how-are-routes-checked-after-all-material-decisions) therefore checks the final projected play plane independently, with the same distinction between geometric clearance and actor traversal. The same report separately exposes `supports_passed` for the `static-solid-contact-v1` profile. For each declared floor, ceiling or wall constraint it inspects final material cells immediately outside the feature's rectangle. A check passes when at least one inspected cell has `MaterialState::Solid`; the wall check inspects both vertical sides. It retains checked/missing counts, the first missing coordinate and the feature/constraint identity. Partial contact can therefore pass, and `passed` still means the route profile alone. A consumer requiring both qualifications must inspect both booleans. This catches total removal of a required support by routes, modules, modifiers or final overrides. It does not establish that the whole apparatus survived, that its support spans the entire footprint, that the solid is itself grounded, or that the resulting assembly remains stable after simulation. Cell provenance and fixture-specific raster controls are needed for those stronger claims.

Section: Hierarchical procedural places and structural routes > How are hard constraints and preferences resolved?
Rules under one parent run in descending priority, with lexical rule ID breaking ties. A rule requests an exact `count`; each slot considers distinct authored candidate rectangles relative to the parent. Candidates rank by weighted preference score, then finite-curve rank, then candidate ID. Hard constraints filter this ordered list. Candidate rejection reasons are retained. This is a bounded, deterministic priority placement strategy: a feasible arrangement that would require moving an earlier high-priority placement may be rejected. There is no claim of complete search over all possible layouts. | Declaration | Exact semantic check | |---|---| | `intersects_route` | Candidate intersects an explicit regional passage footprint. Curve succession does not satisfy it. | | `minimum_separation` | Euclidean distance between sibling rectangle extents is at least the greater of their two requested separations. | | `floor`, `ceiling`, `wall` | Candidate contacts the corresponding declared solid parent interior surface or a previously placed solid sibling surface. A separate final-cell report checks whether a solid contact survives rasterization; neither check models stability after simulation. | | `open_volume` | Candidate fits inside a shelled parent's interior and does not overlap a sibling for which either side requires open volume. Ancestors are not competing siblings. | | `service` | A declared `service` or `liquid` route lies within `neighbor_distance` of the candidate rectangle. This is bounded geometric access, not liquid dynamics. | | `occupancy_min/max` | Sum of this rule's placed sibling rectangle areas divided by parent rectangle area falls in the inclusive range. It is a semantic area quota, distinct from aggregate material weights. | | `count` | Exactly this many stable slots are placed per parent unless an authored omission fallback records an exception. Candidate IDs are not reused within the same rule instance. | | `required_neighbors`, `forbidden_neighbors` | Named sibling tags are present/absent within `neighbor_distance`; final checks see all siblings, including later declarations. | | `exclusive_family` | At most one placed sibling occupies the named family. | | `minimum_sockets`, `maximum_sockets`, `connected` | Counts stay within the declared range; connected features have a compatible attached passage socket. Required socket matches are mechanically checked. | | `allowed_materials` | Declared shell/interior and integrated aggregate contributions must obey the feature's declared material set; an empty set imposes no feature-local material filter. Final hard overrides retain their separate authority. | Preferences are weighted, finite scores for closeness to a route, parent floor, ceiling or wall, a boundary between two selected semantic sibling themes, or progressive finite-curve density. Theme-boundary scoring uses already established sibling feature geometry and theme records; use higher-priority

Section: Procedural generation fields and masked modifiers > Which context is available to guidance and sculpting?
The generator first resolves the original theme selection, old polyline brushes and hard parameter/candidate overrides, then rasterizes that initial candidate. It captures context at this point, before field-guided changes, structural modules, material/aggregate modifiers, connective carving, explicit paths or hard material overrides. All fields and modifier predicates for the cell see this same capture. | Channel | Initial proposal meaning | |---|---| | `occupied` | 1 for any non-Empty material, otherwise 0 | | `solid` | 1 only for the existing `MaterialState::Solid`; Powder is occupied but not solid | | `fluid` | 1 only for the existing `MaterialState::Liquid` | | `material` | Exact existing material ID, consumed by a `material` field or predicate | | `depth` | Downward-positive `y - surface(x)` using the original Strata surface formula | | `slope` | Absolute surface-height difference across x−1/x+1, divided by two; one-sided at the admitted coordinate boundary | | `route` | Binary initial shared-network membership for Flow Network/District Grammar; zero for Strata | The analytic surface uses the original effective `surface_y` and `relief`, even when the candidate is District Grammar. Slope recomputes the original theme, brush and hard-parameter state at each neighboring surface sample. Consequently an authored height brush can contribute slope even with zero noise relief. It does not read neighboring material occupancy or recursively evaluate fields. A modifier's `context` predicate is `any`, `empty`, `occupied`, `solid`, `fluid` or `material`; only the last requires `context_material`. For example, an occupied-only carving modifier can remove initial terrain without a later empty-only modifier treating that new hole as initially empty. Material added by a module does not retroactively change a field mask. This fixed observation point prevents order-dependent context feedback and keeps cross-chunk sampling local. The standalone graph accepts a copied `FieldContext` from a native caller. Binary channels must be finite in `[0,1]`; material IDs must exist; absolute depth and nonnegative slope are bounded by `2 * 2^40`. That value interface is not a live World-query hook. A future adapter supplying live observations would need its own immutable snapshot, revision and scheduling contract.

Section: Procedural world generation candidates > What is the control precedence?
The evaluation order is stable and independent of manifest array insertion order. IDs are required; duplicate IDs within a layer are rejected. For brushes, paths, modifiers and hard overrides, lower `priority` runs first, with lexical ID as the tie-break. Later values win. Moving an item in a JSON array is not a hidden priority control. | Order | Control | Meaning | |---|---|---| | 1 | Global parameters and resolved theme parameters | Establish the selected candidate's initial shape and palette distribution | | 2 | Broad polyline brushstrokes | Blend theme weights and selected shape parameters using radius, strength and falloff | | 3 | Hard parameter/candidate overrides | Assign exact values within a half-open world-space rectangle | | 4 | Initial raster and context | Capture the original proposed material, surface and route context before later changes | | 5 | Scalar fields and modifier influence | Evaluate the field DAG once and capture each modifier's application/exclusion/context/shape mask | | 6 | Masked theme and geometry guidance | Apply all theme blends; reblend theme/old brush parameters; apply direct edits and mappings; reapply hard geometry controls and rasterize | | 7 | Prepared feature modules | Add or carve structured zones in dependency order, clipped to bounds and optional field masks | | 8 | Masked material or aggregate modifiers | Use the original captured influence to select discrete existing material IDs | | 9 | Shared network and explicit guide paths | Reserve connective space after modules/modifiers; a guide may carve Empty or paint another material | | 10 | Hard material overrides | Force the final material, including intentionally blocking a route | Schema 3 inserts accepted semantic shell/interior/aggregate proposals between steps 6 and 7 and restores explicit semantic passages after step 9. Existing native modules and material modifiers can therefore contribute to semantic places, while final hard material overrides still win. The hierarchy's final-cell route report observes that complete stack and reports any blocked passage; it does not reinterpret a hard override as optional. Recipes without grammar retain the table's preceding behavior. The [field/modifier contract](procedural-generation-fields-and-modifiers.md) defines the two guidance stages, mapping endpoints and immutable context. No earlier modifier can change the context observed by a later modifier. Recipes without new controls retain their old material behavior; fixed legacy hashes cover all three candidates in four signed chunks. Brush points are world-space `[x,y]` pairs. A single point is a dab; multiple points form a polyline. Influence uses distance to the nearest segment, a smooth radial falloff raised

Section: Semantic four-plane generation and bounded interlayer contracts > What does GEN-005 implement?
**Current source / [#192](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/192):** `PlanePlan` compiles one existing GEN-004 hierarchy into four coherent material proposals and copied feature, projection, fixture and link records. Its native API is [generation_planes.hpp](../../native/include/cybersand/generation_planes.hpp); its compiler is [generation_planes.cpp](../../native/src/generation_planes.cpp). The optional `semantic_planes` member of a schema-3 recipe has its own schema 1 and algorithm 1. It does not renumber the retained GEN-001/002/003/004 schemas. A canonical feature owns every projection. The compiler uses the same stable feature IDs, parent hierarchy, seeds, absolute rectangles, named structural routes and material intent on all planes. It cannot generate four unrelated layouts and subsequently label them as one place. The geometry reference in each projection points to the actual feature or canonical route it sampled. | Role | Plane | Source and authority | |---|---|---| | Play | `play` | Existing generator proposal or authored semantic projections; material collision and admitted actor placements belong to this plane. | | Rear | `scripted` | Shared shells, service geometry and machinery interiors, plus finite independently clocked native reagents. | | Atmosphere | `effects` | Explicit empty-space policy, bounded gas/particle projections and finite sources/drains. | | Far | `background` | Shared silhouettes and architectural masses in a frozen native World. | The opt-in [semantic depth scene](../../godot/semantic_depth.tscn) and [owner](../../godot/scripts/depth/semantic_plane_runtime.gd) demonstrate the contract. The ordinary asynchronous sandbox, material kernels, Rapier backend, physics clocks and retained depth comparison hosts keep their existing owners. Section: Semantic four-plane generation and bounded interlayer contracts > Where is atomic admission enforced?
The native compiler validates the complete bounded plan before returning it. A `PlaneGenerationJob` privately stages all four material arrays. `advance` respects its cell slice; Pending, Cancelled and Failed jobs expose no partial material publication. Ready results bind the plan fingerprint, revision, bounds, content hashes and registration receipt. Stale or modified native results fail `accepts`. The adapter copies output and compresses nonempty row runs into vertically merged local rectangles before handing over a full bundle. `CyberWorldGenerator.configure` prepares a candidate generator and plane plan before replacing its previous configuration. The authored plane revision is separate from the adapter's monotonic request serial, so an identical authored configuration retains the same semantic bundle identity. Changing configuration retires pending adapter jobs; a rejected configuration preserves them and the last valid configuration. `CyberSemanticPlaneRuntime.install_bundle` validates copied geometry, materials, metadata, fixtures, links, budgets and any actor proposals before replacement. The inherited depth owner constructs all four candidate native Worlds privately. Only a successful complete preparation publishes the new set and its registries, synchronously at one owner boundary. No renderer can obtain a mixed feature revision from the middle of that operation. Failed admission retains the previous Worlds, clocks, publications, registries and generation. A differing replacement after initial admission needs the expected current owner generation. The finite retired-revision ledger rejects an old bundle resubmission. It has an explicit capacity outcome rather than silently evicting history and reopening a stale-admission path. Existing per-plane packet identity, monotonic serial, independent clocks, failed-world quarantine and frozen background caching still apply.

Section: Semantic four-plane generation and bounded interlayer contracts > How do finite fixtures own native reactions?
A fixture belongs to one semantic feature and one dynamic plane. Its declaration names an ordinary material, contained bounds, mode, target clock, first tick, period, finite positive repeat count and optional cleanup tick. `setup` is once at tick zero; `source` and `drain` start after installation. A drain writes Empty. Cleanup must follow the last scheduled application. Expected products are copied diagnostic expectations; the source programme never paints them. The refinery and cavern use native Salt/Water fixtures. Rear Water transport and Brine production are observed after ordinary native ticks; expected Brine is not an authoring material in those fixtures. Separate Water/spray and vent/drain programmes demonstrate the other responsibilities. The complete authored set is accounted by fixture ID and application count. Tests retain controls with programmes inactive or reaction partners absent, and require every helper/section to complete; zero exit with a script error is a failure. The owner retains bounded install, activate, reset and retire receipts for fixtures and links. An identical validated bundle retry is idempotent: it neither resets clocks nor duplicates a source or replays setup. A conflicting payload with the same identity/revision rejects. A deliberate whole-bundle reset creates a new generation and permits a new setup in those new Worlds. Retirement blocks future application, invalidates issued link observations and preserves its last receipt. Completed finite feeds remain spent unless the owner explicitly resets. Fixture ownership is assigned by the canonical semantic region. The request tile containing the record's canonical anchor carries its registration ID. Reordered independently requested tiles therefore produce exactly one union of registrations without needing the owner chunk to be resident first. The current host installs complete regions only; per-tile records are data for GEN-007/006, not authorization for partial live replacement.

Section: ADR-014 Single semantic place and atomic four-plane admission > Decision
Compile one immutable semantic plane plan from the existing hierarchy. Projection records reference canonical feature or route geometry. Typed links are static, presentation or narrowly permitted runtime routes. Fixtures declare finite material feeds and cleanup; existing native rules own reaction products. Keep generated arrays private until all four are Ready. Copy and validate the complete bundle at the owner boundary, construct all candidate Worlds before replacing the active set, and publish matching feature revisions in one synchronous commit. Preserve the last valid set on any admission failure. Runtime routes consume owner-issued, copied, identity-bound observations with bounded effects and one-use serials. A static background reference cannot grant runtime write authority. Actor proposals are play-only values consumed through an existing actor session. Generation workers cannot instantiate physics bodies.

[GEN-007](../systems/generation-workbench-2.md) adds `inspect_generation(position, plane, expected_revision, expected_fingerprint)` to `CyberWorldGenerator`. Workbench comparison binds the same seed and coordinates for both recipes and rejects stale result serials. `adopt_configuration(prepared_owner, expected_revision)` transfers immutable plans only after the caller has joined the private preparation worker. It rejects null, self, unconfigured, pending or stale owners. The receiving adapter serial advances; the native recipe revision and its material/diagnostic receipt remain unchanged and are reported separately. Section: Semantic four-plane generation and bounded interlayer contracts > Which semantic links are allowed?
Every link has a stable ID, adapter/template ID, source and target feature IDs, planes, classification, permitted effect, bounded target rectangle, material, parameters, revision and lifecycle. Endpoints must exist and have a non-omitted projection on the named plane. Target rule selection is local to the source's canonical region and must resolve unambiguously. | Family | Classification | Admitted meaning | |---|---|---| | `explosion` | Runtime | `play → scripted`, `blast`, Fire, bounded disc inside the declared rear damage zone. | | `vent` | Static | Play/rear vent or drain corresponds to a named effects source/drain fixture. | | `vent` | Runtime | `scripted → effects`, `burst`, admitted effects material and bounded disc. | | `window` | Presentation | `play → background`, `visibility` composition region. No background mutation permission. | | `pipe` | Static | `play → scripted`, `correspondence` between projections of declared pipe/service geometry. | | `waterfall` | Static | Play Water source plus a named effects spray source in the target zone. | | `machinery` | Static | Play material collision/interaction geometry and corresponding rear fixture/shell. | Static means generation/registration correspondence. Presentation means copied composition metadata. Runtime means an explicit owner-mediated command route. Those classes are validated separately; a link cannot gain runtime authority by changing a label. Unsupported families, reversed routes, arbitrary cross-plane writes, runtime background writes and mismatched fixture references reject. The host issues a copied observation for an installed runtime link. A command must match its bundle/reset generation, link revision, endpoint revisions, source plane/tick and one-use observation serial. Only the permitted center and radius may vary, within the registered zone and maximum radius. The existing owner enqueues and applies the approved blast/burst. Pixel overlap and ordinary native reactions never issue events. A consumer must explicitly request and submit an observation; the examples' event controls exercise that path.

Section: Authoring and inspecting coherent semantic depth scenes > Make reagents finite and products observable
Specify a stable fixture ID, feature rule, dynamic plane, feature-relative rectangle, ordinary material and finite tick schedule. Use one-time `setup` only at tick zero, and use positive start ticks for source/drain programmes. Repeat is strictly positive and finite. A cleanup tick must follow the final feed. Section: Generation Workbench 2 inspection and transactional authoring > Why is this cell or feature here?
`CyberWorldGenerator.inspect_generation(position, plane, expected_revision, expected_fingerprint)` rejects requests that no longer identify its accepted configuration. It returns **deterministic on-demand replay** from the immutable accepted generator, not a stored historical execution trace. The result includes absolute coordinates, plane, recipe/algorithm identity, proposal identity and the native material. The workbench separately checks available copied preview material and identifies its receipt. Uncached material is reported as unavailable for that readback comparison, rather than being invented from its colour. The native sampler records the initial candidate, initial material/context, effective parameters, actual scalar and typed field values, masks and exclusions, context predicate outcomes, ordered modifiers, selection draws and realized aggregate weights/material. Semantic detail identifies the accepted feature, ancestry, producing rule, constraints, sockets and routes. Plane replay records policy, base generator, ordered projections, masks, material contributors, associated fixture/link metadata and final hard override precedence. Rejected decisions and unavailable information are explicit. Trace collections are bounded; `truncated`, `omitted_entries` and the declared collection limit distinguish incomplete detail from a complete explanation. `omitted_entries` counts omissions from native per-cell trace collections; separately bounded semantic metadata also sets `truncated`, without adding those omissions to that counter. Do not read the counter as a total for every array. The UI imposes an additional serialized trace limit. Ordinary generation stores no complete per-cell event log. Replay cannot observe subsequent simulation, claim that a fixture has already produced its expected products, or recover an unrecorded historical decision. Fixture expectations and execution receipts have different owners. The native implementation lives in [world_generation.cpp](../../native/src/world_generation.cpp), [generation_planes.cpp](../../native/src/generation_planes.cpp) and the [Godot adapter](../../godot/native_extension/cyber_world_generator.hpp). The public older `inspect_cell` and `inspect_plane_cell` routes remain available; the unified method adds caller-supplied identity validation.

Section: Generation Workbench 2 inspection and transactional authoring > How do visual authoring and JSON roundtrip?
The graph canvas displays typed spatial nodes and retained scalar fields with ports, native types/units and declared sampling work. Named subgraphs have their own selectable namespace. Node parameters and connections are submitted through the same candidate transaction as other edits; invalid types, dependencies, cycles or capacity fail native validation. Advanced instance bindings and outputs remain in the full Spatial JSON editor. Form edits preserve other supported fields that the selected form does not expose. The hierarchy tree presents accepted native feature IDs and parent relationships. Selecting a feature frames its bounds and replays its provenance. Rule editing changes declarative grammar; plane editing changes policies, projection templates, fixture schedules and links together. The existing brushes compile gestures into bounded strokes, exclusions, paths, modifiers, modules or hard material rectangles. They never paint cached output directly. The diagnostic selector solos scalar masks and typed fields. False colours are presentation of returned values, not an alternative source of field values. Vector arrows and bounded streamlines sample the copied diagnostic grid; missing samples terminate a line. Feature bounds, socket directions and route overlays consume the accepted semantic plan. Route colours qualify the native base generator report; the qualification scene separately checks its final projected play plane. Neither graph clearance nor a green line proves a particular actor's gravity/controller traversal. Feature histograms and density views count actual semantic records. Cost views separate conservative charged work from measured local chunk generation time. Inspection `logical_cost` is the normal generation per-cell bound; it excludes constructing and copying the explanation. Stage `projection_checks` counts examined spatial-index entries, while prepared `spatial_index` counts describe the actual bins and candidates. None is a measured replay CPU duration. The generation-only plane composite combines real plane materials at the same absolute coordinates. The scene's rendered material compositor owns parallax, lighting and actual four-plane graphical qualification.

**Current: no such guarantee.** CYSD1 restores a fixed demo level and selected metadata. Identical re-export proves equality of what the format stores. Section: Generation Workbench 2 inspection and transactional authoring > How do failed edits, undo and redo preserve state?
Interactive edits copy and validate a candidate on one exclusive worker with a private native adapter. At most one worker and one newest pending candidate exist; newer requests retire older serials without blocking the preview. The joined worker transfers its immutable compiled plans through `adopt_configuration`, which checks the receiving revision and increments its adapter serial. Native recipe revision and receipts retain their original identity; adoption does not rewrite them to imitate a new native execution. Scripted `apply_recipe` uses the same preparation and commit boundary synchronously. A bounded material/plane preflight catches exhausted generation budgets before the accepted recipe changes. Invalid JSON, native rejection or an exhausted budget preserves the accepted recipe, preview, pending preview job and undo/redo stacks. Draft text may remain invalid for correction. Cancellation invalidates the request immediately; already-running bounded preparation may finish privately and its result is discarded. Closing the scene joins its owned workers before releasing them. Only a successful commit pushes canonical recipe content into bounded history. Graph, rule, parameter, plane and brush edits all use this boundary. Undo/redo restores canonical recipe content and deterministic material/semantic output, while configuration receives a fresh adapter revision and UI session token. Those fresh identities prevent old asynchronous results from re-entering merely because the recipe content matches an earlier version. Recipe acceptance retires old jobs, cache entries, traces and comparison results. View changes have their own token. Preview admission checks the expected chunk, extent, revision, fingerprint, plane/stage and copied payload shape. Auxiliary jobs carry their request serial and recipe session. Cancellation publishes no partial seed or comparison data. Trace admission checks its captured token again. These are finite authoring transactions. They do not rebase player edits into new generation or replace an active gameplay World's ownership contract.

Section: Procedural Deepworks qualification and visual review > How are routes checked after all material decisions?
The structural table in issue #193 requires one primary route reaching all major regions, two optional loops and secondary passages. The qualification oracle must sample the **final projected play material**, after all plane projections and final hard overrides. A semantic route record alone cannot prove clearance. The scene's independent clearance check requires a 7 × 7-cell square of final Empty play cells at every tested route center, then checks four-neighbor connectivity. It explicitly reaches all four regions, all eight galleries, the two outboard courtyard loops in Copper/Ember and their secondary connections. A deliberate blocking hard override is a negative control. The graph describes a floating clearance profile; it does not certify that a particular walking, flying or articulated actor can traverse the map. Actor/controller acceptance remains separately scoped. Whole-map and tiled generation agree on every material plane, canonical semantic and projection records, and the normalized union of fixture/link registrations. The retained test uses reverse-order 128-cell tiles for all four seeds, an alternate forward 256-cell partition for the reference seed, four independently configured workers generating 512-cell quadrants, and 31/4096-cell budget slices through a seam. Native worker comparisons qualify scheduling independently of a Godot UI preview. Budget exhaustion rejects the attempted edit while preserving the previously accepted plan.

**Current scene: The Fourfold Works.** [gen007-deepworks.json](../../examples/worldgen/gen007-deepworks.json) describes one 1024 × 1024 total map, projected into play, scripted/rear, effects/atmosphere and frozen background/far. Its native hierarchy owns the districts, galleries, apparatus and architectural details. Reusable rules and plane templates expand that hierarchy. No authored bitmap or per-material-cell listing supplies the map. The retained Linux qualification covers reference seed **19301** and declared variants **19317, 19337 and 19361**. Each contains four major regions, eight named galleries, 24 tagged microfeatures, 14 structures crossing native chunk boundaries, two connected optional loops, and four paired native exhibits: eight independently checked play/rear setups. These are measured fixture quantities, not guarantees for arbitrary seeds or future recipe edits. See the [structural receipts](../audits/gen007/qualification.json) and [capture manifest](../images/gen007/capture-manifest.json). Structural, initial-containment and exact generation-parity checks cover all four seeds. Full native mechanism execution and clock-isolation checks use reference seed 19301; all four seeds have retained rendered comparisons. The [qualification viewer](../../godot/scripts/worldgen_qualification.gd) uses the existing semantic-plane runtime and material compositor. Launch it directly: ```sh godot --path godot res://gen007_qualification.tscn ``` The Workbench 2 graph/tools page can load the same recipe for editing. Its generation preview and the material-rendered scene are distinct views of the same native proposal. The viewer starts from a complete validated bundle; sources and reactions are independently owned by the established dynamic-plane clocks. The [acceptance ledger](../audits/2026-10-21-gen007-workbench-qualification.md) records actual measured counts, all declared seeds, source/runtime identities, timings, memory, retained captures and unresolved requirements. Availability of the recipe or a passing structural count is not visual acceptance.

Each major region contains a corresponding play/rear apparatus. The feed fixtures provide ordinary native reagents; expected-product metadata is never used as painting instructions. Removing the feed or the reaction partner produces none of the claimed product in any apparatus. Fabricated no-op and aborted-helper receipts are rejected. A helper abort or script error invalidates the run even when the process exits zero or other sections report passing assertions. Rear-only execution must leave play and frozen far data unchanged; effects have their own owner and clock. Complete fixture application accounting prevents an unvisited or silently aborted setup from being labelled passed. Finite feeds expire, and explicit reset creates new Worlds and fresh lifecycle identities.

Section: Procedural Deepworks qualification and visual review > How is deliberate composition kept procedural?
Author the major district silhouettes and routes first, then reuse gallery, cabinet and apparatus rules inside those places. Named features and stable IDs make the composition inspectable. Candidate layouts and seeded details supply variation while structural material roles and passage clearance remain explicit. Keep the reference seed and all variant seeds declared in the fixture. Material choices follow the [MAT-002 catalogue](../systems/building-material-catalogue.md): stable structural walls and containment, local metal/glass/service accents, bounded reactive contents and thematic background treatment. A random palette swap does not establish coherent regional identity. Empty air, sightlines and rear windows are intentional composition choices; four-plane treatment does not mean every cell must be nonempty. The recipe report must retain its UTF-8 byte size, reusable rule/template counts, expanded feature counts and manually fixed placements. Authored region bounds, routes and shared apparatus proportions are legitimate declarative design; listing every output material cell is not. Inspect the hierarchy/plane rules in the workbench to determine which choices are fixed and which depend on seed. The current recipe is **61,845 UTF-8 bytes**, with 26 grammar rules and 124 plane templates: 111 projection, eight finite-feed and five link templates. Native expansion produces 161 semantic features and 336 projections. Its [builder](../../tools/worldgen/build_gen007_recipe.py) writes only declarative JSON; the native generator performs feature expansion, seeded candidate selection, route construction and final material rasterization. The [qualification manifest](../../examples/worldgen/gen007-qualification.json) retains the counts and authoring ledger. The manually fixed design consists of four district anchors, two shared gallery definitions, one reused optional-loop definition and four exhibit definitions. The source contains 43 candidate boxes, 83 relative projection rectangles and eight relative fixture rectangles. Native expansion reuses this feature geometry. The baseline has no final hard material overrides. The native route-distance preference selects two of four candidate cabinet sites in each gallery; all four declared seeds produce different actual cabinet layouts and different play/rear material hashes. The far apparatus and sparse effects treatment deliberately retain identical material hashes across these seeds. Reusable definitions include upper/lower galleries, both cabinet arrangements, cabinet windows, gauges, shelves, signals, service rails and optional-loop courts. Optical cores reuse apertures and four braces; vaults reuse locks; every native vessel reuses pilot strips, base feet and inlet posts. The eight galleries each have nonempty treatment and intentional empty cells on all four planes. The structural receipts retain those per-gallery counts for every declared seed.

Section: Procedural Deepworks qualification and visual review > How are cost and performance claims reported?
GEN-007's bounded candidate indices accelerate sampling by identifying nearby grammar features, routes and projections. They preserve canonical record order and still use the original geometry/mask tests. Index creation is charged to preparation work and memory. Conservative logical charges remain explicit and must fit declared recipe limits; the indices do not authorize unbounded output. The recipe declares at most 4,000,000,000 logical operations for a whole four-plane bundle, 16,000,000,000 for generic final-raster validation, 16 MiB of charged plane-plan storage and 64 MiB of publication data. The four qualified seeds fit those limits. Native grammar storage and plane-plan storage are separate charges; neither is process memory. Seed 19337 leaves only about 0.8% of the plane-operation budget despite four unused template slots. New seeds or denser edits can receive an explicit bounded refusal and require fresh qualification. Report actual local generation, validation and preview durations separately from logical units. Include compiler/runtime, OS/CPU, renderer, resolution, seed, worker/slice settings and peak-memory measurement method. A charged-operation heatmap is an estimate; a measured-chunk-time heatmap is local timing at chunk resolution. Neither establishes target-PC performance or per-cell timing. The declared process envelope is **2 GiB for headless qualification/reactions** and **4 GiB for graphical execution**. The original provisional 2 GiB graphical bound failed during cold Mesa rendering and remains a retained failure. The cold/warm difference is consistent with renderer initialization and shader-cache overhead; the measurements do not attribute the peak to a particular allocation. The final canonical software-renderer run uses `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`, `LP_NUM_THREADS=2` and `GALLIVM_PERF=nopt`; its fresh XDG/Mesa-cache peak fits the revised 4 GiB envelope. Cold and warm timing/RSS records, Godot static allocation peak, native charged storage and their different scopes are retained in the [audit](../audits/2026-10-21-gen007-workbench-qualification.md) and [raw evidence directory](../audits/gen007/). The Linux process wrapper records the maximum child/descendant RSS, not aggregate simultaneous process-tree memory.

Section: Generation Workbench 2 inspection and transactional authoring > How do seed and before/after comparisons work?
Seed cards run the same accepted declarative recipe at one to four explicitly entered portable integer seeds. Each job owns a private native generator and advances under a cell slice. Results are bounded to a 128 × 128 rectangle per plane. Cards display the seed, measured preparation/generation time and charged logical work alongside the four images. The retained result also identifies its bounds; the cards do not expose a material hash. The browser does not imply full-map qualification for an untested seed. Pinning stores a canonical recipe and rectangle. A later comparison uses that rectangle and the **same current seed for both recipes**, so it isolates recipe changes. Material differences are exact cell counts/masks. Semantic differences compare stable IDs and copied records, reporting additions, removals and changed records. Semantic record admission is bounded to 4,096 records, with explicit truncation above that limit; addition/removal/change counts cover the retained records, not an unbounded plan. Detailed change lists have their own smaller cap, separate from those retained-record counts. Introduced/removed planes without aligned data are labelled unavailable. The comparison buffer, seed queue, trace size, graph canvas, preview cache and streamlines are explicitly bounded by the [configuration reference](../reference/configuration-reference.md#generation-workbench-2-limits). Measured timings include the reported local scope and environment. Logical charges and sampled visual density are not target-hardware performance claims.

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > What comparisons would establish useful behavior?
Record a comparison manifest before interpreting a score. At minimum it should identify the source/runtime and rig capabilities, arena layout and material configuration, actor counts, actuation/assist lane, observation profile, decision and message schedules, controller/checkpoint, training privileges, seed policy, time limit and scoring rules. Distinguish these evaluation classes: | Evaluation tag | Intended interpretation | |---|---| | `matched` | Equal rig, lane and observation profile with scripted cadence; humans are rejected. Further resource/compute matching still needs an experiment manifest | | `asymmetric` | Declared information, actuation, population or compute differences | | `oracle_reference` | Declared oracle privilege; no optimal-play claim | | `mechanics` | Mechanism, capacity or timing demonstration; not a policy ranking | Use paired map/initial-state seeds, exchange sides or spawn locations, retain failed runs and report variation across episodes. A single arena win is an example, not a statistically supported policy ranking. A stronger aggregate force is not necessarily a more efficient actor policy. For density experiments report both actor count per free arena area and a stated body-footprint measure. More actors at fixed area also adds action opportunities, energy and tag capacity. Smaller areas at fixed count change travel distance and confinement. Preserve those distinctions when interpreting the result. Useful ablations include fixed-area count sweeps, fixed-count area sweeps, constant-density population/area scaling, terrain edits enabled versus disabled, independent random streams versus correlated inputs, and nearby coordination enabled versus disabled under a matched budget. Geometry and passability changes must be recorded; the ablation is not automatically a pure density intervention. Actor-contact-on/off trials remain unavailable until actor contact is implemented. Measure the outcome that matches the hypothesis: passage creation and traversal time for the Digger example, coverage and dispersion for exploration, or virtual tags and survival for battle. Also report per-actor and aggregate results, energy or actuator work, saturation, decision age and capacity/command refusals. Clustering, heading agreement and success are different measurements. Crowding may help, hinder or make no difference; no monotonic density benefit, trained-NCA advantage or advanced-model advantage is claimed without those experiments.

results.query: How do two normalized velocity outputs make a drone fly far from the ground without unlimited gravity compensation, hidden goal steering or deleting collision momentum?
facts: The existing version-2 physical_wire_action envelope carries exactly move for action profile 4ly_velocity_v1; two finite components in [-1,1] are unit-disk normalized then multiplied by axis speed limits in cells per second.
World axes are positive right and down; the stabilizer receives own velocity and attitude but no position, goal, route, obstacle map, reward or mutable World.
Acceleration and braking share a bounded effort ellipse; gravity compensation consumes the same total thrust cap before response and slew.
Bounded torque supplies upright assistance, no integral can wind up and the legacy extra extreme-motion brake is bypassed.
Desired-speed limits constrain requests without overwriting physical velocity; actual Rapier gravity, passive drag and contacts remain effective.

Section: 4LY physical free-flight and assisted velocity control > How do two policy outputs become bounded flight?
The policy supplies only desired horizontal and vertical velocity through the existing version-2 `physical_wire_action` envelope. This profile admits exactly the `move` action field: a `Vector2` or an array of two finite numeric components in `[-1, 1]`. Components outside that range, unknown fields and nonfinite values are rejected. An admitted diagonal is normalized to the unit disk, then scaled by the profile's axis speed limits. World `+x` is right and `+y` is down; one world pixel is one cell and speed is cells per second. The [interface reference](../reference/interfaces-and-message-contracts.md#physical-free-flight-actions) owns exact packet and publication fields. At each fixed physical step the local controller compares desired and sampled velocity. It applies declared acceleration or braking limits, includes gravity compensation in the same requested thrust vector, saturates its total magnitude and applies bounded response/slew. Attitude correction supplies a separately bounded torque toward the authored upright attitude. These are authored game mechanics in adapter units; no calibrated SI propulsion or finite flywheel momentum model is implied. Exact defaults and limits live in the [configuration reference](../reference/configuration-reference.md#physical-free-flight-values). Gravity compensation consumes the available thrust budget. When thrust cannot support the chassis, an admitted zero-velocity request cannot hold it aloft. There is no hidden integral state to accumulate unreachable demand. Desired speed limits constrain requested motion; they do not clip velocity introduced by collision or an external impulse. The 4LY path does not add the legacy extreme-motion brake or a second gyro after the declared controller budget. Passive drag and actual contact/material forces remain physical influences.

Section: SetA actor controls and legacy policy compatibility > Which capabilities distinguish the three models?
| Model | Movement and actions | Intended comparison | |---|---|---| | **Runner** | Accelerated ground movement, limited air steering, buffered jump with brief coyote time, jump-release height control and an edge-triggered horizontal dash | Responsive platform traversal with deliberate jumps and bursts of horizontal movement | | **Skimmer** | Normalized two-axis thrust, held boost, held unpowered airbrake and finite rechargeable energy; depleted power restores gravity | Direct steering through open space, with a cost for sustained thrust and fast bursts | | **Crawler** | Strong ground traction, a short hop, supported obstacle clamber and held brace | Slower, controlled movement over uneven material surfaces | These are gameplay rules in the current cell/pixel coordinate system, not calibrated physical models. In particular, Skimmer movement does not implement Water buoyancy or pressure, and Crawler traversal does not confer wall/ceiling adhesion or a general grappling capability. Native cells continue to own material state; the actor cannot paint away an obstacle to make its movement succeed. Runner coyote time accepts a recent departure from supported ground; its input buffer permits a jump press shortly before landing to be used when support arrives. Releasing primary while rising cuts the jump. Holding primary does not automatically retrigger a jump, and holding secondary does not repeatedly request new dashes. Crawler's brace is a movement rule, not a physical anchor that makes an unsupported material structure load-bearing.

Section: 4LY physical free-flight and assisted velocity control > Can the stabilizer see a target or secretly navigate?
The shared stabilizer receives the normalized motion request, sampled linear velocity, angle and angular velocity, its copied resolved profile and fixed step duration. It receives no goal, route, obstacle map, ground-clearance query, reward, evaluator outcome or mutable World access. Its output is force/torque and copied diagnostics. Identical admitted inputs produce identical assistance regardless of world position or a producer's private goal. Human, scripted and policy producers submit through the same session admission and actuator path. Goal selection and route behavior belong to those producers. The current 4LY demo supplies an admitted zero-velocity conformance request every six physical ticks. It is not a flight teacher. A later producer may use its own copied observations to choose a velocity request; that does not give the local stabilizer navigation authority. A qualified flight teacher and actual-host episode interface belong to 4LY-003.

results.query: Does zero drone input hover forever, and how do lease expiry cancellation power off pause takeover and reset differ from an authorized neutral request?
facts: An admitted zero move requests physical braking and approximate hover while available thrust permits, without storing a position target.
The initial continuous authored power profile has no fuel or reserve-depletion timer.
Cancellation and expiry discard request and response state, select passive fallback and apply no assist without deleting momentum; cutoff is immediate rather than slew-delayed.
Explicit host power-off disables both propulsion and angular assistance and cannot be overridden by the two-output policy.
Run actor epoch producer sequence issued-observation control-generation and source-relative lease fences reject stale replies; pause takeover and replacement require fresh authority.
Published mode, fallback reason and lease state distinguish inactive assistance from a fresh external neutral command.
Paused observations grant no authority; resume refences flight generations, and unexpected physical step ordering suspends the session until replacement.

Section: 4LY physical free-flight and assisted velocity control > How do neutral, cancellation, power-off and suspension differ?
| State | Assistance and authority | |---|---| | Admitted nonzero `move` | Track desired velocity within bounded force/torque and response limits while the source-observation lease remains valid | | Admitted zero `move` | Physically brake toward zero velocity and approximately hover while thrust permits; no world-position target is stored | | No command, cancellation or lease expiry | Passive fallback: discard the request and response state, apply no propulsion/stabilizing torque, and retain physical momentum and gravity | | Explicit propulsion disabled by the host | Apply no propulsion or stabilizing torque; a fresh command cannot override the host switch | | Lifecycle suspension | Retire pending command authority and stop further physical steps; a physical step completed just before suspension can still be accounted, and resume requires fresh authority | | Fault quarantine | Revoke current command and assistance, mark suspension, and preserve the last finite physical sample for diagnosis | | Reset, close or replacement | Retire the old incarnation, controller response state and command history; old replies cannot act on the replacement | The fallback mode and lease state are published explicitly. Passive fallback does not claim a fresh external zero-velocity command. Enabling propulsion is not a policy output and does not revive a retired lease. Cancellation, reset and power cutoff immediately clear force/torque response; the ordinary enabled slew limits do not delay this removal of authority. The initial profile declares no simulated fuel tank or energy-depletion timer, so stationary authorized hover is not defeated by an undocumented resource countdown. Power/thrust limits remain effective. The session retains run, actor, epoch, monotonic sequence, actually issued observation, control generation, producer and lease fencing. Expiry remains relative to the source observation's tick, not command arrival. Cancellation invalidates previously issued observations. The completed tick which reaches a flight lease's deadline retires it before another reply can reuse that old observation. Reusing a slot or resuming cannot renew stale authority. Copied views cannot mutate live tuning or controller state.

**Current 4LY-001 contract / 4LY-002 profile candidates:** a session-installed `4ly_*` actor declares `action_profile = "4ly_velocity_v1"`, `control_mode = "4ly_velocity_v1"` and `profile_version = 1` in its copied observation. Its command still uses the version-2 `physical_wire_action` envelope above. The action object must contain exactly one field: ```json {"move": [0.6, -0.8]} ``` The two finite numeric components must individually lie in `[-1, 1]` before unit-disk normalization. `Vector2` is also accepted by the in-process API. A finite oversized request is rejected in this profile; the retained legacy normalizer still clamps its own vectors. Arrays of the wrong length, booleans, NaN/infinity, missing movement and extra fields such as `effort`, `trim`, abilities, goals or equipment are refused. Existing run/actor/epoch/producer, sequence, issued-observation and lease checks apply before actuation. The admitted vector is world-relative: `+x` right, `+y` down. Componentwise multiplication by the resolved `desired_speed` gives cells/second. Diagonal normalization precedes this mapping; unequal axis limits therefore describe an ellipse of possible desired velocities. Desired speed is not an enforced cap on physical motion after collisions or external impulses. `Session.set_propulsion_enabled(actor_id, enabled)` is an explicit host/fixture switch, outside the two-output action. It revokes existing input before changing power. `Session.takeover(actor_id, expected_epoch, producer)` revokes old capabilities before assigning a new authorized source; neither operation reconstructs the body or deletes momentum. Suspension, cancellation, expiry and reset retain their existing lifetime fences. The [4LY lifecycle table](../systems/physical-free-flight.md#how-do-neutral-cancellation-power-off-and-suspension-differ) distinguishes an authorized neutral request from passive fallback. The resolved profile descriptor carries `profile_hash`, `controller_id`, units, axes, speed mapping, empty default loadout, fallback, neutral and resource semantics. Its **`capabilities`** subdescriptor is a deep-copied static physical contract for collider dimensions, mass/inertia, desired-speed limits, acceleration/braking authority, response/slew times, force/gravity margin, drag and upright torque. That subdescriptor deliberately omits actor name, evaluator label, goal, position and reward. Dynamic propulsion, lease/fallback state and saturation remain separately observable. Controller receipts add `controller_hash` and `fixed_delta`. `profile_hash` is SHA-256 of the validated resolved profile serialized with sorted keys and full float precision. `controller_hash` is the embedded SHA-256 of checked-in UTF-8 controller source with the `SOURCE_SHA256` value replaced by the literal `<CONTROLLER_HASH>`; its conformance test checks the digest. The embedded digest remains available when exported scripts omit source text. Keep repository/runtime identity alongside these hashes; they are not an attestation of the physics engine or a learned-policy result. Saturation and slew flags expose the active bounds. Section: 4LY physical free-flight and assisted velocity control > What can an ordinary player or external producer do with the new family?
Open **F5 → set4LY → Trainer / Hauler / Drifter / Dart** in the regular sandbox or an exploratory Play host. Select the keyboard, scripted-demo or external-policy source and Apply. This resets the authored map and creates a fresh matching Rapier chassis at that host's spawn; it never converts the old body's live mass, inertia or collider. **WASD** submits only the admitted world-frame horizontal/vertical `move` request. Releasing the keys sends authorized neutral; focus/menu/input cancellation retires authority and falls back to passive physical behavior. **R** resets the retained selection. The visible F5 button reports the selected profile, producer, current flight mode and a tooltip with the lease/fallback and resolved profile hash. The selection panel shows movement, assistance, reset and empty-loadout semantics. Equipment choice and equip-only requests are disabled and independently refused at the host for all four flight profiles. The same session accepts the demo's current neutral request and the external policy's already-defined version-2 wire action. A demo source here is a *neutral conformance producer*, not a qualified navigation teacher. The four-drone family shares the session controller, force/torque actuator, contact owner and observation schema. No extra policy steering, training fast-path, Web ownership change, scientific fixture substitution, or unmeasured browser/platform qualification is implied. It may be selected with the ordinary multi-NPC demonstration checkbox, one body per drone. Collider-aligned rendering uses the real bridge's transform and rectangle dimensions. A small thrust mark shows the **applied** controller force and an intent mark shows the requested desired velocity, only while an admitted lease is live. Neither mark drives a pose, changes the force budget, or reconstructs a second motion trajectory.

Section: 4LY physical free-flight and assisted velocity control > What can an ordinary player or external producer do with the new family?
Open **F5 → set4LY → Trainer / Hauler / Drifter / Dart** in the regular sandbox or an exploratory Play host. Select the keyboard, scripted-demo or external-policy source and Apply. This resets the authored map and creates a fresh matching Rapier chassis at that host's spawn; it never converts the old body's live mass, inertia or collider. **WASD** submits only the admitted world-frame horizontal/vertical `move` request. Releasing the keys sends authorized neutral; focus/menu/input cancellation retires authority and falls back to passive physical behavior. **R** resets the retained selection. The visible F5 button reports the selected profile, producer, current flight mode and a tooltip with the lease/fallback and resolved profile hash. The selection panel shows movement, assistance, reset and empty-loadout semantics. Equipment choice and equip-only requests are disabled and independently refused at the host for all four flight profiles. The same session accepts the demo's current neutral request and the external policy's already-defined version-2 wire action. A demo source here is a *neutral conformance producer*, not a qualified navigation teacher. The four-drone family shares the session controller, force/torque actuator, contact owner and observation schema. No extra policy steering, training fast-path, Web ownership change, scientific fixture substitution, or unmeasured browser/platform qualification is implied. It may be selected with the ordinary multi-NPC demonstration checkbox, one body per drone. Collider-aligned rendering uses the real bridge's transform and rectangle dimensions. A small thrust mark shows the **applied** controller force and an intent mark shows the requested desired velocity, only while an admitted lease is live. Neither mark drives a pose, changes the force budget, or reconstructs a second motion trajectory.
