Section: 4LY physical free-flight and assisted velocity control > Which identities and observations may a capture claim?
The resolved, versioned profile covers collider dimensions, mass/inertia, gravity reference, friction/restitution, desired-speed mapping, acceleration/braking/total-thrust limits, response and slew, passive linear/angular drag, attitude gains/torque and declared resource semantics. Validation occurs before body allocation. The copied capability descriptor publishes profile and controller identities and hashes; retain these with source/runtime identity when exporting evidence. Matching a profile name alone does not establish compatible tuning or code. Requested action, admitted normalized action, desired velocity, requested and applied assistance, saturation/response state and sampled physical motion are separate publications. Applied assistance describes this actuator's bounded contribution. It is not a decomposition of Rapier gravity, passive damping, contacts or delayed native material response; no unavailable passive-force breakdown or total physical energy accounting is claimed. `flight.command` identifies the accepted raw/admitted command; `command_live` states whether it currently has lease authority. `flight.applied` identifies the sequence and step tick associated with the current actuator receipt. The separate `flight.last_step` preserves the most recently completed commanded step's admitted action and controller receipt, including its original producer, control generation, sequence, source tick, session step tick and physical step. Cancellation clears current command/assistance publication while retaining that labelled historical step until replacement or close. Neither a stored history entry nor a newly accepted command proves that another physical step occurred. The top-level applied impulse fields account for this actuator's force or torque multiplied by the admitted step duration; they do not describe a pre-step impulse motor or the sum of all forces on the body. The 60 Hz physical cadence and existing six-tick decision interval are separate from the command lease. A missed fresh decision does not manufacture neutral input or renew authority: an already-live lease may continue only to its original deadline, where the completed physical tick retires it into passive fallback. Any later fresh command still requires a newly issued observation and sequence; an old observation cannot prolong its command by being submitted late.

results.query: How do 4LY-002 profiles expose policy-observable capability descriptors and actual assistance while keeping the controller goal-blind?
facts: The profile descriptor exposes a copied static capabilities subobject for rectangle size, mass/inertia, requested speeds, acceleration/braking, force/response/slew, drag, attitude and gravity/vertical force margin.

This subdescriptor contains no evaluator label, secret actor name, goal, world position or reward; dynamic flight assistance/lease/resource state is published separately in the physical session observation.
The four source profiles use shared action profile 4ly_velocity_v1, source-hashed goal-blind controller, one rigid chassis, and explicit empty default loadouts.

Measured Linux and Windows physical profiles share identity hashes and pass prospectively registered envelope comparisons; static capabilities or those measurements alone do not grant navigation learning, owner-feel or Web execution acceptance.

Section: 4LY-003 physical flight laboratory > Policy observation and normalization
The versioned `4ly-observation/v1` dictionary is copied from the real owner and task goal. Fields in canonical insertion order: 1. `version`, `action_version`, `run_id`, `actor_id`, `epoch`, `observed_tick`, `observation_id`, `control_generation` 2. `goal_delta_cells` (Vector2, world +x right/+y down), `arrival_radius_cells` (scalar positive) 3. `velocity_cells_per_second` (Vector2), `orientation_sin`, `orientation_cos` (dimensionless), `angular_velocity_rad_per_second` 4. `actuator_mode` (string), `assistance_valid` (true only while a live admitted command owns a structurally valid controller response; false after expiry or cancellation even though the configured controller's reset receipt remains structurally valid), `command_age_ticks` (-1 if absent), `command_live`, `lease_remaining_ticks` 5. `resources` (continuous authored supply, powered, fuel measurement invalid), `capabilities` (copied immutable physical *values*, without model name), `local_obstacles` (eight world-fixed rays, R/NE/N/NW/L/SW/S/SE, maximum 80 cells, normalized hit distance, per-ray validity mask, hit flag) No absolute goal, scene geometry, route, future disturbance, evaluator status, reward, score, source profile ID or global map is provided. The policy producer and teacher see the same dictionary. Owner ray queries are 8 finite Rapier queries against *actual* installed native terrain colliders; invalid sensing is explicit with empty arrays and `available=false`. A valid ray with no collision reports distance 1.0 and hit=false. Controller assistance receives **no** scene position, target or rays. `4ly-flat-observation/v1` is a **54-float**, fixed-order `CyberPhysicalFlightObservationAdapter.flatten()` output: | Offset (0-based) | Contents | Normalization and supported range | |---|---|---| | 0-1 | Relative goal x/y | divide 512 cells, clamp [-1,1] | | 2-3 | Own velocity x/y | divide respective `desired_speed`, clamp [-4,4] | | 4-5 | Angle sine/cosine | unchanged [-1,1] | | 6 | Angular velocity | divide 8 rad/s, clamp [-4,4] | | 7-11 | Mode one-hot | velocity, neutral, passive_no_lease, power_off, other | | 12 | Command age | -1/18 when absent, otherwise ticks/18; [-1,1] | | 13 | Live flag | 0 or 1 | | 14 | Remaining lease | ticks/18 in [0,1] | | 15 | Powered flag | 0 or 1 | | 16-29 | Physical capabilities | width/64, height/64, mass/20, inertia/14000, speed x/240, speed y/240, acceleration/1200, braking/1200, thrust response/5, velocity response/5, max force/24000, gravity/500, vertical force margin/24000, angular drag/8; each clamped [-1,1] | | 30-37 | 8 local ray distances | [0,1], zeroed if mask invalid | | 38-45 | 8 hit flags | 0/1, zeroed if invalid | | 46-53 | 8 validity masks | 0/1 | Malformed source versions or nonfinite values return an empty result rather than supplying fabricated observations. Capability scaling uses published schema bounds; raw physical values remain in the dictionary for diagnostics, and clipping is declared for the flat learner input. Negative velocity ratio may exceed 1

validated. Code 0 is never applied, hashed or read back. A request with every code 0, one with only Water at 0, and the explicit default therefore hash to the same `policy_hash`; these are registered vectors. **Canonical bytes.** These are hashed with SHA-256 to `policy_hash`. Integers are little-endian: ```text "lcb-liquid-policy\0" 18 bytes policy_version u16 catalogue_digest | capability_matrix_digest 32 + 32 raw bytes N u16 (material_id u16, family_code u8, variant_code u8) × N normalized, ascending F u8 (family_code u8, block_version u16, byte_length u32 = 4·L, L × i32) × F M u16 (material_id u16, block_version u16, byte_length u32 = 4·L, L × i32) × M ``` - Wire lengths count words; canonical lengths count bytes (4·*L*). - A wire word is narrowed to u8/u16 only after its range check above. - Two envelopes are the same policy if and only if their normalized canonical bytes are equal. - The normalized envelope re-encodes the applied policy, and decoding it reproduces the same policy. **Validation precedence.** The first failure wins, so a given malformed input has exactly one refusal: 1. every element is an int32 (`malformed_policy`); 2. length ≥ header + 3, then magic, `envelope_version` and `policy_version` (`malformed_policy`); 3. `catalogue_digest`, then `capability_matrix_digest`, each compared with the running build. Either mismatch is `stale_capability_matrix`, and `detail` names the digest. This check runs before any catalogue-dependent interpretation; 4. section structure: counts and block lengths in range, exact consumption (`malformed_policy`); 5. per assignment: `unknown_material` (outside the catalogue or reserved 10), `not_a_liquid`, `unknown_family`, `unknown_variant`; then strictly ascending IDs and completeness over all liquid descriptors (`malformed_policy`); 6. normalization of code 0 (a non-reference variant with code 0 is `malformed_policy`); 7. per assignment: `combination_rejected`, `not_selectable`, `variant_unsupported`, `platform_unsupported` (no native handshake, any non-default), `family_unavailable` (not compiled/qualified); 8. blocks, family then material: - strictly ascending owners (`malformed_policy`); - a known `(owner, block_version)` and a schema-matching length (`unknown_parameter`); - a family block only for an assigned family, and a material block only where the material's applied family declares it (`malformed_policy`); - every field in its schema range (`malformed_policy`); - then any missing mandatory block (`unknown_parameter`). `water_semantics_incompatible`, `capacity_refused` and `normalization_required` depend on the World setup. They remain native-only checks after step 8. Each refusal returns `{code, material|null, detail}` and leaves the live session, its readback and its `policy_hash` untouched. **Historical oracle schemas are illustrative.** The original profiles register two contract-test schemas only to exercise the rules: - a mandatory `inertial_cellular_v1` v1 block (`damping_q16` 0..65536, `speed_cap_q8` 256..2048); - an optional Water v1 block, valid only under `cellular_yield_v1` (`flow_rate_permille` 1..1000). #200 appends the actual W-CY material

results.query: How can an LCB pressure World be hashed, inspected and saved for exact continuation, and how does that differ from a CYSD1 level save?
facts: World::physical_state_hash() version 2 covers clock, selected/applied regions, effective physics configuration and scheduler geometry, policy, family parameters, pending events, body-mask occupancy, stored cells with sidecars, activity, gas state and the exact shared quantity ledger with construction identities. Historical content_hash and state_hash definitions are unchanged.

CYPS2 retains continuation state, exact quantity accounting and construction bindings behind a SHA-256 digest. Restore validates schema, source roles, aggregate closure and stored authority before returning a replacement; refusal preserves the running World. Historical CYPS1 explicitly refuses rather than silently changing its interpretation.
CYSD1 stores no liquid policy and always reconstructs on default families; it is never an exact continuation.

Section: Level saves and exact replay > Can a failed world be saved or recovered?
**Current:** ordinary Godot level export rejects a quarantined World; it must not label partial tick state as a valid level. Raw serialized native reads remain diagnostic. A previously saved, validated level or explicit fresh level/reset can replace the failed World. Invalid replacement leaves the fault and partial state intact. Section: Level saves and exact replay > How does CYPS2 differ from CYSD1?
**Current on main through accepted PR #246 (`ec58d919`, 2026-10-25).** `World::save_physical_state()`/`restore_physical_state()` and the bridge's `export_physical_state`/`import_physical_state` write and read **CYPS2** (`kPhysicalStateFormatVersion` 2), an exact tick-boundary continuation for LCB comparison Worlds. Its canonical description is the [pressure persistence contract](../architecture/pressure-flow-v1.md#persistence-cyps-v2) and [shared native setup/accounting contract](../architecture/liquid-prepared-setup-and-receipts.md). | | CYSD1 | CYPS2 | |---|---|---| | Purpose | finite level exchange | exact continuation of a comparison World | | Liquid policy | not stored; import always reconstructs on default families (NC-10) | policy envelope stored and re-admitted by the running build | | Clock, epochs, regions, pending events, activity blocks | omitted | stored | | Pressure sidecars and gas table | n/a (lossy; never a continuation) | stored | | Shared quantity accounting and construction binding | omitted | exact source/sink and rule totals, visible+overfill, separate material cell counts, prepared/normalization identities | | Integrity | codec checksum and native validation | SHA-256 of the body, then range and invariant checks | | Failure | live World intact | `invalid_argument`/`LiquidPolicyRefused`; live World intact ("running world preserved") | | Continuation | none claimed | bit-identical physical and state hash, including at another worker count | CYPS omits execution settings (workers, capacities come from the caller), host-owned transient body masks and Rapier state, and requires settled discovery to be disabled. It is not general sparse-world persistence, replay input capture or full application replay. The owner-requested native codec freeze does not freeze production Cell/global ABI or those missing host contracts; CYSD1 is unchanged. Historical CYPS1 belongs to the #245 source/artifact evidence and is explicitly refused by this decoder. A valid digest does not excuse inconsistent accounting: restore validates closure, roles, quanta and actual stored authority. The native prepared builder can normalize final setup tuples only with explicit opt-in and a bound receipt. It cannot normalize a live World. Godot's normal level import still reconstructs defaults; native candidate CYSD1 ingress preflights nonzero fractional W-CY Water and returns `normalization_required` rather than silently rounding. The old Godot dictionary run getter is not the typed native receipt and provides no full host-replay proof.

Section: Level saves and exact replay > May saving run concurrently with a tick?
**Current: no.** Call construction/export/import at a safe boundary with exclusive World ownership. `copy_level(World&, ...)` clears transient obstacles so temperature sampling reads stored cells. The caller must rebuild the body projection before the next cellular tick. Export is therefore not a concurrent const query, even though it does not change saved material bytes. The Web controller performs these operations on its synchronous owner. A future asynchronous save service needs an explicit capture/handoff contract; borrowing mutable World storage from a writer is **Rejected**.

results.query: If I opt into whole-cell Water, which final setup cells are rounded, how are temperature and overlaps handled, and must the comparator use the same normalized setup?
facts: Native preparation takes unique final cell tuples after overwrite resolution, refuses duplicate coordinates, sorts row-major, omits ambient Empty and preserves nonambient Empty thermal authority; it never normalizes an edit history or reveals an overwritten earlier rectangle.

Whole-cell preparation with fractional Water refuses normalization_required without explicit water-normalize-v1; an explicit request also normalizes the fractional-capable comparator and retains a receipt even for zero net delta. Section: LCB Water comparison contract and reference fixtures > Four controlled Water settings (Gate D) > Water quantity normalization
- **Common comparator.** The common initial comparator is **full-cell Water**: every Water cell at `maximum()` (255 at mass8). This is exactly representable in all four regimes, so both reference fixtures use only full Water cells. - **Fractional cells.** For a whole-cell (`W-CY`) or any regime without fractional support, a setup containing fractional Water is **refused** (`normalization_required`) unless the caller explicitly opts in to a registered setup conversion. The registered rule, implemented in accepted main native #200 source through #246, is **`water-normalize-v1` (corrected 2026-10-23)**: - **Rounding.** A Water cell of mass `m` (1 ≤ m ≤ `maximum()`) becomes one full cell (`maximum()`) when `2·m ≥ maximum()`, evaluated in at least 32-bit arithmetic. Otherwise it becomes Empty. `maximum()` is odd for mass bits 3–8, so the smallest up-rounding mass is `(maximum()+1)/2`: **128/255 rounds up and 127/255 rounds down** at mass8, and 4/7 up, 3/7 down at mass3. The earlier wording "`maximum()/2`" wrongly rounded 127/255 up. - **Per-cell signed delta.** `δ = (maximum() − m)` for an up-round, `δ = −m` for a down-round. Cells are visited in deterministic row-major order (ascending y, then x). - **Receipt.** The receipt holds rule ID and version, mass bits, the canonical setup hash and seed before and after, cells up/down/unchanged, `Σδ⁺`, `Σδ⁻` and the net delta, and a receipt hash that is part of the run receipt. - **Ledger.** The net delta is booked as a **declared setup-only source/sink** at tick 0. It is not physical conservation, and it is not a live hot-swap. Matched comparisons that need a conversion compare post-normalization states and report the delta. Nothing rounds or deletes partial mass silently. Native preparation resolves immutable final tuples, preserves thermal/foreign state, checks actual installed payload and binds the one-shot tick-zero ledger seed to the receipt. The explicit Godot constructor refuses partial final Water; its normalization opt-in and full normal-application routing remain integration gaps. See the [native setup/receipt contract](../architecture/liquid-prepared-setup-and-receipts.md) and [accepted evidence](../audits/2026-10-25-lcb001-shared-contract-acceptance.md). - **Reverse direction.** A whole-cell or inertial Water cell entering a FreeMass-valued observation counts as `maximum()`.

The [Water quantity normalization law](../operations/lcb-water-comparison-and-fixtures.md#water-quantity-normalization) owns rounding, signed setup delta and matched post-normalization comparison. This implementation executes that registered law on the final tuples. It validates mass bits 3–8 and uses checked integer quantities and totals. | Native target requirement and request | Outcome | |---|---| | Fractional-capable target, no opt-in | Preserve fractional Water; no normalization receipt | | Whole-cell target, fractional Water, no opt-in | Native `normalization_required` refusal | | Either target, explicit `water-normalize-v1` | Same normalized payload and normalization receipt for both comparator arms | | Explicit rule with already-full/empty setup | Retain an explicit receipt even when the net delta is zero | `PreparedWorldBuilder` derives the quantity requirement from the admitted native policy. It validates the original Water coherence lane against the selected policy before rounding can remove a cell. Precision and ambient must match the requested World, and only the implemented SerialInPlace/PhasedInPlace backends are accepted. Policy admission precedes candidate allocation. The preparation bound is at most 1024 cells per side and 1,048,576 explicit records; a caller may lower the record budget. Inclusive endpoints and the native reservation halo have checked coordinate bounds. World chunk capacity can still refuse an otherwise valid setup. Allocation/length and expected reservation-capacity failures return native capacity outcomes. Unexpected installation, digest or quantity invariant failures return a separate native preparation-failure outcome. No failed candidate is installed into the retained live session. The builder reserves cell/thermal storage, installs the final tuples, captures the actual prepared payload, and compares its digest with the immutable value. It checks actual Water quantity before attaching a construction ledger once at tick 0. The ledger retains the exact before/after payload/setup identities and normalization receipt digest. An alternative before mass such as 128 versus 129 cannot borrow the same after-255 World to assert a different installed normalization history. Water `cellular_yield_v1/reference` is admitted in this native branch, with its own optional Water material block v2 (`viscosity_index` 0–255, default 0). Its ingress requires `maximum()` per Water cell. A fractional public bool `set_cell_state` returns false before mutation/allocation; native setup/import preflight returns `normalization_required` where applicable. No FreeMass transfer fallback or foreign Paste/Slush parameter supplies its motion law. The [family policy](liquid-solver-family-policy.md) owns the wider family and material-hook contract.

results.query: Can a caller manufacture a refused construction record, and what state survives a failed native setup attempt?
facts: ConstructionRefusal is privately constructed by native validation or preparation; a caller-provided reason or dictionary cannot create a native-issued outcome. Policy/setup refusal and unexpected native preparation failure have distinct outcome kinds.

An exact raw policy refusal binds the actual bounded request words, including request-only family code zero. A builder outcome binds its normalized policy envelope and cannot pretend to recover an earlier raw host request.

A refused or failed candidate is never installed. Its construction-attempt receipt is separate from the applied-run receipt and requires unchanged captured live state/setup and a nonzero unchanged generation.
Capacity/refusal outcomes are distinct from internal preparation failures; oversized raw input throws before parsing rather than issuing a token that claims a truncated exact request.

facts: The completed-boundary quantity ledger covers stored visible Water plus pressure overfill across the whole World, including body-masked, paused and out-of-interest cells. Section: Transport profiles > How does actual motion drive mixing and erosion?
**Current:** after a successful powder fall into Empty, `World::mix_after_motion` may exchange it with an unlike exposed neighbouring powder, using a real void above or below the candidate as loose-flow evidence and at most five occupied neighbours. The source must actually have fallen vertically; activity flags and update epochs cannot initiate mixing. The displaced candidate must not already have been written this tick. Density eligibility remains a separate path and still excludes every powder/powder pair. Identical powder grains are not shuffled. Lateral Water movement/transfer may pick up the grain below its source. At least 64 successfully transported mass units are required, and effective disturbance is `mass * carrying / 255`. It must reach both 64 and `pickup + occupied * packing`. The eight-neighbour occupancy counts hard surfaces and support-capable grains. Gentle rejects occupancy at least four; erosion permits it above threshold. A coordinate-stable four-tick lane bounds pickup to at most one per source on that lane. There is no stored disturbance, delayed transport debt or probability that can gradually eat a resting bed. Once flow stops, pickup stops immediately. Both paths use the existing whole-cell conservative swap, preserving material, both state bytes and temperature, including Water fill. Each touched coordinate is within radius two of the original update; writes remain within radius one. The diagonal path includes the vacated/intermediate source, checks occupancy and body masks, and cannot bypass a wall by checking only its destination. Braced Stone remains excluded. The shared radius and job ownership are unchanged. Telemetry kinds 8 and 9 count powder mixing and grain transport separately from Empty movement, density swaps and conversions. Kind 11 counts new neighbour reads. Existing histogram bounds/overflow apply; disabled hooks make no new neighbour probes. No extra wake or per-cell motion field is introduced. Horizontal sampling caps the existing lateral candidates at one; the first direction uses the existing deterministic rule. Water and yielding liquids previously attempted up to two; Oil, Acid and Lava already attempt at most one, so setting two does not invent additional movement. Gravity and diagonal falling are unchanged. Cadence 1..60 gates only lateral movement using coordinate-stable phases and the existing earliest per-block wake deadline, without catch-up. This can wake quiet blocked liquid at later eligible times; it is not a guaranteed sleep or performance improvement. Chemistry/lifecycle cadence is untouched. Telemetry kind 10 counts eligible lateral candidate probes (target byte is a placeholder, not the encountered material); kind 4 counts Water mass units transferred, not transfer calls. Sampling never multiplies carrying strength. See [dated results](../audits/2026-09-09-issue-13-transport.md); visual acceptance and production

Section: Water state precision experiment > Mathematical contract
Mass bits b=4/6/8/10 give M=15/63/255/1023; physical fill=m/M. Input is an exact rational n/d in [0,1]; quantize per cell Q=floor((2*n*M+d)/(2*d)), nearest with half up. Zero becomes Empty. Record requested rational sum, actual initial integer sum and error=sum(Q)/M-requested. Full-cell basin inputs are exact. Integer additions/subtractions and capacity caps remain exact; no fractional remainder is stored. Lateral request floor(3*positive difference/4), then existing integer viscosity scaling; merge amount=min(request,source,M-target), subtraction and addition identical. Empty has zero quantity. Output divides by each arm's M; runtime conservation compares every tick against that arm's initial integer total. All fixtures are closed and nonreactive: source=sink=0, including shelf removal. P1: four mass arms, delay8. Common normalized policy maps film48/255 and tolerance 1/255 by nearest/half-up: film=3/12/48/193, tolerance=0/0/1/4. Zero tolerance is intentional nearest representation, not permission to add a minimum transfer. Front threshold uses ceil(128*M/255); one-cell levelness is spread<=M; tiny residue means mass<=Q(1/255), with zero threshold counting no positive cell. P2: same four masses/delay8, normalized policy versus literal tolerance1. Film remains normalized48/255 in both: replacing film by1 would redefine film intent and conflate two threshold changes. Mass8 policies are identical controls. P3: mass8/normalized, delay8 versus Water-only delay4. Legal semantic countdown domain0..12, including all pairwise max merges, pre-decrement timing, movement, creation/reset and repeated transfers. Out-of-domain Water delay rejected by experiment setter; no generic state compression claim. Exhaustive storage tests also preserve every non-Water byte a/b value and epoch across writes.

Section: LCB Water comparison contract and reference fixtures > Four controlled Water settings (Gate D) > Water quantity normalization
- **Common comparator.** The common initial comparator is **full-cell Water**: every Water cell at `maximum()` (255 at mass8). This is exactly representable in all four regimes, so both reference fixtures use only full Water cells. - **Fractional cells.** For a whole-cell (`W-CY`) or any regime without fractional support, a setup containing fractional Water is **refused** (`normalization_required`) unless the caller explicitly opts in to a registered setup conversion. The registered rule, implemented in accepted main native #200 source through #246, is **`water-normalize-v1` (corrected 2026-10-23)**: - **Rounding.** A Water cell of mass `m` (1 ≤ m ≤ `maximum()`) becomes one full cell (`maximum()`) when `2·m ≥ maximum()`, evaluated in at least 32-bit arithmetic. Otherwise it becomes Empty. `maximum()` is odd for mass bits 3–8, so the smallest up-rounding mass is `(maximum()+1)/2`: **128/255 rounds up and 127/255 rounds down** at mass8, and 4/7 up, 3/7 down at mass3. The earlier wording "`maximum()/2`" wrongly rounded 127/255 up. - **Per-cell signed delta.** `δ = (maximum() − m)` for an up-round, `δ = −m` for a down-round. Cells are visited in deterministic row-major order (ascending y, then x). - **Receipt.** The receipt holds rule ID and version, mass bits, the canonical setup hash and seed before and after, cells up/down/unchanged, `Σδ⁺`, `Σδ⁻` and the net delta, and a receipt hash that is part of the run receipt. - **Ledger.** The net delta is booked as a **declared setup-only source/sink** at tick 0. It is not physical conservation, and it is not a live hot-swap. Matched comparisons that need a conversion compare post-normalization states and report the delta. Nothing rounds or deletes partial mass silently. Native preparation resolves immutable final tuples, preserves thermal/foreign state, checks actual installed payload and binds the one-shot tick-zero ledger seed to the receipt. The explicit Godot constructor refuses partial final Water; its normalization opt-in and full normal-application routing remain integration gaps. See the [native setup/receipt contract](../architecture/liquid-prepared-setup-and-receipts.md) and [accepted evidence](../audits/2026-10-25-lcb001-shared-contract-acceptance.md). - **Reverse direction.** A whole-cell or inertial Water cell entering a FreeMass-valued observation counts as `maximum()`.

results.query: How do I diagnose intermittent 180 second physical actor Godot hangs on Windows and Linux without hiding failures?
facts: Both platform runners share independent pre-termination diagnostics, retain the 180-second outer deadline and strict failure/error/skip oracle, and fail the three suspect cases after 45 seconds without new progress; capture starts after 30 idle seconds and never extends the failure deadline.

Original case/phase/rig/model/tick markers and coarse sequence/step heartbeats remain visible. Linux attempts GDB stacks and wait-state capture; Windows attempts process/thread state and wrapper/child minidumps. A fixture-only 120-second observer uses copied context, emits sticky error and never self-kills before capture.

The standard campaign requires 600 physical executions: 50 per OS/mode/test stratum across Windows/Linux, serial/three-process parallel and three suspect tests, plus 20 imports. Source/run/attempt/runtime completeness and every failure remain visible. The earlier paired campaign separately requires reproduced control hangs, matching scope and zero patched failures; neither a captured call nor a passing helper alone proves repair.

The earlier same-host campaign qualified the cooperative deferred-BVH join with six Windows control hangs versus zero candidate hangs in 300 Windows/Linux trials. Integrated PR #236 passed exact-head ordinary gates and merged as 13b8e631f3e8fbaa2176ed41afc02c434b11e558; fresh standard campaign 40129364630 at that source completed 600/600 physical passes, 0/600 timeouts, zero other failures and 20/20 import passes, independently verified. Section: LCB Water comparison contract and reference fixtures > Four controlled Water settings (Gate D) > Water quantity normalization
- **Common comparator.** The common initial comparator is **full-cell Water**: every Water cell at `maximum()` (255 at mass8). This is exactly representable in all four regimes, so both reference fixtures use only full Water cells. - **Fractional cells.** For a whole-cell (`W-CY`) or any regime without fractional support, a setup containing fractional Water is **refused** (`normalization_required`) unless the caller explicitly opts in to a registered setup conversion. The registered rule, implemented in accepted main native #200 source through #246, is **`water-normalize-v1` (corrected 2026-10-23)**: - **Rounding.** A Water cell of mass `m` (1 ≤ m ≤ `maximum()`) becomes one full cell (`maximum()`) when `2·m ≥ maximum()`, evaluated in at least 32-bit arithmetic. Otherwise it becomes Empty. `maximum()` is odd for mass bits 3–8, so the smallest up-rounding mass is `(maximum()+1)/2`: **128/255 rounds up and 127/255 rounds down** at mass8, and 4/7 up, 3/7 down at mass3. The earlier wording "`maximum()/2`" wrongly rounded 127/255 up. - **Per-cell signed delta.** `δ = (maximum() − m)` for an up-round, `δ = −m` for a down-round. Cells are visited in deterministic row-major order (ascending y, then x). - **Receipt.** The receipt holds rule ID and version, mass bits, the canonical setup hash and seed before and after, cells up/down/unchanged, `Σδ⁺`, `Σδ⁻` and the net delta, and a receipt hash that is part of the run receipt. - **Ledger.** The net delta is booked as a **declared setup-only source/sink** at tick 0. It is not physical conservation, and it is not a live hot-swap. Matched comparisons that need a conversion compare post-normalization states and report the delta. Nothing rounds or deletes partial mass silently. Native preparation resolves immutable final tuples, preserves thermal/foreign state, checks actual installed payload and binds the one-shot tick-zero ledger seed to the receipt. The explicit Godot constructor refuses partial final Water; its normalization opt-in and full normal-application routing remain integration gaps. See the [native setup/receipt contract](../architecture/liquid-prepared-setup-and-receipts.md) and [accepted evidence](../audits/2026-10-25-lcb001-shared-contract-acceptance.md). - **Reverse direction.** A whole-cell or inertial Water cell entering a FreeMass-valued observation counts as `maximum()`.

**Subsequent unmerged LCB-003 extension, 2026-10-25:** the normal liquid panel can rebuild an unblinded body-free Water Feel run under an explicit family. It retains the sampled player, original recipe/actions, independent version1 Water policy and ordinary control/ledger behavior, and requires Exploratory. Solver reset/semantic changes preserve accepted selection transactionally; blind/body/future fractional whole-cell source routes refuse as documented in the [owner contract](../architecture/liquid-prepared-setup-and-receipts.md#ordinary-water-feel-preparation). The [dated local proof](../audits/2026-10-25-lcb003-water-feel-constructor.md) does not requalify #19's frozen blind study, select a perceptual winner, or supply actual new Web/publication acceptance. The frozen registration below is unchanged. One version-1 `WaterExperimentPolicy` is the only normalized representation consumed by World construction and every selection surface. Its fields are: | Field | Domain and default | Authority | |---|---|---| | `version` | exactly 1 | schema | | `mass_bits` | integer 3..8; default 8 | simulation | | `coherence_ticks` | integer 0..12; default 12; named `current`, `three-bit`, `short`, `none` map to 12, 7, 3, 0 | simulation | | `rest_policy` | exactly `current-normalized-v1` | simulation | | `render_fill_levels` | exactly 4 for this experiment | presentation | | `interface_mode` | `coverage` or `oriented`; default `coverage` | presentation | | `scenario_id` | registered Water Feel scenario | recipe | | `seed` | unsigned 31-bit integer; default 0 | recipe | | `source` | `default`, `profile`, `launch` or `panel` | provenance | The canonical serialization uses those keys in that order and a SHA-256 over compact UTF-8 JSON. Derived simulation values are computed once during validation: `maximum=(1<<mass_bits)-1`, `film=Q(48/255)`, and `tolerance=Q(1/255)`, where `Q(n/d)=floor((2*n*maximum+d)/(2*d))`. Runtime mass is an integer in the candidate lattice stored in the existing superset lane. Transfer subtracts and adds the same integer. Zero is Empty. Coherence is the existing pre-decrement countdown and max-on-merge rule with the configured emission/reset maximum. The policy is immutable after World construction. Profile JSON, launch arguments and the panel all call the same parser, validator, canonicalizer and resolver. Precedence is panel draft over launch over profile over defaults, with field origins retained in effective provenance. A complete candidate is validated before construction. The owner constructs and populates a fresh World, then atomically replaces the current World only after success. Invalid input or candidate construction leaves the old World, render exchange and effective-policy identity intact. Render-only mode changes may hot-switch because they cannot mutate authoritative state.

facts: Current #201 branch admits reference/cached/cached_dormant with the same pressure law and unchanged defaults; source-matched runtime and final ready-PR acceptance remain separate pending gates.

Complete vertical/row head closure and global resident gas identity/order include paused contributors. Component BFS reuse preserves global census/reducer/history/relabel; incomplete proofs fall back completely, and remote gas resolution revokes motion certificates.

Certificates prove a bounded motion no-op and preserve stationary failed-motion contacts, mandatory material/lifecycle/other-liquid work, cadence and pending obligations. Same-job touched stencils select ordinary motion; execution3 uses one ordinary warmup visit and eight eligible failed-proof deferrals, and restore is cold. Execution3 additionally gates the whole certificate layer on usable heads and prior Water work, charges fixed8-tick work-credit trials and suspends32 eligible-head ticks after deficit/uncertainty; off/cold invalidation is constant work and reactivation clears stale tags before use.

Execution identity encoding1 binds execution3, variant and four requested budgets separately from physical authority. Godot copied unsigned counters/budgets use decimal strings; prepared heads may be stale after transport/edits and never authorize skipping. A no-partial-write copied chunk roster permits complete actual resident head sampling, including gas-discovery allocations; fixed coordinate envelopes do not establish complete coverage.

Complete-tick and edit costs, initialization, repair/validation, fallback, declared storage and whole-process RSS must retain sleeping/churn negatives. Old execution1 local timings do not prove execution3 or global/platform speedup. Numerical prepared-head discrepancies and net ROI Water balance are distinct from projection parity, gross face flux and actual Rapier displacement.

Section: Bounded pressure cache and Water motion certificates > Motion certificates preserve ordinary obligations
`cached_dormant` can skip only the pressure motion stage of a Water update. Chemistry, material lifecycle, WaterUpdate events, other liquids and ordinary scheduler ownership continue. This confers no generic region/chunk skip authority. A fresh proof requires full Water, zero cohesion, zero flow and zero overfill; the relevant prepared head; closed down/diagonal/lateral destinations; and a gradient inside the reference start dead band. Any body mask within the 5×5 stencil declines the certificate. Failed gravity and diagonal probes can report stationary body contacts and signed impulses even when the Water pixels do not move. Pixel stability or zero rounded transport is therefore insufficient. Pending explosion obligations and non-unit Water cadence decline the shortcut. An actual same-job mutation touching the stencil immediately takes ordinary motion, rather than proving against a pre-tick head after local writes. Owner barriers revoke neighbouring certificates for producer edits and head changes. Reconstruction never restores cached certificates as authority. **Execution version 3** retains the earlier bounded proof retry law. A cold or invalidated stencil first takes one eligible ordinary visit. A failed complete proof defers eight further eligible visits before retrying. Only the exact valid tag can skip motion; countdown bytes transition directly to cold, never to valid. Changed inputs restart warmup. These constants control derived work, not physics, rest tolerance or simulation cadence. Execution3 also admits the whole certificate layer. Unusable heads/index disable it without stamping certificate arrays. Cached1 allocates no unused certificate buffer. While disabled/cold, producer or gas invalidation marks contents cold in constant time; reactivation performs one bounded, charged cold reset before any certificate read. Actual Water material calls in a preceding tick are required before cold activation, so an already sleeping zero-visit World does not pay periodic full-resident resets. Each eight-eligible-tick trial charges one work credit per invalidated certificate cell (including cold reset),40 per complete proof attempt and one per valid reuse; each actually saved motion call supplies eight credits. A positive-cost zero-saving or credit-deficit window suspends the layer for32 eligible head ticks. All ordinary motion, body probes, material/cadence work continues while suspended. Uncertain arithmetic conservatively declines admission. These are fixed deterministic **work-budget weights**, not measured nanoseconds or a proof of wall-clock break-even on every machine. Final total-cost measurements remain required; slower outcomes stay visible.

Numeric Water mass units are meaningful only for `Prepared`; unresolved interpolation sentinels retain their explicit status. The value is from the last pre-kernel preparation and can be stale after transport or host writes, or unprepared after restore. The getter allocates and prepares nothing and grants no freshness or skip authority. Counter differences describe a measured interval; attempts count complete local proofs, while declines also include warmup/backoff and mandatory-obligation deferrals. `get_liquid_comparison_hash(1 or 2)` returns a 16-digit hexadecimal projection. Unknown IDs or an unavailable World return an empty string. Readback exposes neither mutable World storage nor certificate authority. Constructor/setup, host edits and verification are separate intervals. Section: Inertial cellular reference > Which fields, parameters and law are authoritative?
The optional slot has signed16 `vx/vy` and signed8 `ax/ay`. Velocity/accumulators use16 quanta per cell. Admitted ranges are vx −32…32, vy0…32 and each accumulator −15…15. New products, paint and reconstruction default to zero. The actual stored slot is six bytes/alignment2 on the measured Windows LLVM ABI; this is not a production Cell ABI change or a portable raw-struct save format. The reference law retains q16, gravity4, vmax32, turn1/8, deflect3/4, density-swap drag1/4 and rest threshold1. Damping defaults to1/16; the optional native family block(owner4, version2) contains exactly one signed int32 `damping_numerator` in0..16, over the fixed denominator16. Omission applies1; all seventeen values execute in the same Brine/reference law. This is not the historical illustrative IN blockv1(`damping_q16`, `speed_cap_q8`), which remains refused by the running native schema. Unsupported versions, lengths, ranges or blocks on an unused family refuse before candidate installation. The existing `inertial-update-v1` order is U1 support; U2 one gravity application; U3 diagonal re-aim or support cancellation and carried-velocity deflection; U4 saturation; U5 signed truncating damping; U6 accumulator travel with every target rechecked; U7 rest/sleep eligibility. First contact ends travel. Wall, body mask and same-material contact are inelastic; only Empty is horizontally enterable. A lighter foreign material is exchangeable only downward under the existing density/exchange gate. The immutable `physics_diagnostics.disable_powder_exchange_targets` causal control denies every Powder target before U1 support, U3 diagonal re-aim and every U6 travel recheck, including when telemetry is disabled; it does not change default eligibility. See the existing [diagnostic-control contract](../operations/physics-characterisation.md#which-variants-are-isolated-from-production-defaults). `World::inertial_parameters()` returns the actual immutable applied damping numerator. The complete parameter/state/update identity is canonical little-endian data hashed by `inertial_extension_identity(actual)`. Default1 retains the earlier identity bytes exactly. An explicit1 block has the same effective-law identity as omission but a distinct policy hash because the requested/applied block is retained. Other numerators change both effective identity and policy hash; native capture never substitutes a host-supplied parameter claim. The [native parameter vectors](../reference/inertial-parameter-vectors.json) independently bind accepted/refused policy envelopes, policy hashes and actual identity digests through `tools/lcb/inertial_parameter_contract.py`; historical illustrative vectors remain unchanged. Damping removes `trunc(v*n/16)` independently per signed component. Numerator16 removes all velocity before travel; zero removes none. Remainders are diagnostics and are not accumulated as hidden damping. Consequently a default1/16 lateral speed below16 can persist above the rest threshold, and zero damping can retain a tail indefinitely. The matched native30-tick control records actual outcomes rather than asserting every damping arm settles. Gravity, support/contact impulses and per-component/L1 ledgers remain separately exact.

Section: pressure_flow_v1 reference — corrected Water pressure family > Gas compartments
**Topology.** Every Empty region reachable from an unmasked Water cell's 4-neighbourhood, or carrying a live compartment label, is labelled with a 4-connected breadth-first fill. Body-masked cells and every non-Empty material (walls, solids, foreign liquids) are impermeable; volume counts only Empty cells. Before the fill, serial preparation materializes any unallocated chunks that contain transient body-mask cells, using the ordinary bounded chunk-capacity and failed-tick quarantine path. Only a mask-free **unallocated chunk is one uniformly Empty node** of `chunk_size²` cells, so topology never depends on allocation; a sealed region that includes one makes it resident so every cell can carry its label. A region larger than `kCompartmentVolumeLimit` (16 384 cells), or connected to a region that was, is the vented atmosphere. **Identity by label overlap, never by amount.** Old compartments are unioned with the new regions their labelled cells fall in; each connected component then resolves deterministically (components by smallest root, regions by lowest `(y, x)` anchor): | Component | Result | |---|---| | no old compartment, region holds unresolved/atmosphere cells | **create**: new id, generation 0, amount = unresolved + atmosphere cells (atmospheric for its free volume) | | no old compartment, vacuum cells only | stays `kVacuumLabel`; no compartment | | one old → one region | **continue**: same id/generation; volume recomputed; amount += atmosphere cells absorbed | | many old → one region | **merge once**: survivor = lowest id; amount = sum; generation = max+1; ancestry = all parents; others retired `merged` | | old → several regions | **split**: parents retired; new ids in anchor order; generation = max+1; volume-proportional floor shares, the integer remainder to the region holding the lowest `(y, x)` cell | | any region is atmosphere | **vent**: every old compartment retired `vented`, its amount booked to `GasLedger.vented`; atmosphere cells relabelled `kAtmosphereLabel`; a later seal creates a **new** id | | old compartment, no region | **collapse**: amount booked to `GasLedger.collapsed` | Ids are monotonic and never reused. `GasLedger` closes exactly: `amount_live + vented + collapsed == created + absorbed` (inspection reports `closes`). Pressure is isothermal: gauge (mass units) = `atmospheric_head_rows × maximum() × (amount − volume) / volume`, saturating at ±2³⁰. Suction (negative gauge) is allowed. **Labels move with the gas.** `move_cell` swaps sidecars, so a vacated cell inherits the displaced cell's label (a rising bubble keeps its identity). A kernel-vacated cell (Water drained by a transfer, a kernel conversion to Empty) is `kVacuumLabel`: it adds volume, never amount. A host paint/erase leaves `0` (unresolved). This distinction prevents water-born voids from being created

Section: Level saves and exact replay > What does import validate, and what stays intact on failure?
The codec checks lengths, header/version fields, checksum, decompression and bounded metadata types/ranges. Native validation checks exact payload length and legal material IDs (`0…131` except reserved `10`). Selected-material metadata accepts paintable IDs through `CyberCellWorld.LAST_MATERIAL`; Empty remains an invalid selection. Section: Inertial cellular reference > Why does IN require radius three?
Travel writes reach at most two cells per axis: after saturation and nonnegative damping |v|≤32 and |accumulator|≤15, so division by16 produces at most two unit moves. Eligibility is rechecked before each actual step. At most one extra neighborhood probe occurs after or alongside a final travel position. Starting vy32/ay15 reaches y+2 and U7 reads y+3; a contact-side query can similarly reach x±3. Shared powder-exchange Stone bracing inspects one further neighbor of a target within the same radius-three envelope. Brine does not execute the Water carrying stencil. Absent storage reads as Empty on the exclusive serial owner path, as in Current cellular motion. Eligibility queries allocate nothing; an actual serial move uses the shared destination allocator and its explicit capacity/failure contract. Phased jobs retain the prepared-domain guard and never allocate missing storage themselves. Reserving Empty chunks must not change the IN motion tuple at positive or negative chunk seams. An IN World therefore explicitly requires `maximum_rule_radius>=3`. The existing scheduler validates radius≤half an even core, prepares neighbor chunks, and separates same-phase expanded domains. Candidate/control comparisons must use identical admitted execution geometry; the protected exact Current preset retains radius2. Native boundary tests exercise signed coordinates, core8/core64, chunk seams, observed read3/write2 reach, no prepared tick allocation and actual four-worker execution. Configured workers and observed task participants are separate `TickStats` values. The Water successor above adds its own complete carrying/packing proof, actual `maximum()` quantity, coherence, direct-ingress refusal and existing normalization preparation. The historical radius3 Brine proof alone never qualified that mapping.

The [desktop build guide](local-build-and-validation.md#shared-play-session-and-owner-qualification) owns acquisition and import; this packet does not rebuild or replace runtimes. On Windows PowerShell, replace the source and local paths: ```powershell $Expected = 'FULL_40_CHARACTER_REVIEWED_COMMIT_SHA' python tools/play/create_manual_packet.py --expected-sha $Expected ` --godot 'C:\Godot47\Godot_v4.7-stable_win64.exe' ` --godot-archive 'C:\Downloads\Godot_v4.7-stable_win64.exe.zip' ` --output 'C:\CyberSand-evidence\play-manual-first' ``` On Linux: ```bash python3 tools/play/create_manual_packet.py \ --expected-sha FULL_40_CHARACTER_REVIEWED_COMMIT_SHA \ --godot /opt/godot/Godot_v4.7-stable_linux.x86_64 \ --godot-archive /tmp/Godot_v4.7-stable_linux.x86_64.zip \ --output /tmp/cybersand-play-manual-first ``` The generator refuses the wrong or dirty source, untracked files, an existing output directory, incomplete native source inventory, stale/unmaterialized runtime bytes, or an unpinned/mismatched engine. It runs the existing full `check_repository.py --require-materialized` logic unchanged. Official archive hashes authenticate the executable bytes; Windows also checks the console companion used by the existing launcher. No weaker provenance mode is provided. Output belongs outside the checkout and contains local paths/host information. `IDENTITY.json` pins commit/tree, engine and selected native/Rapier identities; `PRECHECK.json` retains the repository gate; `CHECKLIST.md` explains the route; `RESULTS.csv` starts with **51 untested cases**. The immutable-file manifest protects the checklist and launch instructions while permitting human edits to the result sheet. Preserve each attempt separately. Complete feasible rig checks within the same engine process. A later preflight deliberately refuses newly generated untracked metadata, including `.gd.uid` files. Retain the first launch/import log and `git status` output; preserve that checkout as evidence and prepare a fresh dedicated checkout and packet at the same reviewed SHA. If an editor import is required, record it separately under the [source execution policy](ci-execution-and-performance.md) import watchdog (1,200 seconds at the default scale) and reconcile its generated files before claiming a clean source. This packet does not delete metadata, ignore changes or promise an automatic relaunch after import.

Section: CI execution watchdogs and advisory performance > Shared capacity and concurrency
The GDExtension matrices each use `max-parallel: 8`. Together with Native's six families, the routine regression phase can use 22 slots before small auxiliary jobs. This leaves capacity within the owner's stated 40 standard hosted slots, but is not an account-wide cap: multiple PRs and other repositories add demand. Physical stress has its own smaller matrix budgets. Launch exceptional campaigns deliberately and use the [workflow audit](../audits/2026-11-01-ci-workflow-audit.md) and machine inventory when changing independent fan-out. Automatic GDExtension, Native and Documentation PR runs group by PR identity and cancel superseded checks. Main pushes and manual qualification use run identity, so a same-ref experiment cannot block or cancel a newer explicit qualification. No broad repository lock is introduced. Cancelled checks are not successful qualification, and original completed or failed artifacts retain their status. GitHub's default concurrency queue replaces an older pending member even when `cancel-in-progress` is false; run-unique manual groups avoid that hidden loss. See [GitHub concurrency semantics](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency).

Section: CI execution watchdogs and advisory performance > Scheduling estimates and hosted safety boundaries
[The Godot planner](../../tools/ci/godot_job_plan.py) discovers every current fixture and derives a deterministic complete matrix from expected execution cost. The 2026-11-01 scheduling change separates that estimate from each case's unchanged generous watchdog and from the six-hour hosted-job safety boundary. The previous sum-of-watchdogs partition multiplied short hosted jobs; its historical arithmetic remains in the 2026-10-31 audit. **Current:** every admitted case retains its full process allowance, 300 seconds for independent readback and 240 seconds for sequential diagnostics/cleanup. The shared `godot_process_cleanup_seconds()` includes up to three legacy snapshots, capture-owner retirement and engine-tree retirement. Import retains its own full allowance. Three metadata operations, 70 minutes for setup/artifact steps and 10 minutes of headroom remain reserved. A shard admits its next case only when that case's full allowance fits the remaining execution boundary. Unstarted cases are explicitly incomplete and fail coverage; an underestimate never shortens a running case's watchdog or silently counts missing work. The source inventory at intake is 246 Linux cases, including 13 rendered cases, and 233 applicable Windows cases. Machine discovery remains authoritative as the game expands. The dated [scheduling qualification](../audits/2026-11-01-ci-scheduling-qualification.md) records estimator inputs, selected counts, original results and limitations. The [hosted job limit](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits) remains six hours; an individual case that cannot fit or an oversized matrix is rejected. The six Native families retain the exact original 20 commands and scientific inputs. [Their planner](../../tools/ci/native_execution_policy.py) derives 180/350/180/333/284/223-minute parents for TSan, normal, ASan, worldgen, soliding-normal and soliding-ASan respectively. The physics CLI inventory still contains all 154 original invocations, each with a 300-second operation budget; a bounded eight-process dispatch preserves arguments and output identity while all assertions run in their original order on the main test thread. The source inventory and family receipts remain required by the stable `native` gate. All independent matrices use `fail-fast: false`. New PR commits cancel superseded automatic checks for that PR; manual qualification and main push runs have unique run groups and retain their original attempts. Required aggregate jobs run after an admitted matrix or scope classifier failure. A skipped job is not accepted as a successful behavioral gate. The retired optional four-shard serial-migration job is replaced by mandatory [Linux coverage verification](../../tools/ci/verify_linux_godot_shards.py) on every admitted run. It checks the complete original inventory, source/tree, runtime, policy, run/attempt, real rendered commands, natural completion, unchanged raw logs and required independent PLAY readbacks. The existing Windows coverage reader derives its complete plan from the same source.

Section: CI execution watchdogs and advisory performance > Original failures and process ownership
[The native command owner](../../tools/ci/run_timed_command.py) writes an initial incomplete receipt before launch, retains file-backed output and records the original final exit. Linux child-subreaper ownership and process creation identities include rapidly detached descendants. A zero root exit with a live child is a teardown failure. Forced cleanup is scoped to owned identities; namespace mismatch fails closed instead of treating unrelated host PIDs as ours. Windows diagnostic fixtures use their separate strict Job owner. Godot process diagnostics retain partial logs, actual exit codes, the last real application/worker/physics marker, process/thread activity and available stack or dump evidence. Early capture after prolonged inactivity is diagnostic; the complex fixture's generous failure clock is independent. Diagnostic failure or a process exiting during capture cannot convert an expired case into a pass. Original failed artifacts remain unchanged when a later corrected source runs. The adverse controls include correct fast execution, actual 16-second success beyond the former operation limit, an actual assertion after 16 seconds, nonzero subprocess exits, no-progress hangs, successful parent exit with surviving children, rapid detached children and preservation of the first attempt. Dedicated Windows controls separately exercise actual 20-second success and a 20-second delayed exit 19. These are harness controls, not game qualification.

Section: CI execution watchdogs and advisory performance > Owner policy and acceptance boundary
The 2026-10-31 owner decision replaces historical short execution deadlines with generous watchdogs. A slowdown is an observation to investigate. Assertions, crashes, invalid simulation, incorrect rendering, unjoined processes and missing source-bound evidence remain failures. Cold startup time, warmed gameplay latency, simulation throughput, render submission and physical display cadence are separate measurements. Larger watchdogs do not qualify poor gameplay feel. The committed [policy JSON](../../godot/tests/support/ci_execution_policy.json) is consumed by [GDScript](../../godot/tests/support/ci_execution_policy.gd), [Python](../../tools/ci/execution_policy.py), native shell wrappers and PLAY readers. The policy identity records its bytes, schema and effective scale. `CYBERSAND_CI_WATCHDOG_SCALE` may enlarge local allowances; invalid, nonfinite, boolean or shrinking values fail. Hosted workflows explicitly select scale 1, and planners reject configurations above the supported hosted job limit. | Workload | Initial hard watchdog | Interpretation | |---|---:|---| | Cold Main acknowledgement | 600 seconds | Maximum setup allowance, not a target | | Ordinary or rendered case | 1,200 seconds | Complex fixtures receive the larger allowance below | | Godot import | 1,200 seconds | Separate preflight on each isolated shard | | Operation, independent readback, graceful teardown | 300 seconds | Shared operation clock includes dependent provenance reads | | Complex fixture | 3,600 seconds | Inner fixture can report its own failure before its parent expires | | Complex fixture process | 3,940 seconds | Fixture plus 300-second unwind, 30-second capture and 10-second forced cleanup | | Native compile or substantial native command | 3,600 seconds | Command-specific aggregate arithmetic may extend this | | Dependency preparation | 1,200 seconds | Separate from scientific sampling windows | | Expensive hosted job starting point | 180 minutes | Derived parents extend when the complete child inventory requires it | Fixed tick counts, sample windows, input pulses, sanitizer environments, solver parameters, fixture geometry and adverse-control delays are scientific or protocol inputs. They do not become watchdogs merely because they contain a number. In particular, BUSY001's held native phase controls retain their original protocol bounds and the scene smoke check retains its 180-frame count.

Section: IN-TOOLS #361-A — opt-in metered physical Liquid Drain > Selecting and operating the profile
Use an existing supported physical actor with held equipment. Open **F5**, choose **Liquid Drain**, then explicitly choose **Metered Water v1 — experimental** or **Metered Brine v1 — experimental** and **Equip only**. The profile selector is available only for physical U10. **Ordinary U10** selects the retained behavior. Changing equipment requires the existing chassis to be held and the previous pending use to be retired. Aim with the pointer independently of movement. Hold left mouse or **M** to request repeated pulses; release stops future uncommitted pulses. Right mouse requests one precision pulse at 35% of selected equipment power. Opening a blocking panel, losing focus, pausing or retiring control cancels the pending intake. Release the buttons before rearming after cancellation or a new owner. Stopping the worker retires pending equipment and its retained control generation. A direct stop/start cannot revive that lease; a normal fresh control boundary or reconstruction must precede another activation. Main ordinarily stops the worker on scene exit; qualification joins for read-only census and then explicitly establishes fresh control before resuming. Healthy restart preserves the selected physical-owner mode. It does not enable the sampled character or run sampled spawn recovery inside that physical World. The actor status shows the cumulative registered sink and remaining allowance in **Water units** or **Brine cells**. Its tooltip identifies the last applied, refused or fault outcome, selected material, native generation and policy. A refusal produces no accepted drain effect or recoil. The displayed allowance is a finite permission to remove material, not an inventory of recovered liquid. Current FreeMass Water and CY Brine work in ordinary native physical gameplay. For IN, use the existing **PLAY** session panel: choose a physical rig, select **Water: inertial**, set radius **3**, **Build selected session**, then play/resume and equip metered U10 through F5. The existing **Mixed Current Water + inertial Brine** preset similarly supplies a supported no-PF Brine owner. Authored exploratory maps also support prepared physical actors. The native-default-demo Liquids route excludes articulated equipment owners and is not this route. A legacy/imported IN World without its initial native construction receipt refuses this profile. The metered selector does not itself change solver policy or normalize liquid.
